title: Total Endovascular Aortic Arch Repair: A Review of Current Technologies and Clinical Decision Frameworks.
abstract: Endovascular technologies offer less invasive alternatives to open aortic arch repair in high-risk patients. This review evaluates contemporary total arch reconstruction platforms. PubMed literature through February 2026, manufacturer documentation, and ClinicalTrials.gov were reviewed. Branched, fenestrated, and alternative devices were assessed regarding anatomy, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes. No formal systematic review or meta-analysis was performed. Technical success rates reached 90-100%. Branched devices enable three-vessel revascularization, while fenestrated systems accommodate complex anatomy. Stroke rates ranged from 3.7% to 11%; endoleaks and reinterventions remained concerns. To date, anyway, device selection, anatomical suitability, planning, and institutional expertise are essential for optimal outcomes.

title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.

METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.

RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).

CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Epidemiology of 376,383 arteriovenous fistula creations for hemodialysis over 9 years within the Brazilian Unified Public Health System and the Private Healthcare Sector.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine trends in AVF creation for hemodialysis across Brazil from 2015 to 2023, assessing differences in frequency, geographic distribution, and sectoral disparities between the public and private healthcare sectors.

METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using anonymized data from national administrative databases: DATASUS (public sector) and D-TISS (private sector). The majority of AVF creation procedures were included. Statistical analyses considered regional adjustments and were performed using SPSS v.20, with significance set at p < 0.001.

RESULTS: Over the nine- year period, 376,383 AVF procedures were recorded, with 90.57% occurring in the public sector. While the absolute number of AVF creations increased, the ratio of AVFs per 1,000 dialysis patients showed a declining trend. Regional disparities were evident, with the Southeast and South regions presenting higher procedure rates compared to other areas. The private sector consistently reported lower creation rates.

CONCLUSION: Although, separately, dialysis and AVF rates have risen steadily in Brazil, the relative rate between them has shown a decreasing trend over the years. The predominance of AVF procedures in the public system is more pronounced.

In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited.

title: Nursing Ultrasound Monitoring of Arteriovenous Fistulas in Haemodialysis: The ECHO-NURSE Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease affects up to 16% of adults worldwide, and patients with kidney failure treated with haemodialysis require reliable vascular access. Autologous arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred access, yet their function may deteriorate due to stenosis or thrombosis. Doppler ultrasound is a key non‑invasive tool for assessing autologous arteriovenous fistula haemodynamics, but evidence on nurse‑performed serial Doppler monitoring remains limited, particularly in Italy.

OBJECTIVES: To describe temporal trends in Doppler-derived haemodynamic parameters measured by nurses and compare trajectories between patients with and without autologous arteriovenous fistula complications.

DESIGN: Longitudinal observational study conducted over 4 months with monthly ultrasound assessments.

PARTICIPANTS: Forty‑two adults with a stable autologous arteriovenous fistula undergoing maintenance haemodialysis were enrolled; three presented with baseline stenosis.

MEASUREMENTS: Nurses recorded brachial artery diameter, mean velocity, volumetric flow, end‑diastolic velocity, pulsatility index, and resistance index using standardised Doppler protocols. Linear mixed‑effects models evaluated level and trend differences between groups.

RESULTS: Patients with stenosis showed consistently lower flow‑related parameters and higher Doppler indices. Vessel diameter and volumetric flow exhibited significantly attenuated temporal increases in the stenosis group (p < 0.001 for trend differences). Velocity parameters and Doppler indices displayed parallel trends but differed in mean levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Nurse‑performed serial Doppler monitoring characterised autologous arteriovenous fistula haemodynamics and distinguished profiles associated with stenosis. Findings support integrating structured ultrasound assessment into nursing‑led vascular access pathways.

Autologous arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred access, yet their function may deteriorate due to stenosis or thrombosis. Doppler ultrasound is a key non‑invasive tool for assessing autologous arteriovenous fistula haemodynamics, but evidence on nurse‑performed serial Doppler monitoring remains limited, particularly in Italy.

title: Emergency department management of pediatric traumatic arrest.
abstract: More than 20% of pediatric out-of-hospital arrests are secondary to trauma. It is uncommon for children with traumatic arrest to regain spontaneous circulation, with reported mortality rates typically >90%. Hemorrhage control, early blood administration, and evaluation for reversible causes of arrest should be prioritized. Clinicians should avoid prolongation of resuscitation when efforts are unlikely to be successful, such as when patients have unwitnessed arrest or no signs of life on initial evaluation. This review discusses the most common reversible causes of traumatic arrest as well as important and controversial aspects of treatment, including resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta and emergency department resuscitative thoracotomy. It also addresses which patients are most likely to benefit from resuscitation, how to decide when to terminate resuscitation, and how to debrief after resuscitation.

title: Haemostasis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
abstract: MASLD is the most prevalent chronic liver disease and a significant cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality. Portal hypertension may develop before advanced fibrosis, driven by vascular and metabolic alterations that concurrently affect systemic haemostasis and promote intrahepatic interactions between endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and haemostatic pathways. Once cirrhosis is established, the rebalanced haemostatic state is largely independent of aetiology, with impaired fibrinolysis representing the principal MASLD-associated difference. In non-cirrhotic MASLD, increasing in vivo platelet activation, a progressive procoagulant imbalance between factor VIII and protein C, and reduced fibrinolysis, including increased plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and prolonged clot lysis, have been described, although their attribution to MASLD is complicated by the concomitant metabolic factors. Clinically, MASLD is associated with increased risks of venous thromboembolism, portal vein thrombosis, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, increasing with disease severity; however, prospective data linking specific haemostatic alterations to incident thrombosis remain lacking. Within the liver, platelets act as central hubs interacting with dysfunctional liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatic stellate cells, Kupffer cells, and hepatocytes, orchestrating platelet-neutrophil crosstalk, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and coagulation activation, thereby promoting immunothrombosis, hepatic stellate cell activation, microvascular remodelling, and fibrogenesis. Coagulation proteases may additionally contribute to MASLD progression through protease-activated receptor signalling in hepatocytes and hepatic stellate cells. These observations raise the hypothesis that antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapies could modify MASLD progression, although evidence remains predominantly preclinical and observational. This review synthesizes haemostatic balance and thrombotic complications in MASLD, the endothelial-inflammation-haemostasis axis in MASLD progression, and emerging perspectives.

Portal hypertension may develop before advanced fibrosis, driven by vascular and metabolic alterations that concurrently affect systemic haemostasis and promote intrahepatic interactions between endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and haemostatic pathways. Once cirrhosis is established, the rebalanced haemostatic state is largely independent of aetiology, with impaired fibrinolysis representing the principal MASLD-associated difference.

title: A Novel Hybrid Gripper for Endovascular Interventions Using Collaborative Robotic Arms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current robotic systems for endovascular interventions automate intravascular navigation. However, tool preparation, assembly, and exchange are still performed manually, which limits procedural automation.

METHODS: To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid gripper that combines a rigid gripping section for manipulating proximal tool ends with a hydraulic gripping mechanism for grasping, moving, and rotating guidewires and catheters with diameters from 0.25 to 3 mm.

RESULTS: The hydraulic gripping mechanism generated friction forces comparable to or greater than manual manipulation for all tested tools. The balloon withstood at least 307 inflation-deflation cycles (approximately 1.6 times the number required for a typical intervention). A dual-arm collaborative robot successfully assembled endovascular tool configurations and navigated catheters and guidewires through multiple vascular bifurcations in a thoracic aorta simulator.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed hybrid gripper enables both robotic tool preparation and intravascular manipulation using a single end-effector, expanding the scope of robotic automation in endovascular interventions.

However, tool preparation, assembly, and exchange are still performed manually, which limits procedural automation. METHODS: To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid gripper that combines a rigid gripping section for manipulating proximal tool ends with a hydraulic gripping mechanism for grasping, moving, and rotating guidewires and catheters with diameters from 0.25 to 3 mm.

title: Individualised Versus Conventional Balloon Dilation for TIPS: Hepatic Encephalopathy in a Propensity-Matched Before-After Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a major complication of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, 717 patients with cirrhosis underwent TIPS with 8-mm covered stents between December 2015 and December 2023. Patients received conventional 8-mm full dilation (n = 408; before December 1, 2020) or individualised dilation (n = 309; from December 1, 2020 onward), with the balloon diameter (5-7 mm) chosen by an 11-factor scoring system. The primary endpoint was overt HE (West Haven grade II-IV) within 6 months. Propensity score matching, inverse probability weighting, Fine-Grey and E-value analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Six-month overt HE was lower in the individualised group (14.6%; 45 of 309) than in the conventional group (27.5%; 112 of 408), yielding an absolute risk reduction of 12.9 percentage points (number needed to treat, 8; p < 0.001). After propensity score matching on 18 covariates (259 pairs), the conditional odds ratio was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.27-0.66; p < 0.001), consistent with inverse probability weighting (odds ratio, 0.47). Six-month re-bleeding (1.5% vs. 1.3%), stent dysfunction (3.9% vs. 4.2%) and ascites improvement (61.0% vs. 62.1%) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: An individualised balloon dilation strategy incorporating an 11-factor scoring system was associated with reduced post-TIPS HE, with no clear difference in variceal re-bleeding, stent dysfunction or ascites recurrence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400087533.

Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

title: Early US Experience Using the Symani for Robotic-Assisted Microvascular Surgery.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted microsurgery provides motion scaling, tremor filtration, and enhanced visualization, offering potential advantages for complex microsurgical tasks. Following Food and Drug Administration authorization, the Symani Surgical System was introduced into clinical practice in the United States in April 2024. This study presents the first multi-institutional US experience with Symani, evaluating feasibility, reconstructive outcomes, and technical challenges during its inaugural year of use in the United States.

METHODS: All robotic-assisted procedures performed between April 2024 and April 2025 at two tertiary academic centers were retrospectively reviewed. Demographics, clinical indications, flap type, and anastomotic details were extracted. Primary outcomes were anastomotic patency and flap loss. Secondary outcomes included overall surgical complications and conversion to conventional microsurgery.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients underwent robotic-assisted microsurgical procedures. Median age was 51 [IQR 39-63] years; 55.6% were female, and 74.1% identified as White. Indications included oncologic reconstruction (48.1%), trauma (18.5%), degenerative bony disease (14.8%), infection (11.1%), peripheral vascular disease (3.7%), and morphea (3.7%). A wide variety of flaps were performed, most commonly deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) (44.4%), free vascularized fibular grafts (18.5%), and scapular flaps (14.8%). Robotic assistance was employed for 27 arterial anastomoses (84.4%), three venous anastomoses (9.4%), and two nerve coaptations (6.3%). Anastomotic configuration was predominantly end-to-end (71.9%). No flap loss occurred. One patient (3.7%) required re-exploration for pedicle kinking. Two conversions to conventional non-robotic microsurgery were required (7.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Early US multi-institutional experience demonstrates the Symani system is feasible and safe across diverse reconstructive procedures, enabling reliable microvascular anastomoses and nerve coaptations with minimal complications and no flap loss.

Following Food and Drug Administration authorization, the Symani Surgical System was introduced into clinical practice in the United States in April 2024. This study presents the first multi-institutional US experience with Symani, evaluating feasibility, reconstructive outcomes, and technical challenges during its inaugural year of use in the United States.

title: Changes in Circulating Insulin and Glucose Homeostasis After Portosystemic Shunt Creation and Obliteration: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The liver removes about half of secreted insulin on first pass. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched through September 2026 for paired glucose or insulin measurements before and after either intervention. Ratios of post-intervention to pre-intervention means were pooled by random effects with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, excluding cohorts at critical risk of bias.

RESULTS: Fifteen cohorts (17 records) were included. After shunt creation, fasting insulin rose 49% (95% confidence interval 24% to 80%; 6 cohorts) and the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance rose 55% (5% to 129%; 4 cohorts), whereas fasting glucose (2.5%; -0.3% to 5.4%; 5 cohorts), glycated haemoglobin, and fructosamine were unchanged. Glucose tolerance worsened in one of two cohorts tested (area under the curve +14%). Insulin rose more than C-peptide or proinsulin in four cohorts; clamp-measured insulin sensitivity was unchanged. After obliteration, fasting insulin fell 15% (one cohort) and insulin area under the curve 17% and 19% (two cohorts). Antihyperglycaemic requirements changed in both directions after shunt creation and fell after obliteration.

CONCLUSIONS: Shunt creation raises insulin by nearly half without changing fasting glucose or glycation markers, and obliteration reverses the pattern. Secretion markers change less than insulin, indicating altered first-pass hepatic insulin extraction rather than secretion. Insulin-based resistance indices may mislead after shunting, and the consequences of chronic shunt-induced hyperinsulinemia need prospective study.

Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.

title: The many faces of contrast-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The increased use of endovascular procedures shows an increase of neurological deficits after intravascular administration of iodine-based contrast media (ICM). Unfortunately, nonuniform terminology is confusing and may explain low awareness of this ICM-associated neurological adverse drug reaction (nADR). Consequently, we conducted this study to summarize identified risk factors, clinical presentations, radiological features, pathophysiological mechanisms, and treatment strategies of ICM-associated nADR. Additionally, we evaluated, if unifying different terminology of nADR seems to be warranted.

METHODS: A PRISMA-2020 systematic literature search was conducted. We included scientific articles on contrast-induced encephalopathy (CIE), contrast-induced neurotoxicity (CIN), and transient cortical blindness (TCB) following administration of ICM. A total of 228 records were eligible for inclusion.

RESULTS: The majority of neurological adverse reactions manifests after invasive contrast enhanced procedures and are mostly described as CIE, CIN, and TCB. Patients present with stroke mimickers and TCB. The onset of symptoms varies from shortly after the administration of ICM till up to 24 h following ICM application. In most of the patients the neurological symptoms are reversible. The available evidence suggests that there seems to be a common underlying pathophysiology, most likely due to dysfunction of the blood brain barrier. Risk factors include chronic or end stage renal disease, underlying vascular dysfunction, ICM volume, and the territory of ICM administration.

CONCLUSIONS: There is need for implementation of formal criteria and raising awareness on risk factors and therapeutic management of nADR following ICM administration. The authors suggest to summarize currently different terminology under 1 umbrella of contrast-associated encephalopathy.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: The increase of diagnostic and therapeutic endovascular procedures reveals ICM-associated neurological adverse reactions. Knowledge and awareness on neurotoxic effects after ICM application must be raised among radiologists and clinicians which may be enhanced by unifying the nomenclature.

Unfortunately, nonuniform terminology is confusing and may explain low awareness of this ICM-associated neurological adverse drug reaction (nADR). Consequently, we conducted this study to summarize identified risk factors, clinical presentations, radiological features, pathophysiological mechanisms, and treatment strategies of ICM-associated nADR.

title: SLC3A2 Silencing Alleviates Aortic Dissection via cAMP-PKA Activation and Disulfidptosis Inhibition.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Disulfidptosis, a novel disulfide stress-induced cell death, remains unexplored in AD. We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis. Bioinformatic analyses of Gene Expression Omnibus datasets combined machine learning algorithms to identify SLC3A2 as a core gene. A murine AD model was established using β-aminopropionitrile and angiotensin II, with lentiviral knockdown of SLC3A2. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells (HAVSMCs) were challenged with BAY-876 to induce disulfidptosis. Histological staining evaluated medial degeneration and elastic fiber integrity. Disulfidptosis was assessed by measuring cystine accumulation and the protein expression of filamin A (FLNA) and NCK-associated protein 1 (NCKAP1). The involvement of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)-protein kinase A (PKA) signaling was verified by genetic knockdown of its catalytic subunit (PRKACA). We observed SLC3A2 was upregulated in AD. SLC3A2 knockdown delayed lethal aortic rupture, reduced aortic medial degeneration, decreased reactive oxygen species and cystine, while restoring glutathione and free thiols. In HAVSMCs, SLC3A2 silencing preserved filamentous actin integrity, reversed the BAY-876-induced downregulation of α-smooth muscle actin and smooth muscle 22 alpha, and restored the aberrant expression of FLNA and NCKAP1. Mechanistically, SLC3A2 knockdown reactivated the cAMP-PKA signaling axis suppressed by BAY-876, and PRKACA knockdown abrogated the protective effects of SLC3A2 silencing on oxidative stress, cytoskeletal integrity, and disulfidptosis. In conclusion, SLC3A2 drives AD progression by suppressing cAMP-PKA signaling, thereby exacerbating oxidative stress and disulfidptotic cytoskeletal collapse. Targeting the SLC3A2/cAMP-PKA axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.
englishSummary: Aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Disulfidptosis, a novel disulfide stress-induced cell death, remains unexplored in AD. We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis.

title: Minimally Invasive Surgery for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy Using a Double-Row SpeedBridge Repair with Rip-Stop Augmentation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The present video article describes a minimally invasive surgery (MIS) technique utilizing a double-row rip-stop SpeedBridge (Arthrex) repair for the treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT). This procedure is utilized when nonoperative treatment has failed, with the goal of returning patients to their previous levels of activity while avoiding the complications associated with more open procedures. All products mentioned in the videos are manufactured by Arthrex.

DESCRIPTION: The surgical technique is performed with 4 small incisions-2 distal and 2 proximal. Any Haglund deformity and/or enthesophyte are resected with use of an MIS burr through the 2 distal portals. The central third of the Achilles tendon is partially detached with this resection and is repaired with use of a double-row repair. Proximal anchors are placed, and sutures are passed through the Achilles tendon. Working knotless sutures are tensioned to create a rip-stop suture. The sutures are passed and shuttled to the distal row, creating a double-row repair. The distal row is drilled and tapped. The double-row repair is completed with insertion of distal anchors under appropriate tension.

ALTERNATIVES: Nonoperative treatment is beneficial in the initial stages of the condition and is successful in 60% to 80% of patients1-3. Initial treatment strategies for IAT include RICE (rest, ice, compression, and elevation), nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and physical therapy. Eccentric exercise and extracorporeal shockwave therapy have shown promising results3. Paratendinous injections, such as with platelet-rich plasma, have shown various levels of success and need further evaluation3. When nonoperative treatment has failed, operative treatment is a viable option. The surgical approach should be chosen on a patient-specific basis, as different tendinopathy patterns and different associated osseous and soft-tissue conditions may influence preoperative planning. There are a variety of different surgical techniques that include open, endoscopic, and MIS procedures.

RATIONALE: This MIS technique utilizing a double-row SpeedBridge repair with rip-stop augmentation yields fewer wound complications, less pain, quicker initiation of rehabilitation protocols, and quicker return to sport compared with more invasive techniques. Furthermore, the addition of the rip-stop augment to the double-row SpeedBridge repair improves dynamic mechanical strength and mitigates suture tearing through the tendon4.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES: In our experience, patients who undergo this technique will be weight-bearing in a controlled-ankle-motion boot immediately postoperatively and out of the boot by 6 weeks postoperatively, with progressive return to full activities as tolerated. Our study of 61 patients undergoing the double-row SpeedBridge repair demonstrated favorable outcomes, with Foot and Ankle Disability Index scores improving from a mean of 56.3 preoperatively to 98.62 at 12 months postoperatively and visual analog scale pain scores improving from a mean of 7.25 to 0.476. There were no postoperative ruptures at a mean follow-up of 12.5 months. Eleven patients had minor complications within 3 months, including 6 who reported some central numbness over the Achilles tendon6. We expect these outcomes to improve as surgeons become more comfortable and skilled performing MIS techniques.

IMPORTANT TIPS: Proper patient selection (chronic IAT with Haglund deformity and/or an enthesophyte) will help ensure optimal outcomes.It is important to develop a subcutaneous plane for suture passage.The use of fluoroscopy or a nanoscope is helpful in ensuring that the proper bone is resected with the MIS burr.We have found that the irrigator from the MIS burr can be utilized alongside a Frazier suction tip to help remove excess bone.Suture management is important. Precisely maneuver the sutures at all times; it is very important that the sutures do not get tangled so that the procedure flows efficiently.Make sure to fully tension both sutures in order to place the ripstop.

This procedure is utilized when nonoperative treatment has failed, with the goal of returning patients to their previous levels of activity while avoiding the complications associated with more open procedures. title: Induced ubiquitination drives ER protein degradation through a VCP-dependent pathway.
abstract: Heterobifunctional proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable degradation of disease-relevant proteins but have largely been limited to cytosolic targets. Using reporter cell lines and the dTAG system to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases, we found that luminal substrates are resistant to degradation, whereas ER membrane proteins are efficiently degraded across multiple topologies. CRISPR screens confirmed dependence on cullin-RING ligases but did not identify canonical ER-associated degradation (ERAD) components, except the AAA ATPase VCP. Combined loss of DERL1/2/3 and depletion of HRD1 did not impair degradation, further supporting independence from canonical ERAD machinery. Mechanistic studies showed that ubiquitination is required for VCP binding and that removal of ubiquitin chains releases VCP, suggesting direct extraction of ubiquitinated substrates. An atorvastatin-cereblon PROTAC induced VCP-dependent degradation of HMGCR, preventing its compensatory accumulation during statin treatment. Together, these findings support a model in which ubiquitination by a cytosolic E3 ligase is sufficient to engage VCP and drive extraction, potentially bypassing canonical ERAD machinery.

title: Migration of a Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Stent Causing Incomplete Cardioplegic Arrest: Stent Gone Astray!
abstract: Right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) stenting is an established palliative option in tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) when surgical repair poses a high-risk. We report a rare, life-threatening complication in a 4-year-old child with TOF, a hypoplastic pulmonary annulus, and multiple comorbidities that precluded primary corrective surgery. RVOT stenting was therefore planned. During catheterization, the stent embolized, necessitating emergency surgical retrieval. Intraoperatively, the stent was seen lodged across the aortic valve, preventing complete leaflet coaptation, and causing the cardioplegia to leak into the left ventricle. This resulted in an incomplete cardioplegic arrest. Real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) identified the mechanism of cardioplegia failure, delineated the stent position, guided its repositioning, and facilitated successful cardioplegia delivery and definitive surgical repair. This case emphasizes meticulous anatomical evaluation and highlights the indispensable role of intraoperative TEE in high-risk RVOT stenting.

We report a rare, life-threatening complication in a 4-year-old child with TOF, a hypoplastic pulmonary annulus, and multiple comorbidities that precluded primary corrective surgery. RVOT stenting was therefore planned.

title: Iatrogenic pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm following chest tube insertion.
abstract: We report a rare case of pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm developing immediately after tube thoracostomy in a 62-year-old man with tuberculous pleural effusion. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a pseudoaneurysm arising from a subsegmental pulmonary artery branch associated with lung laceration. The lesion was successfully treated by endovascular coil embolization, with complete clinical and radiological resolution at follow-up.

title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm in patients with malignancy: a population-based claims study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The co-occurrence of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and malignancy is increasingly relevant in an aging population. However, the population-based co-prevalence, temporal relationship, and potential impact of concomitant cancer on AAA management remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: This retrospective population-based cohort study analyzed claims data from 3,088,992 individuals insured by a large German statutory health insurance provider (AOK PLUS) between 2010 and 2023. AAA and cancer cases were identified using standardized ICD-10-GM and OPS codes.

RESULTS: AAA was recorded in 13,494 individuals (period prevalence: 4,368/1,000,000) and cancer in 316,603 (10,249/100,000). A recorded diagnosis of both conditions during the observation period was identified in 4,745 patients (35.2% of patients with AAA), predominantly men (5:1). Among patients with incident diagnoses of both diseases (n = 531), AAA was recorded before cancer in 51.6%, cancer before AAA in 41.2%, and both simultaneously in 7.2%. At the first recorded AAA diagnosis, rupture was less frequently documented in patients with recorded cancer than in those without (2.9% vs. 5.9%; p < 0.001). Among patients with AAA, the proportion undergoing aneurysm repair was comparable between patients with and without recorded cancer (25.5% vs. 26.2%). Exploratory Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested a longer interval from first recorded AAA diagnosis to treatment in patients with recorded cancer (p = 0.041), while competing-risk analysis showed a slightly lower cumulative incidence of repair (p = 0.02) and more frequent death before repair (p < 0.01). Systemic cancer therapies were administered with similar frequency in AAA patients with cancer and the overall cancer cohort (26.5% vs. 28.1%).

CONCLUSION: The co-prevalence of AAA and malignancy is substantial. In patients with a recorded cancer diagnosis, exploratory analysis suggested a longer observed interval from the first recorded AAA diagnosis to aneurysm treatment, while competing-risk analysis showed a slightly lower cumulative incidence of repair and more deaths before repair. Cancer-related imaging may influence AAA detection, but disease onset and progression could not be assessed. These findings support coordinated vascular-oncology care and warrant further studies integrating detailed clinical and imaging data.

However, the population-based co-prevalence, temporal relationship, and potential impact of concomitant cancer on AAA management remain incompletely understood. METHODS: This retrospective population-based cohort study analyzed claims data from 3,088,992 individuals insured by a large German statutory health insurance provider (AOK PLUS) between 2010 and 2023.

title: Left vertebral artery dissecting aneurysm compressing the cervical nerve roots and mimicking cervical radiculopathy: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vertebral artery dissection usually presents with head and neck pain or posterior circulation ischemia. In rare cases, a dissecting aneurysm or focal arterial dilatation may compress adjacent cervical nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus, thereby mimicking cervical radiculopathy.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old woman presented with an 8-day history of head and neck pain and a 4-day history of progressive weakness of the left upper limb. Neurological examination suggested involvement of the left C5-C6 nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus. Conventional imaging of the cervical spine and shoulder identified degenerative and musculoskeletal abnormalities; however, these findings did not adequately explain the rapidly progressive proximal weakness. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brachial plexus demonstrated relative enlargement and increased signal intensity of the left C5 nerve root compared with the contralateral side. Targeted color Doppler ultrasonography revealed focal dilatation of the left vertebral artery with suspected dissection-related changes and compression of adjacent neural structures. Electrodiagnostic testing supported involvement of the left C5-C6 nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus, and digital subtraction angiography confirmed a left vertebral artery dissecting aneurysm. The patient subsequently underwent reconstructive endovascular stent treatment. Her neck and shoulder pain improved markedly after treatment, and the strength of the left upper limb gradually recovered.

CONCLUSION: Vertebral artery dissection associated with a dissecting aneurysm and neural compression should be considered in patients presenting with acute or subacute neck and shoulder pain accompanied by progressive proximal upper-limb weakness, particularly when common cervical spine, shoulder, or peripheral nerve disorders do not adequately explain the neurological localization or clinical course.

In rare cases, a dissecting aneurysm or focal arterial dilatation may compress adjacent cervical nerve roots or the upper trunk of the brachial plexus, thereby mimicking cervical radiculopathy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old woman presented with an 8-day history of head and neck pain and a 4-day history of progressive weakness of the left upper limb.

title: Sleep, stasis, and thromboprotection: what hibernating mammals can teach us about cardiovascular risk.
abstract: Prolonged immobility is one of the best-known triggers for venous blood clots, yet hibernating brown bears spend months lying still without ever developing them - and something similar seems to hold for many people with chronic paralysis. Thienel and colleagues recently offered a compelling explanation: platelets in hibernating bears sharply downregulate a protein called HSP47, dropping to roughly 55-fold below normal levels. HSP47 turns out to drive clot formation on two fronts at once, by boosting platelet activation and by prompting neutrophils to release the web-like structures that help clots take hold. Suppress it, and both arms of the process weaken together. That this pattern shows up across bears, immobilized patients, bed-rest volunteers, and other animal models suggests it isn't a quirk of bear physiology but something closer to an ancient survival mechanism. Here we consider why immobility's clotting risk seems to shift over time, look at an HSP47-blocking compound called Col003 that is already showing promise, and ask whether HSP47 might eventually double as a marker of clotting and inflammatory risk more broadly.

title: "I just assumed that you just were born with small veins and that's that…": A Qualitative Study of the Experiences of Black and Hispanic Americans Living with Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical outcomes of adults living with peripheral artery disease (PAD) have been reported. However, the experience of Black and Hispanic American adults living with PAD, remains understudied. Guided by a multilevel health disparities framework, the aim of this qualitative study was to explore patient factors that may contribute to disparities in disease outcomes.

METHODS: Thirty Black and Hispanic American adults with confirmed diagnosis of PAD participated in semi-structured interviews between July 2022 and January 2023. Participants were recruited from an academic medical center and a network of federally qualified health centers affiliated with a safety-net hospital in Denver, Colorado. All interviews were audio-recorded, professionally transcribed and analyzed using Kilbourne et al.'s multilevel framework, which examines the origins of health and healthcare disparities through a health services research lens. The analysis explored patient-level determinants of disparities within the healthcare system.

RESULTS: Overarching themes included: 1) persistent confusion and misunderstanding about PAD, 2) debilitating pain and the loss of physical freedom from PAD, 3) when PAD forces people out of work, 4) PAD and the loss of social connection and 5) emotional unraveling, fear, and psychological distress from PAD.

CONCLUSIONS: Through seeking to understand the experience of Black and Hispanic American individuals living with PAD, this study suggests PAD may often be unmanaged, exacerbating and complicating the physical, mental, and emotional symptoms associated with this disease.

However, the experience of Black and Hispanic American adults living with PAD, remains understudied. Guided by a multilevel health disparities framework, the aim of this qualitative study was to explore patient factors that may contribute to disparities in disease outcomes.

title: Bleeding risk in patients with venous thromboembolism receiving concomitant direct oral anticoagulants and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients initiating direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) often use concomitant medications that may increase bleeding risk, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs); however, data on DOACs combined with SSRIs are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the risk of major bleeding in venous thromboembolism (VTE) patients receiving DOACs with or without concomitant SSRI treatment. Secondary aims included major bleeding stratified by sex, age, type of DOAC, type of SSRI, and coexisting cancer as well as fatal bleeding and all-cause mortality.

METHODS: Nationwide Swedish register-based study of patients ≥18 years with first-time VTE initiating DOAC (apixaban or rivaroxaban), between 2014 and 2023. In a 1:2 propensity-score-matched cohort, Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for major bleeding, fatal bleeding, and all-cause mortality during 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: Of 46,479 eligible patients, 4574 receiving DOAC + SSRI were matched to 9148 on DOAC-alone. Median age was 73 years, 65% were women. Major bleeding rate was 5.2 (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.4-6.1) per 100 patient-years on DOAC + SSRI and 4.4 (95% CI, 3.8-4.9) on DOAC-alone; HR 1.13 (95% CI, 0.92-1.39), with no significant difference between the groups. No difference was observed for fatal bleeding; HR 1.31 (95% CI, 0.86-2.02), whereas mortality rate was higher on DOAC + SSRI than on DOAC-alone; HR 1.28 (95% CI, 1.14-1.44).

CONCLUSION: The absence of differences in major bleeding is reassuring given the common use of concomitant treatment. Higher mortality on DOAC + SSRI, despite no difference in fatal bleeding, may reflect residual confounding but warrants further investigation.

Secondary aims included major bleeding stratified by sex, age, type of DOAC, type of SSRI, and coexisting cancer as well as fatal bleeding and all-cause mortality.

title: [Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia: Endovascular and Surgical Management].
abstract:
AIM: Acute mesenteric ischaemia is a life-threatening emergency associated with high mortality and requires rapid diagnosis and immediate initiation of treatment. Early restoration of mesenteric perfusion is crucial for patient outcome. Revascularisation can be achieved by endovascular or open surgical techniques. The aim of this report is to illustrate different revascularisation strategies in two patients with acute superior mesenteric artery occlusion and to discuss their clinical indications and limitations.

INDICATIONS: Two patients with acute thrombotic occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery were treated using different revascularisation strategies. In the first patient, early diagnosis and the absence of radiological signs of advanced intestinal ischaemia led to primary endovascular aspiration thrombectomy. In the second patient, advanced intestinal ischaemia with transmural bowel necrosis and perforation necessitated open surgical revascularisation combined with intraoperative assessment and treatment of bowel viability.

METHODS: This study is a case-based video report supplemented by a selective narrative review of the literature. The diagnostic findings, technical aspects of revascularisation, management of intestinal viability, and postoperative courses are presented. The two treatment strategies are discussed in the context of the available literature. No systematic literature review or quantitative meta-analysis was performed.

CONCLUSION: Acute mesenteric ischaemia requires a rapid, time-critical, and interdisciplinary treatment approach. Endovascular treatment may be an appropriate minimally invasive option, particularly in patients with early diagnosis and without evidence of advanced intestinal ischaemia. Open surgical treatment remains essential in advanced or complex cases, particularly when bowel necrosis or perforation requires surgical exploration and resection. Current evidence suggests potential advantages of endovascular treatment; however, due to heterogeneous and predominantly retrospective data, general superiority of either endovascular or open surgical treatment cannot be established.

Early restoration of mesenteric perfusion is crucial for patient outcome. Revascularisation can be achieved by endovascular or open surgical techniques.

title: Systematic Review of Patient Priorities and Shared Decision Making in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease Treatment Decisions.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts.

DATA SOURCES: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase.

REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155). Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase were searched for English language studies published from 1 January 2000 to 17 December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with symptomatic PAD, reporting experiences, information needs, priorities, or decision making related to PAD treatment. Two reviewers independently screened studies, resolving disagreements by consensus with a third reviewer. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated using a structured thematic narrative approach.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included in the systematic review, comprising qualitative, mixed methods, observational registry or cohort, and stated preference studies, and one stepped wedge cluster randomised trial. Most qualitative and cohort studies were rated moderate to high quality. Participant reporting in the 34 studies was limited: seven studies (21%) did not report sex, two (6%) recruited men only, and most mixed sex studies recruited predominantly men; and 18 (53%) did not report ethnicity and, where reported, participants were predominantly White. Across heterogeneous studies, recurring patient valued domains included pain relief, walking ability, independence, emotional wellbeing, function, quality of life, treatment burden, risk, and uncertainty. Decision making processes were shaped by preferred involvement, trust, communication, clarity of options, and continuity of care. Studies identified a mismatch between patients' preferred and experienced decisional roles, with reported involvement lower than desired. Stated preference evidence showed heterogeneity in risk tolerance and treatment trade offs. Trial evidence reported improvements in shared decision making measures and patient knowledge after structured decision support and clinician training.

CONCLUSION: Patient valued outcomes and treatment trade offs vary across lower extremity PAD contexts and individuals. Shared decision making may help incorporate these priorities into treatment decisions, supported by tailored information, continuity of care, clinician training, and decision support tools.

title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.

RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.

However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. title: Patients Educating Patients: A Scalable Patient-Led Webinar Model Integrating Patient and Clinician Expertise in Venous Thromboembolism Care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with venous thromboembolism (VTE) face knowledge gaps about diagnosis, treatment, and management. We report the implementation of the National Blood Clot Alliance's (NBCA) Patients Educating Patients (PEP) Talks webinar series as a novel educational model for VTE survivors.

METHODS: PEP Talks is a virtual, monthly educational webinar series hosted by NBCA and moderated by two patient leaders and a clinical expert. Sessions featured patient-identified VTE topics with structured discussion and live interactive components, with recordings available for on-demand viewing. Program evaluation included registration volume, live attendance, and recording views. Participant engagement was measured by number of reactions and questions submitted during sessions. We assessed impact with pre- and post-webinar questions.

RESULTS: Twelve sessions were held between October 2024-January 2026. Eleven were recorded and uploaded online. A total of 5,731 individuals registered for the series. Across 12 sessions, 713 unique individuals attended at least one live session, with 1,600 total live attendances. Recordings accumulated 7,657 total views. Among attendees, the majority were VTE survivors (72%), followed by caregivers/relatives (6%) and healthcare professionals (7%). Individuals from 35 countries participated, with most from the US (78%). The majority (58% - 81%) viewed more than 75% of each session. Participant engagement was high, with 2,024 participant-generated questions and 269 positive audience reactions. Pre- and post-session polling demonstrated high levels of patient satisfaction and self-reported understanding of VTE-related concepts.

CONCLUSION: PEP Talks demonstrates the feasibility of a scalable, patient-centered educational webinar model for VTE survivors, achieving high engagement and favorable participant-reported educational outcomes.

We report the implementation of the National Blood Clot Alliance's (NBCA) Patients Educating Patients (PEP) Talks webinar series as a novel educational model for VTE survivors. METHODS: PEP Talks is a virtual, monthly educational webinar series hosted by NBCA and moderated by two patient leaders and a clinical expert.

title: Association between the platelet to lymphocyte ratio and the clinical outcome of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and clinical outcomes in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using appropriate tools, and pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects model with sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Ten studies involving patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage were included. The meta-analysis showed that a higher platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio was associated with an increased likelihood of poor functional outcome. In contrast, no clear association was observed between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and delayed cerebral ischemia in the pooled analysis. The odds ratios for pneumonia and deep vein thrombosis each came from a single independent study rather than from pooled meta-analytic analyses; these unpooled estimates therefore remain exploratory and should not be interpreted as combined effect sizes. Substantial heterogeneity was present across analyses, and sensitivity analyses suggested that the results for functional outcome and delayed cerebral ischemia were not entirely stable. The available evidence is limited by the small number of studies, heterogeneity in threshold values and outcome definitions, and geographic concentration of the included populations. In conclusion, the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio may serve as a readily available prognostic marker in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, but current evidence is insufficient to support its routine clinical use. Further large, well-designed multinational studies are needed to establish optimal thresholds and to clarify its incremental value in prognostic assessment.

We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. title: A pseudo-ischemic tumor ecosystem couples malignant stress and inflammatory myeloid remodeling across adenocarcinomas.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis and tumor immune remodeling may converge through hypoxia, myeloid inflammation, neutrophil extracellular traps, platelet engagement, and endothelial dysfunction. We investigated whether they define a conserved, transcriptomically measurable tumor state.

METHODS: We integrated a lung adenocarcinoma extracellular-vesicle RNA dataset with three venous thromboembolism cohorts to derive five immunothrombotic modules. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from lung (LUAD), pancreatic (PAAD), and gastric adenocarcinoma (STAD) were analyzed. We defined the pseudo-ischemic tumor ecosystem (PTES) as a transcriptomically defined molecular state reflecting coordinated malignant-cell stress and inflammatory-myeloid activity, rather than direct evidence of tissue ischemia or a diagnosis of cancer-associated thrombosis or venous thromboembolism. A tissue-resolved Core PTES, calculated as the mean of standardized malignant-stress and inflammatory-myeloid programs, was evaluated in 37 single-cell samples and 1107 TCGA tumors. Associations with immune states, Hallmark pathways, inferred cell-cell communication, and overall survival were assessed. The primary survival analysis used continuous Core PTES per one-standard-deviation increase, with high-versus-low PTES analyzed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Direct analysis showed the strongest effects for malignant stress (Hedges' g = 1.116), NET-like activity (g = 1.477), and endothelial activation (g = 1.288). Single-cell analysis retained 143,101 cells and localized malignant-stress and inflammatory-myeloid programs to their respective compartments. In TCGA, high Core PTES most strongly separated the inflammatory program (median difference = 1.134; rank-biserial r = 0.735). Cross-cancer GSEA identified recurrent proliferative, inflammatory, metabolic, and hypoxic programs, including E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, TNF-NF-κB, IL6-JAK-STAT3, glycolysis, and hypoxia. Inferred SPP1-CD44 and SPP1-ITGAV/ITGB1 interactions were detected across all three cancers. In multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, and stage, each one-standard-deviation increase in Core PTES was associated with poorer overall survival in LUAD (HR = 1.205, 95% CI 1.045-1.389) and PAAD (HR = 1.458, 95% CI 1.138-1.868), but not STAD (HR = 0.912, 95% CI 0.755-1.103); the cancer-stratified pooled HR was 1.168 (95% CI 1.060-1.288). High-versus-low sensitivity analyses showed the same cancer-specific pattern.

CONCLUSION: PTES captures a conserved pseudo-ischemic ecosystem linking malignant stress with inflammatory-myeloid remodeling. It is a hypothesis-generating, transcriptomically defined ecosystem measure rather than evidence of literal tissue ischemia, a diagnostic measure of cancer-associated thrombosis or venous thromboembolism, or a validated prognostic biomarker. Prospective clinical phenotyping and functional validation are required.

We investigated whether they define a conserved, transcriptomically measurable tumor state. METHODS: We integrated a lung adenocarcinoma extracellular-vesicle RNA dataset with three venous thromboembolism cohorts to derive five immunothrombotic modules.

title: Computed tomography assessment of distal anastomotic new entries after type A dissection repair.
abstract: Distal anastomotic new entries after type A aortic dissection repair provide a communication between the prosthetic lumen and the residual false lumen. Their presence is associated with distal aortic dilatation and reintervention, yet they often remain underreported on routine computed tomography angiography. This video tutorial describes a systematic approach on how to identify and measure these entries using multiplanar reconstruction. The distal anastomosis is first aligned in two orthogonal planes, using external felt reinforcement as a landmark when available. The complete anastomotic circumference is inspected to establish direct continuity between the prosthetic lumen and the false lumen. The entry is then separately aligned to obtain an en face, perpendicular view, allowing measurement of its maximum dimensions. Examples after hemiarch and zone 2 arch replacement illustrate the distinction between anastomotic entries and other sources of false-lumen perfusion. Longitudinal cases demonstrate persistent patency with aortic enlargement, spontaneous closure and thoracic false-lumen resorption 2 years after branched endovascular treatment. This approach supports consistent anatomical assessment, as well as longitudinal reporting.

title: Prevalence and associated factors of peripheral arterial disease in hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is common in hemodialysis patients and associated with adverse outcomes, but its prevalence and associated factors remain heterogeneous.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to April 8, 2026. Cross-sectional and cohort studies reporting PAD prevalence or associated factors were included. Random-effects models were used. Heterogeneity was explored using subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: The pooled prevalence was 23% (95%Confidence Intervals [CI], 20%∼26%) based on ankle brachial index ≤ 0.9, 42% (95%CI, 29%∼56%) based on ultrasonography or other imaging, and 19% (95%CI, 11%∼33%) based on clinical criteria. Both research regions and proportion of male were associated with heterogeneity. Factors associated with PAD included abdominal obesity (Odds Ratio [OR]=5.41), diabetes mellitus (OR=2.90), cardiovascular disease (OR=2.01), cerebrovascular disease (OR=1.91), male sex (OR=1.70), smoking (OR=1.64), hypertension (OR=1.34), C-reactive protein (OR=1.06), age (OR=1.04), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=1.02), dialysis vintage (OR=1.01), albumin (OR=0.97), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=0.94), Black race (OR=0.78), and serum creatinine (OR=0.75). Associations varied by diagnostic criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: PAD is common in hemodialysis patients, with prevalence varying substantially by diagnostic criteria and study settings. Several demographic and clinical characteristics were associated with PAD; however, most evidence was derived from cross-sectional studies and was of low or very low certainty. These findings should not be interpreted causally. Standardized diagnostic criteria and well-designed prospective studies are needed to improve the certainty and comparability of future evidence.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to April 8, 2026. Cross-sectional and cohort studies reporting PAD prevalence or associated factors were included.

title: Systematic Review of COVID-19 Vaccine Adverse Events, Efficacy, and Immunogenicity Among U.S. Military Health System Beneficiaries.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 vaccination was implemented throughout the Military Health System (MHS) to protect beneficiary health and maintain operational readiness. Although vaccine safety, effectiveness, and immunogenicity have been extensively evaluated in civilian populations, evidence specific to U.S. military personnel and other MHS beneficiaries has not previously been synthesized. This systematic review assessed adverse events, vaccine effectiveness, and immune responses following COVID-19 vaccination among MHS beneficiaries.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was a sub-analysis of a broader scoping review of COVID-19 vaccination outcomes. Seven bibliographic databases and relevant government and health organization websites were searched for English-language peer-reviewed and grey literature published from December 2020 through September 30, 2025. Eligible studies included active duty service members, retirees, or eligible dependents who received a U.S.-authorized COVID-19 vaccine. Paired reviewers independently conducted study screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Disagreements were resolved through consensus.

RESULTS: Of 9,396 records identified in the parent scoping review, 14 studies met eligibility criteria for the MHS population, including 7 cohort, 5 cross-sectional, and 2 case-control studies published between 2022 and 2025. Twelve studies had low overall risk of bias and 2 had moderate risk. Six studies evaluated adverse events and 8 evaluated vaccine effectiveness or immunogenicity. Severe adverse events following vaccination were uncommon. Although myocarditis and pericarditis occurred more frequently after vaccination than among unvaccinated individuals, their incidence was substantially higher following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination was also associated with reduced risks of post-infection venous thromboembolism, kidney complications, prolonged illness, and persistent symptoms. Vaccine effectiveness against infection was 89.2% during the pre-Delta period and 70.2% during Delta predominance, with mRNA-1273 demonstrating the highest effectiveness. Immunologic studies showed robust humoral and cellular responses following vaccination. Booster vaccination and hybrid immunity increased the magnitude, breadth, and durability of antibody responses, including improved neutralization of immune-evasive variants.

CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 vaccination was safe, immunogenic, and effective among MHS beneficiaries. Severe vaccine-associated adverse events were rare, while vaccination reduced infection, severe illness, long-term complications, and adverse outcomes associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Booster vaccination and hybrid immunity enhanced protection against emerging variants. These findings support continued evidence-based vaccination strategies to protect beneficiary health, force readiness, and deployability.

Although vaccine safety, effectiveness, and immunogenicity have been extensively evaluated in civilian populations, evidence specific to U.S. military personnel and other MHS beneficiaries has not previously been synthesized.

title: Surgical Treatment of Superior Mesenteric Arteriovenous Fistula after an Unsuccessful Endovascular Approach: A Case Report.
abstract: A superior mesenteric arteriovenous fistula (SMAVF) is an uncommon connection between the superior mesenteric artery and vein, usually secondary to surgery or trauma. Manifestations range from abdominal pain to portal hypertension. Although endovascular management is often preferred, surgery may be required in complex cases. We report the case of a 40-year-old male with a history of two laparotomies who presented with an acute abdomen. Computed tomography revealed aneurysmal venous dilation, and arteriography confirmed an SMAVF. After an unsuccessful attempt at endovascular coil embolization due to the high-flow shunt, the fistula was successfully closed by surgical ligation. Open surgery remains a definitive and effective option when an endovascular approach is unsuccessful, unavailable, or unsuitable.

Manifestations range from abdominal pain to portal hypertension. Although endovascular management is often preferred, surgery may be required in complex cases.

title: Retrograde Posterior Communicating Artery Access for Distal Carotid Artery Embolization in Acute Carotid Blowout Syndrome: A Case Report.
abstract: Carotid blowout syndrome (CBS) is a life-threatening complication in patients with head and neck cancer and is associated with substantial mortality and neurological morbidity. Endovascular approaches have largely replaced surgical ligation as the standard treatment. We report a case of a 40-year-old woman with a thyroid spindle cell neoplasm who presented with acute profuse hemorrhage from the tracheostomy site. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated luminal irregularity of the right common carotid artery (CCA), with extravasation consistent with CBS. Digital subtraction angiography revealed acute thrombotic occlusion of the right CCA, with preserved cerebral perfusion through the posterior communicating artery (PCom). Recurrent massive hemorrhage occurred during conservative management. After antegrade crossing of the occlusion failed, we achieved retrograde microcatheter access to the carotid artery through the ipsilateral PCom, followed by coil embolization of the distal carotid artery. The patient was discharged after 1 week and reported no recurrent bleeding 1 month after discharge.

Endovascular approaches have largely replaced surgical ligation as the standard treatment. title: Structural insights into three key platelet receptors for the discovery and development of anti-thrombotic therapies: PAR-1, αIIbβ3, and GPVI.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide and is strongly driven by thrombosis, which underlies events including stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis. Platelets are anucleate cell fragments produced by megakaryocytes that are essential for haemostasis but also make major contributions to pathological thrombosis. Although platelet receptors are major targets for antithrombotic therapy, current agents remain limited by bleeding risk, and no new antiplatelet drug has been approved since Cangrelor in 2015. The present review focuses on three structurally and mechanistically distinct platelet receptors with major relevance to drug discovery: PAR1, integrin αIIbβ3, and glycoprotein VI. These receptors represent key nodes spanning the G protein-coupled receptor, integrin, and immunoglobulin superfamily classes, and recent structural studies have clarified their activation mechanisms and drug-binding modes. I highlight how these insights have informed current inhibitors and are guiding the development of safer next-generation antithrombotic therapies. Finally, advancements in studying protein structure and their future impacts on drug design and optimisation are discussed.

title: Osteoporosis is associated with higher five-year surgical complication rates after total shoulder arthroplasty.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Existing retrospective studies of total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) in patients with osteoporosis are limited by short follow-up and small cohorts and may underestimate long-term complications. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the association between osteoporosis and medical and surgical complications after primary TSA.

METHODS: Of 99,028 patients who underwent primary TSA between January 2010 and April 2018, 13,138 had a preoperative diagnosis of osteoporosis and 85,890 did not. Patients with osteoporosis were older, more often female, and more comorbid. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared the cumulative incidence of surgical outcomes, and multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and Charlson Comorbidity Index compared complications.

RESULTS: Patients with osteoporosis had a higher five year risk of revision TSA (3.59% vs. 3.29%; HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.13-1.39; p < 0.001), with higher risks of periprosthetic fracture (HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.06-1.50; p = 0.008) and mechanical loosening (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.05-1.36; p = 0.006), and a borderline association with dislocation (HR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.00-1.26; p = 0.049). Medical complications were also increased, including deep vein thrombosis (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.10-1.31), pulmonary embolism (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.09-1.33), pneumonia (HR: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.06-1.21), fluid and electrolyte imbalance (HR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.27-1.71), transfusion (HR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.10-1.34), urinary tract infection (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.15-1.23), and myocardial infarction (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 1.04-1.28).

CONCLUSION: A preoperative diagnosis of osteoporosis is associated with a higher 5-year risk of revision, periprosthetic fracture, and mechanical loosening after primary TSA.

title: Research Evolution, Knowledge Structure, and Emerging Trends in Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: BackgroundRecurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) poses challenges for secondary prevention and long-term care. This study aimed to characterize the knowledge structure, research priorities, and thematic evolution of the recurrent VTE literature.MethodsA bibliometric analysis included 1,847 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed Central. Python-based analyses examined country, institution, and author collaboration, citation patterns, keyword bursts, thematic clustering, and knowledge evolution.ResultsPublication output increased substantially, particularly after 2000, with the United States and Italy among the leading contributors. Major themes included thrombophilia, recurrence risk factors, anticoagulation, post-thrombotic syndrome, bleeding, cancer, and pulmonary embolism. Keyword bursts suggested an expansion from mechanistic research toward risk prediction, long-term outcomes, and individualized management.ConclusionsRecurrent VTE research has broadened toward risk assessment, treatment benefit-harm evaluation, and long-term outcomes. Further research should validate prediction tools across populations, establish the added value of biomarkers, and evaluate individualized secondary prevention.

title: Female Sex Is Associated With Increased Health Care Use and Revision Risk After Achilles Tendon Repair.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate sex-based differences in complications, health care use, and revision rates after Achilles tendon repair.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults undergoing primary Achilles tendon repair between 2015 and 2023 were identified, stratified by sex, and matched 1:1 using propensity scores. The primary outcome was revision Achilles tendon repair; secondary outcomes were postoperative complications, emergency department visits, inpatient admissions, and opioid prescriptions, assessed at 90-day and 2-year intervals. Follow-up duration was recorded for each cohort. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated, with significance set at P < .05.

RESULTS: A total of 11,251 patients were identified (68.2% men, 31.8% women). The mean follow-up was 82.0 days (men) and 81.8 days (women) for the 90-day analysis and 535.5 days (men) and 569.9 days (women) for the 2-year analysis, with a median follow-up that reached the full window in each cohort. Within 90 days postoperatively, both male and female patients experienced similar rates of wound dehiscence (P = .098), infections (P = .835), and deep vein thrombosis (P = .677). Female patients had significantly more postoperative emergency department visits (7.8% vs 5.6%, OR 1.42, P = .001) and opioid prescriptions (29.4% vs 26.8%, OR 1.14, P = .025) than males. At 2 years, female patients also showed a higher rate of revision surgery (4.4% vs 3.4%, OR 1.31, P = .048).

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with male patients, female patients undergoing Achilles tendon repair had significantly higher rates of health care use (emergency department visits and opioid prescriptions) within 90 days and revision surgery within 2 years postoperatively. Differences in revision were small and may not be clinically meaningful.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

title: Prevalence of a Bicuspid Aortic Valve Among Patients Undergoing Surgery for Aortic Dissection and the Influence of Native Aortic Valve Morphology on Surgical Outcome: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background A bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is associated with aortopathy and an increased risk of aortic dissection, but most patients presenting with dissection have a tricuspid aortic valve. We determined the proportion of patients with BAV among those undergoing surgery for aortic dissection and compared operative strategy, morbidity, mortality, and survival by native valve morphology. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included 132 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for aortic dissection between 2000 and 2025. Dissection was diagnosed by CT, and valve morphology (bicuspid or tricuspid) was determined by intraoperative inspection. Categorical variables were compared using Fisher's exact test, continuous variables using the Mann-Whitney U test, and survival using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test. Results The mean age was 47.6 ± 13.0 years, and 102 patients (77.3%) were male. Supracoronary ascending aortic replacement (SCAAR) was performed in 102 patients (77.3%) and a Bentall procedure in 30 (22.7%). Ten patients (7.6%, 95% CI: 4.2-13.4%) had a bicuspid valve. Assuming a general-population BAV prevalence of 0.5-2%, this corresponds to an estimated relative risk of dissection of about 4-16. Overall mortality was 14.4% (19 patients), including 17 in-hospital deaths (12.9%). Mean follow-up was 4.70 ± 4.80 years (range: 0-22). Age, ICU stay, and hospital stay did not differ between the groups. Bicuspid patients more often underwent a Bentall procedure (50.0% vs 20.5%, p = 0.047) and had higher mortality (40.0% vs 12.3%, p = 0.037). Survival differed between the groups (log-rank χ² = 5.100, p = 0.024), with the divergence occurring early after surgery. Conclusions BAV was present in 7.6% of patients undergoing surgery for aortic dissection, which suggests a higher relative risk of dissection than in the general population, although most dissections occurred with tricuspid valves. Bicuspid morphology was associated with more frequent root replacement and higher early mortality.

Methods This retrospective single-centre study included 132 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for aortic dissection between 2000 and 2025.
