title: Bisphenol A and Its Analogues in Hypertension: Molecular Mechanisms, Epigenetic Regulation, and Therapeutic Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Hypertension is a leading risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including heart failure, stroke, and peripheral artery disease, with a lifetime risk exceeding 90% among adults aged 55-65 years. Its pathophysiology involves arterial stiffness, blood pressure variability, hormonal and neuronal dysregulation, age-related renal change, and endothelial dysfunction. Environmental endocrine disruptors, notably bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogues, are widely used in plastics and epoxy resins and may contribute by interacting with estrogen receptors and disrupting hormonal homeostasis, although human clinical evidence remains limited. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological evidence, molecular mechanisms, and emerging therapeutic strategies linking bisphenol exposure to hypertension. The literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for publications from 2000 to 2025 and appraised with reference to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). The mechanisms considered include oxidative stress, TGF-β/SMAD and MAPK signaling, the PI3K/AKT axis, and FOXO transcription factors, together with epigenetic alterations such as DNA methylation and histone modification. Human studies are appraised separately from experimental work, and exposure relevance, administered dose, and non-monotonic dose-response relationships are addressed explicitly. Therapeutic approaches are organized as exposure reduction, treatment of established cardiovascular effects, mechanism-directed strategies, and experimental approaches including nanoparticle-mediated delivery, chronotherapy, and RNA-based therapeutics; all remain preclinical and none has been evaluated specifically in BPA-associated hypertension. Because the human evidence is predominantly cross-sectional and the mechanistic data derive largely from experimental models, the relationships described should be regarded as associations and plausible mechanisms rather than established causal pathways.

title: Pharmacologic bridging to PTA in hyperkalemic hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVF: Impact on day surgery workflow and procedural feasibility.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia can delay percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) when dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) limit dialysis. We evaluated pharmacologic potassium lowering as a bridge to PTA on the day of presentation.

METHODS: We retrospectively screened 871 PTA encounters in a day surgery unit; 122 met potassium ⩾5.5 mmol/L. Six underwent emergency dialysis and 116 received pharmacologic bridge treatment. The primary endpoint was PTA on the day of presentation without rescue dialysis before PTA.

RESULTS: The primary endpoint occurred in 110/116 encounters (94.8%; 95% CI, 89.1%-98.1%). Paired potassium values were retrievable in 53 patients, decreasing from 6.14 ± 0.42 to 5.10 ± 0.65 mmol/L (p < 0.001). Technical, clinical, and immediate dialysis success were 100%, 98.1%, and 96.2%, respectively, in this detailed cohort. Numeric potassium after treatment was undocumented before the PTA decision in 57/116 encounters.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic bridging was feasible, but incomplete retrospective reassessment limits conclusions about safety and uniform biochemical reassessment.

title: Real-World 30-day Outcomes Following Commercial Adoption of the GORE EXCLUDER Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis: A National Medicare Analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

METHODS: Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.

RESULTS: The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke (<1.3% vs. <1.6%), MI (2.0% vs. <1.6%), AKI (7.2% vs. 6.9%) or SCI (5.0% vs. 4.1%) (all P>.05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).

CONCLUSION: In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.

Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

title: Factitious Disorder Presenting as Recurrent Aortic Emergencies: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Factitious disorder, historically known as Munchausen's syndrome, is a psychiatric condition characterized by the intentional fabrication or induction of symptoms without obvious external incentives. Patients frequently present with dramatic, medically convincing concerns that can mimic life-threatening illnesses and prompt extensive diagnostic evaluations. Although hemorrhagic presentations have been described, presentations mimicking catastrophic vascular disease are uncommon and pose unique challenges for emergency medicine and vascular teams. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man with a subsequently documented diagnosis of factitious disorder repeatedly presented to multiple hospitals with dramatic hematemesis concerning for an aortoenteric fistula. Over an 8-year period, he underwent multiple diagnostic evaluations and several aortic interventions, including endovascular aortic repair and later explantation, despite repeated studies showing no aortoenteric pathology. In 2024, he developed bilateral renal artery occlusions secondary to focal aortic dissection requiring emergent stenting. A psychiatric evaluation at an outside institution ultimately diagnosed Munchausen syndrome. Recurrent presentations across healthcare systems, repeatedly negative diagnostic evaluations, inconsistent objective findings, and family-reported discovery of vials containing a red blood-like fluid provided additional evidence concerning for deliberate symptom fabrication. CONCLUSIONS This case report shows how factitious disorder can mimic life-threatening vascular disease. While urgent pathology must be excluded, recurrent high-acuity presentations accompanied by inconsistent objective findings should prompt cross-institutional record review, multidisciplinary evaluation, and broader diagnostic consideration to prevent unnecessary procedural escalation and iatrogenic harm, facilitate earlier diagnostic recognition, and support appropriate psychiatric intervention.

title: Variations in the penile cavernous circulation and erectile dysfunction: a topic review.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To review anatomical and hemodynamic variations of the penile cavernous circulation and their impact on the interpretation of color Doppler ultrasonography in patients with erectile dysfunction.

METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was conducted focusing on penile arterial and venous anatomy, erectile physiology, Doppler ultrasonography technique, and hemodynamic parameters used in the evaluation of vascular erectile dysfunction. Particular attention was given to cavernous artery variants, collateral arterial pathways, helicine artery morphology, and venous drainage patterns that influence Doppler waveforms and diagnostic thresholds.

RESULTS: Multiple anatomical variations of the penile cavernous circulation were identified, including cavernous artery duplication, intercavernous arterial bridges, and extracavernous arterial pathways. These variants can significantly alter hemodynamic parameters, potentially leading to diagnostic misclassification. Emerging evidence supports arterial leakage as a distinct and underrecognized category of vascular erectile dysfunction, characterized by abnormal arterial outflow patterns that may mimic venous leakage on Doppler evaluation.

CONCLUSION: Accurate recognition of penile vascular anatomy and flow variations during color Doppler ultrasonography is essential for proper classification of vascular erectile dysfunction. Awareness of these anatomical and hemodynamic factors helps avoid diagnostic errors and may facilitate appropriate patient selection for targeted therapeutic strategies, including endovascular and reconstructive interventions.

METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was conducted focusing on penile arterial and venous anatomy, erectile physiology, Doppler ultrasonography technique, and hemodynamic parameters used in the evaluation of vascular erectile dysfunction. Particular attention was given to cavernous artery variants, collateral arterial pathways, helicine artery morphology, and venous drainage patterns that influence Doppler waveforms and diagnostic thresholds.

title: Increased risk of arteriovenous fistula thrombosis in haemodialysis patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis: a retrospective comparative study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the occurrence and timing of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) thrombosis in patients undergoing maintenance haemodialysis (HD) due to ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) and those with non-vasculitic causes of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included patients receiving maintenance HD for AAV-related ESKD and a control group with ESKD attributed to diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis. The AVF thrombosis analysis was restricted to patients with an AVF during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate the association between AAV and AVF thrombosis.

RESULTS: The study included 31 patients with AAV (mean age 71.3 ± 13.6 years; 58% male) and 102 controls (mean age 55.8 ± 17.9 years; 56% male). Among patients with an AVF, thrombosis occurred in 9 of 18 patients (50%) in the AAV group and 6 of 51 patients (11.8%) in the control group (p = .002). In the unadjusted Cox regression analysis, AAV was associated with a higher hazard of AVF thrombosis (HR 4.14, 95% CI 1.43-11.97; p = .009). This association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age (HR 4.46, 95% CI 1.39-14.26; p = .012).

CONCLUSION: AAV was associated with a higher hazard of AVF thrombosis in patients undergoing maintenance HD compared with non-vasculitic ESKD, even after adjustment for age. However, the limited number of thrombotic events and potential residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their implications for vascular access management.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included patients receiving maintenance HD for AAV-related ESKD and a control group with ESKD attributed to diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis. The AVF thrombosis analysis was restricted to patients with an AVF during follow-up.

title: Risk and Outcomes of Acute Aortic Events in Patients With Polycystic Kidney Disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated whether polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is associated with an increased risk of life-threatening acute aortic events (AAEs) and adverse clinical outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool. The mean follow-up was 9.5 years. The primary outcome was the incidence of AAE, defined as aortic rupture, aortic dissection, or death due to aortic disease. Secondary outcomes were in-hospital and post-discharge complications. The matched cohort comprised 3,655 patients with PKD and 36,550 controls. PKD was associated with significantly increased risks of aortic rupture (hazard ratio [HR] 4.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.74-10.16), aortic dissection (HR 2.31; 95% CI 1.50-3.54), and death due to aortic disease (HR 3.82; 95% CI 2.02-7.23). Among 40,995 admissions for AAEs, patients with PKD had a higher risk of new-onset dialysis (odds ratio 2.59; 95% CI 1.13-5.91). After discharge, patients with PKD also had higher risks of stroke, readmission, and new-onset maintenance dialysis than controls.

CONCLUSIONS: PKD was associated with increased risks of life-threatening AAEs and subsequent adverse outcomes. These findings support heightened clinical awareness and risk-based cardiovascular assessment in select high-risk patients.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool.

title: Interventional radiology of the head and neck: Superselective intra-arterial chemoradiotherapy, preoperative tumor embolization, and emergency hemostasis.
abstract: Interventional radiology (IVR) of the head and neck is an essential component of multidisciplinary care, serving to intensify local treatment, to reduce the risk of perioperative bleeding, and to provide life-saving control of catastrophic hemorrhage. This review outlines endovascular treatment in three settings-superselective intra-arterial chemoradiotherapy (RADPLAT), preoperative tumor embolization, and emergency hemostasis for intractable epistaxis and carotid blowout syndrome (CBS)-with emphasis on clinical indications together with their advantages and limitations, anatomical considerations including dangerous anastomoses, devices and techniques, avoidance of complications, pre- and post-procedural imaging, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Association Between Adjunctive Single-Ingredient Diosmin Prescribing and Short-Term Clinical Outcomes in Acute Lower-Extremity Superficial Vein Thrombosis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between documented adjunctive single-ingredient diosmin prescribing and short-term clinical outcomes in adults with acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective 48-hour landmark cohort study of 1,820 consecutive adults with duplex-confirmed acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis treated from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2025. Exposure was a diosmin prescription issued within 48 hours and intended for at least 7 days. The primary outcome was complete resolution or marked clinical improvement at the in-person assessment closest to day 14 within days 10 to 18. Missing baseline covariates were multiply imputed, and propensity scores were estimated within 20 imputed data sets. Stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting targeted the average treatment effect under measured-confounding assumptions. Secondary outcomes, including day-7 pain, were exploratory.

RESULTS: Diosmin was prescribed to 910 patients and not prescribed to 910. Primary improvement occurred in 728/910 (80.0%) and 669/910 (73.5%), respectively. Weighted standardized probabilities were 79.5% (95% confidence interval, 76.8%-82.2%) and 74.7% (71.8%-77.6%), yielding a risk difference of 4.8 percentage points (1.2-8.4) and a risk ratio of 1.06 (1.01-1.12). The E-value was 1.31 for the point estimate and 1.11 for the confidence limit. Excluding 142 patients with concomitant distal deep vein thrombosis gave a similar estimate (risk difference, 4.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 1.3-8.5). Exploratory day-7 pain-response probabilities were 75.0% and 61.5% after imputation, weighting, and marginal standardization. Thrombotic and bleeding estimates were imprecise.

CONCLUSIONS: Documented adjunctive diosmin prescribing was associated with a small increase in short-term clinical improvement. Clinical importance is uncertain, and relatively weak unmeasured confounding could explain the primary association. The exploratory pain finding is hypothesis-generating. These data are insufficient to support routine diosmin use or substitution for guideline-directed anticoagulation; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective 48-hour landmark cohort study of 1,820 consecutive adults with duplex-confirmed acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis treated from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2025. Exposure was a diosmin prescription issued within 48 hours and intended for at least 7 days.

title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.

RESULTS: The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.

CONCLUSION: Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

title: DANTE T1-SPACE MR imaging for visualization of inferior and superior petrosal sinus anatomy in cavernous sinus DAVF.
abstract: DANTE (Delay Alternating with Nutation for Tailored Excitation) is useful for investigating venous sinus conditions, including thrombosis, hypoplasia, and occlusions. The study aimed to assess the efficacy of the DANTE MRI sequence in visualizing the inferior petrosal sinus (IPS) and superior petrosal sinus (SPS) in patients with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). DANTE preparation provides robust suppression of flowing blood signal while preserving stationary tissue signal, which may improve delineation of venous sinus lumen and wall changes compared with conventional 3D TSE sequences. Fourteen patients with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas were retrospectively analyzed. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced DANTE T1-SPACE MRI prior to endovascular treatment. IPS patency was independently evaluated on MRI and descriptively compared with digital subtraction angiography. Nine out of fourteen patients demonstrated occlusion of the ipsilateral IPS. Two had stenotic changes in the IPS. The IPS was identified in all patients, regardless of patency, and transvenous embolization was successfully performed via the IPS in all treated cases. In the SPS, lumen continuity between SPS and Cavernous sinus was confirmed in 5 cases. 78.5% of patients achieved occlusion immediately after treatment, with the remaining patients occluded during follow-up. Contrast-enhanced DANTE T1-SPACE offers high-contrast depiction of IPS/SPS by effective blood-signal suppression with preservation of static tissue signal, facilitating preprocedural anatomical clarification in CSDAVF. This information may be particularly useful in cases with suspected IPS occlusion, where preprocedural anatomical clarification is clinically relevant.

title: When Hip Pain Is Vascular: Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysmal Lesion in Behçet's Disease Treated with a Covered Stent.
abstract: Behçet's disease is a chronic relapsing systemic vasculitis in which arterial involvement is less common than venous disease but carries substantial rupture risk. Internal iliac artery involvement is rare and may be overlooked because symptoms are often nonspecific. We report a 34-year-old man with established Behçet's disease referred from orthopaedic surgery after 2 to 3 months of right hip and deep gluteal pain initially considered musculoskeletal. Plain hip x-ray was unremarkable. Pelvic imaging demonstrated a right pelvic arterial lesion, and computed tomography angiography (CTA) confirmed a 57 mm saccular aneurysmal lesion arising from the right internal iliac artery. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and perioperative immunosuppression was optimized with rheumatology input. Endovascular repair was performed via contralateral left common femoral access using a 6 × 60 mm self-expanding covered stent graft across the diseased internal iliac segment, without adjunctive coil embolization. Completion angiography showed complete sac exclusion with preserved distal internal iliac flow. Recovery was uneventful. One-month CTA confirmed persistent exclusion and stent-graft patency, and the patient remained clinically asymptomatic at 12 months. This case highlights an orthopaedic mimic and supports carefully selected flow-preserving endovascular repair under immunosuppressive cover, with lifelong imaging surveillance to detect late complications in this inflammatory disease setting.Clinical ImpactInternal iliac artery aneurysmal lesions are rare manifestations of vascular Behçet's disease and may present with hip, buttock or groin pain due to deep pelvic mass effect, leading to initial orthopaedic referral and potential diagnostic delay. This case emphasizes the need to consider a vascular cause in Behçet's disease patients with unexplained persistent pelvic or hip pain, especially when plain radiographs are normal. It also illustrates a flow-preserving endovascular strategy using a covered stent graft to exclude the lesion while maintaining internal iliac artery patency. Because Behçet's disease is an inflammatory vasculitis, technical success alone is insufficient; perioperative immunosuppression and lifelong clinical and imaging surveillance remain central to management.

Internal iliac artery involvement is rare and may be overlooked because symptoms are often nonspecific. title: One-Year Results From the EMBRACE Registry Evaluating the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis during BEVAR for Complex Abdominal and Thoracoabdominal Aneurysms.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The stability of bridging stents is critical to ensure the effectiveness and safety of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA). The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR.

METHODS: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up. Patients were divided into BEVAR and fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) arms. This analysis reports the BEVAR cohort, which included patients receiving the VBX Stent Graft as a bridging stent for at least 1 visceral vessel. The primary endpoint was patient-level primary patency at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included technical success, reintervention, and target vessel patency assessed annually for up to 5 years. Secondary safety outcomes included major adverse events and aneurysm-related mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 165 patients (69.1% male, mean age 72.5 ± 9 years) were enrolled, receiving 454 VBX Stent Grafts (26.0% celiac trunk, 28.9% superior mesenteric artery (SMA), 21.8% left renal, and 23.3% right renal artery). VBX Stent Graft technical success was 99.6%. Thirty-day mortality was 7.9%, with major adverse events in 15.2% (1.8% respiratory failure, 7.3% renal function deterioration, 0.6% bowel ischemia, 4.2% paraplegia, and 1.8% major stroke). Freedom from aneurysm-related mortality was 92.1% at 30 days and 90.2% at 1 year. Freedom from patient-level VBX-related reintervention was 91.7%. Patient-level primary patency and secondary patency were 97.7% and 98.5%, respectively. Freedom from target vessel instability at the patient level was 90.4%.

CONCLUSION: Short-term findings from this multicenter registry confirm that the VBX Stent Graft is a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR, demonstrating high technical success, excellent 1-year patency, and low rates of target vessel instability. Ongoing follow-up will evaluate mid-term durability.Clinical ImpactBridging stent performance is fundamental to the success of branched endovascular repair, yet multicenter, real-world data remain limited. This analysis from the EMBRACE registry demonstrates high technical reliability, excellent 1-year target vessel patency, and low rates of VBX Stent Graft-related reintervention. Technical failures were uncommon and were primarily associated with inadequate distal landing zones, highlighting the importance of procedural planning. These findings provide clinicians with contemporary evidence supporting the VBX Stent Graft as a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR and may inform procedural decision-making to optimize target vessel durability.

The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR. METHODS: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up.

title: Past, present and future of Estetrol (E4); a natural fetal estrogen for human use.
abstract: Estetrol (E4) is a natural estrogen produced by the fetal liver with a distinctive pharmacologic profile separating it from other natural and synthetic estrogens. Encompassing 25 years of research and development, this review summarizes the history, biochemistry, pharmacology, clinical development, and potential future applications of E4. Essential features of E4 are (1) its high oral bioavailability, long half-life and minimal binding to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), enabling once-daily oral use, and (2) the limited effects on liver function, especially on hemostatic factors, resulting in a lower risk of venous thromboembolism compared to other natural and synthetic estrogens. Estetrol is further characterized as a natural estrogen with selective tissue activity, with a limited impact on breast tissue and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters, while preserving efficacy including bone mass protection. Estetrol therefore has the potential for a markedly improved safety profile. Clinically, the E4/drospirenone (DRSP) combined oral contraceptive (COC) is available worldwide since 2022 and provides effective contraception, a predictable bleeding profile, and a favorable tolerability profile. In phase 2 and 3 studies in postmenopausal women, oral E4 improves vasomotor symptoms, vaginal and urogenital complaints, and quality of life and wellbeing. Ongoing research is exploring wider uses, including combination with the oral GnRH antagonist relugolix for a COC with a focus on the perimenopausal transition and possible applications of E4 in gynecology, endocrinology, obstetrics, neurology and oncology, especially the treatment of advanced breast and prostate cancer.

title: Revascularisation Strategies in Dialysis-Dependent Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We reviewed dialysis-specific evidence on bypass and endovascular treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia to assess how the available comparisons inform the initial revascularisation decision.

METHODS: We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes. We applied nested restrictions by excluding mixed-open comparisons, retaining adjusted or matched comparisons, then excluding success-selected cohorts and abstract-only reports.

RESULTS: Sixteen reports represented 13 study families. Comparisons differed in whether they captured treatment attempted, treatment received or successful procedures. Selected comparisons reported associations favouring bypass for limb or wound outcomes. In the as-treated dialysis analysis of the Best Endovascular versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients with Critical Limb Ischaemia trial, single-segment great saphenous vein bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.94) and higher mortality (1.69, 1.06-2.70) than endovascular treatment. The estimate for amputation or death was imprecise (1.47, 0.95-2.27). Death handling for reintervention was unclear. Mixed-open comparisons suggested lower early amputation and more bleeding and wound complications. After successive restrictions, the remaining evidence did not establish an initial-strategy preference.

CONCLUSIONS: In dialysis-dependent CLTI, SSGSV bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard but higher mortality in the as-treated BEST-CLI comparison; other favourable limb findings came from non-equivalent cohorts. These associations do not establish a net advantage or preferred initial strategy. Decisions should weigh limb threat, anatomy, conduit suitability, expected survival, perioperative risk, functional goals and treatment burden.

METHODS: We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes.

title: Extensive Cerebral Infarction Following Cerebral Vasospasm Despite Repeated Endovascular Treatment in a Patient With Twig-Like Middle Cerebral Artery.
abstract: Twig-like middle cerebral artery (T-MCA) is a rare cerebrovascular anomaly characterized by replacement of the M1 segment with a plexiform arterial network. Altered cerebral hemodynamics associated with this vascular configuration may contribute to aneurysm formation and hemorrhagic events. However, the influence of cerebral vasospasm on collateral-dependent cerebral perfusion in patients with T-MCA has received little attention. We report a 43-year-old woman who presented with subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by rupture of an anterior communicating artery aneurysm associated with left T-MCA. Cerebral angiography demonstrated markedly limited antegrade flow through the anomalous arterial network, whereas delayed arterial-phase images showed collateral perfusion of the distal middle cerebral artery territory through leptomeningeal pathways arising from the anterior cerebral artery territory. Coil embolization was successfully performed. During the subsequent course, recurrent cerebral vasospasm was treated with repeated intra-arterial fasudil infusions; however, the patient developed extensive cerebral infarction involving both the anterior and middle cerebral artery territories despite repeated endovascular treatment. These findings suggest that cerebral perfusion in patients with T-MCA may depend, at least in part, on collateral circulation from adjacent vascular territories. This case illustrates the potential vulnerability of collateral-dependent cerebral perfusion during vasospasm and suggests that recognition of collateral-dependent perfusion patterns may be important when evaluating and managing vasospasm after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Altered cerebral hemodynamics associated with this vascular configuration may contribute to aneurysm formation and hemorrhagic events. title: Association between the stress hyperglycemia ratio and restenosis at 12 months after first percutaneous transluminal angioplasty in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) is associated with 12-month target lesion restenosis after first percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) of autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis in patients on maintenance hemodialysis (MHD).

METHODS: We retrospectively included 158 MHD patients undergoing first PTA for autologous AVF stenosis at Shaoxing Second Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024. SHR was calculated from preoperative venous glucose and glycated hemoglobin A1c, and patients were grouped by quartiles. The primary endpoint was target lesion restenosis within 12 months, with all patients retained and follow-up administratively censored at 12 months. Cause-specific Cox models were fitted: Model 0 was unadjusted; Model 1 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, smoking, diabetes, hypertension, statin use and antiplatelet therapy; Model 2 further adjusted for dialysis vintage, access site, dialysis modality, pre-procedure stenosis severity, Ln(C-reactive protein), lesion length and vascular calcification. Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses of 13 categorical factors, a Fine-Gray competing-risk model, exploratory mediation analysis and discrimination analysis were also performed.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 104 patients (65.8%) developed restenosis, 11 (7.0%) died before restenosis and 43 (27.2%) were censored at 12 months. Restenosis incidence from Q1 to Q4 was 25.6% (10/39), 50.0% (20/40), 94.9% (37/39) and 92.5% (37/40) (log-rank P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, fully adjusted Model 2 HRs for Q2-Q4 were 2.29 (95% CI 1.04-5.04; P = 0.039), 4.30 (2.08-8.87; P < 0.001) and 5.51 (2.52-12.07; P < 0.001). Each 1-SD increase in SHR was associated with an HR of 1.57 (1.25-1.96) in Model 2 (P < 0.001), and restricted cubic splines showed a nonlinear association (P < 0.001). Ln(CRP) was independently associated with restenosis (HR 1.62, 1.06-2.48; P = 0.027). Subgroup and competing-risk analyses were consistent; the exploratory indirect effect through Ln(CRP) was 0.090 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.000-0.199).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative SHR was independently associated with 12-month restenosis after first autologous AVF PTA in MHD patients, showing a nonlinear relationship. As it derives from routine laboratory tests, SHR may aid preoperative risk stratification; causality and clinical utility require prospective multicenter validation.

METHODS: We retrospectively included 158 MHD patients undergoing first PTA for autologous AVF stenosis at Shaoxing Second Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024. title: Challenging the Concept of Inertness: Hypersensitivity Reaction to a PTFE Vascular Graft-A Case Report.
abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts are widely used for hemodialysis access when autologous vascular reconstruction is not feasible, but true hypersensitivity reactions are exceptionally rare and may closely mimic graft infection. We report a 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on chronic hemodialysis who underwent resection of a symptomatic aneurysmal segment of a native brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula (AVF) and interposition of a 6-mm PTFE graft because the remaining cephalic vein was markedly calcified and unsuitable for primary reconstruction. Four days after surgery, progressive erythema, induration, and vesiculobullous lesions developed around the operative site. Infection, vascular compromise, hematoma, and material-related hypersensitivity were considered. Inflammatory markers were only moderately elevated, peripheral eosinophilia was documented, dermatologic assessment favored a hypersensitivity reaction, and surgical exploration showed extensive inflammatory and fibrotic tissue around the graft without macroscopic purulence. The PTFE graft was completely removed, the AVF was ligated, and the brachial artery was repaired directly. Histopathology demonstrated a prominent eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate with polymorphonuclear cells. The cutaneous reaction regressed rapidly after graft explantation, and hand function recovered fully. Hemodialysis was continued through a tunneled central venous catheter. This case illustrates that severe postoperative inflammation around a PTFE vascular graft should prompt consideration of material-related hypersensitivity alongside infection and supports early graft removal when a progressive reaction is clinically severe and the prosthesis is the suspected trigger.

Four days after surgery, progressive erythema, induration, and vesiculobullous lesions developed around the operative site.

title: Complex Endovascular Repair for Genetically-Triggered Aortic Disease in Italy (CENTRAL Multicentric Registry).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers. Primary endpoints were technical and clinical success, early and mid-term survival, and major adverse events (MAEs). Secondary endpoints included target vessel instability and the need for reintervention. Survival and freedom from adverse events were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 45 CTD patients (62.2% male; mean age, 56.4 ± 11.7 years) were treated with F/BEVAR. Marfan syndrome was present in 80% of patients, and 68.9% were treated for post-dissection TAAA. Most patients presented with type II TAAA (91.1%), and 88.9% had undergone at least 1 prior aortic operation. Technical and clinical success were achieved in 86.6% and 82.2% of cases, respectively. Early mortality and MAEs occurred in 4.4% of patients. During a mean clinical follow-up of 35.0 ± 33.9 months, estimated overall survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 90.0%, 86.7%, and 79.2%, respectively, with no aorta-related deaths. At a mean imaging follow-up of 33.8 ± 32.2 months, target vessel patency was 98.8%. Target vessel instability occurred in 40% of patients, and 42.2% required 1 or more secondary interventions. Reintervention-free survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 75.6%, 72.4%, and 59.0%, respectively. No baseline, anatomic, or procedural variable independently predicted late adverse outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of CTD patients, predominantly treated in complex redo settings, F/BEVAR demonstrated acceptable early and mid-term outcomes. Late adverse events and reinterventions were frequent but consistent with the natural history of CTD-related aortic disease and were not driven by identifiable baseline factors. These findings support the role of F/BEVAR as a valuable approach within a comprehensive, lifelong management strategy for CTD patients rather than as a definitive alternative to open surgery (OS).Clinical ImpactPatients with genetically triggered aortic disease often require multiple interventions throughout their lifetime because of the progressive nature of the underlying aortopathy. In this context, fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) should not be considered an alternative to open surgery, but rather a complementary approach within the long-term management of these patients. This multicenter study provides one of the largest dedicated experiences with F/BEVAR in this challenging population, showing that acceptable early and mid-term outcomes can be achieved even in complex redo and post-dissection settings. These findings support the integration of endovascular techniques into individualized, lifelong aortic treatment strategies at experienced centers, acknowledging the need for continued surveillance and secondary interventions.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs). METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers.

title: Machine Learning Versus Traditional Methods for Predicting Venous Thromboembolism After Surgery: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative venous thromboembolism remains a major cause of preventable morbidity after surgery, and established risk scores may perform inconsistently across surgical populations.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies comparing machine learning with traditional risk models for postoperative venous thromboembolism prediction. Risk-of-bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI. The primary outcome was discrimination measured by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis estimated mean differences versus Caprini with 95% credible intervals. Best and worst-version analyses explored the impact of within-study multiplicity, with subgroup analyses by cancer surgery and procedure type.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies including 177 656 validation patients were included. Meta-ensembles showed the largest improvement compared with Caprini in the best-version analysis (mean difference in AUROC, 0.232; 95% credible interval, 0.129-0.334), with a similar finding in the worst-version analysis (0.237; 0.123-0.351). Several other machine learning classes also had higher AUROC estimates than Caprini, whereas most traditional scores and surgeon judgement did not. Geneva showed lower performance than Caprini. Meta-ensembles ranked first overall, while Caprini and Geneva ranked 14th and last, respectively. Meta-ensembles and boosting models had higher AUROC than Caprini in both cancer surgery analyses; in general surgery, no model class showed higher performance than Caprini in the worst-version analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning models, particularly meta-ensembles, showed higher reported discrimination than traditional scores, but evidence remains limited by heterogeneity, inconsistent calibration reporting, sparse decision-analytic evaluation and infrequent external validation. Clinical adoption requires external validation and demonstration of real-world net benefit.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies comparing machine learning with traditional risk models for postoperative venous thromboembolism prediction. Risk-of-bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI.

title: Disappearance of the Postoperative New SWI Lesions after Flow Diverter Treatment for Cerebral Aneurysms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Little is known about changes over time for SWI lesions newly observed following endovascular surgery. This study was aimed to introduce disappearance of postoperative new SWI lesions after flow diverter (FD) treatment for cerebral aneurysms with serial MRI scans.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective observational study, patients who underwent FD treatment for cerebral aneurysms between December 2017 and June 2024 were analyzed. The patients received dual antiplatelet therapy at least 2 weeks before the treatment to obtain appropriate inhibition of platelet aggregation. Systemic heparinization was introduced during the FD deployment to maintain activated clotting time more than 250 sec. MRI including SWI were routinely obtained preoperatively (1 to 3 days before the FD treatment), postoperative day 1 and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after the surgery. By comparing the preoperative MRI with those obtained postoperative day 1, new lesions in SWI that appeared in the FD-treated vascular territory were detected. Their locations were divided into gray matter supplied by cortical arteries (cortex), white matter and gray matter supplied by perforators (deep nucleus such as basal ganglia, thalamus, and dentate nucleus). The new SWI lesions had been monitored with follow-up MRI for their changes over time and determined whether they disappeared or not.

RESULTS: Seventy-six aneurysms from 73 patients were included. Mean age was 65.2 ± 13.6 years old and 55 (75.3%) were female. On postoperative day 1, 525 new SWI lesions (median number 5 [0-64]) were detected in 67 patients. Of these, 263 (50.1%) were located in the cortex, 244 (46.5%) were in the white matter, and 18 (3.4%) were in the deep nucleus. Of the 525 lesions, 157 (29.9%) in 48 patients were disappeared over time. There were significantly more disappearing lesions in the white matter (125) compared with the other territories (the cortex 26 and the deep nucleus 6) (p < 0.001). Ninety-nine lesions (63.1%) disappeared within 1 month after the FD treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Some of new SWI lesions after FD treatments, especially in the white matter, disappeared. These behaviors were different from those of conventional microbleeds.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Little is known about changes over time for SWI lesions newly observed following endovascular surgery. This study was aimed to introduce disappearance of postoperative new SWI lesions after flow diverter (FD) treatment for cerebral aneurysms with serial MRI scans. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective observational study, patients who underwent FD treatment for cerebral aneurysms between December 2017 and June 2024 were analyzed.

title: AMOTL2: A key regulator of mechanotransduction in development, vascular disease and cancer.
abstract: Mechanical forces play a fundamental role in regulating cell behavior during development, tissue homeostasis, and disease. The angiomotin family protein AmotL2 has emerged as a central integrator of mechanotransduction, linking cell-cell adhesion, cytoskeletal tension, and nuclear architecture to transcriptional control. Through its ability to connect cadherin-based junctions to radial actin filaments and the nuclear lamina, AmotL2 establishes a continuous mechanical axis that enables cells to sense and respond to extracellular forces. This function is essential for epithelial organization, vascular morphogenesis, and endothelial responses to shear stress, in part through regulation of Hippo pathway effectors such as YAP and TAZ. Dysregulation of AmotL2 contributes to pathological states, including abdominal aortic aneurysm, where reduced AmotL2 impairs endothelial mechanotransduction, and cancer, where induction of the p60AmotL2 isoform disrupts polarity, alters nuclear mechanics, and promotes invasive behavior. Emerging evidence further suggests that AmotL2 regulates transcription through direct effects on nuclear structure and chromatin accessibility, positioning it as a key regulator of force-dependent gene expression. In this review, we summarize the structural and mechanistic basis of AmotL2 function and discuss its roles in development, vascular biology, and cancer, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target in diseases driven by altered mechanotransduction.

title: The atherosclerotic cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic burden in the Asia-Pacific, 1990-2050: A global burden of disease 2023 analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, with the Asia-Pacific region bearing over half of this burden. The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised.

METHODS: Using the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we examined mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of CKLM diseases across 39 Asia-Pacific countries from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. The CKLM burden was organized into metabolic antecedents (comprising CKD, MASLD, T2DM and obesity) and downstream atherosclerotic CVD (comprising ischemic heart disease, stroke, aortic aneurysm, and peripheral artery disease).

FINDINGS: In 2023, the Asia-Pacific recorded 286.9 million CKLM-related DALYs (53.2% of global burden), with an age-standardised DALY rate of 6390.9 per 100,000 population. From 1990 to 2023, crude DALYs rose by 78.7%, outpacing the global trends (61.1%), while age-standardised DALYs fell by 25.0% - driven by improvements in atherosclerotic CVD (-35.2%) but counterbalanced by a 20.4% rise in metabolic antecedents. By 2050, age-standardised DALY rates are projected to show a 7.0% point-estimate increase regionally against an estimated 14.9% global decline, with metabolic antecedents likely to expand from 29.9% to 36.2% of the total burden between 2026 and 2050. Intraregional disparities exist across sociodemographic strata, subregions, and age-sex categories. Risk-deleted analyses identify high systolic blood pressure, high fasting plasma glucose, and dietary risks as the highest-yield modifiable targets.

INTERPRETATION: The worsening Asia-Pacific CKLM trajectory is decoupling from improving global trends, driven by a compositional shift from atherosclerotic CVD toward upstream metabolic antecedents. Integrated interventions addressing multiple key modifiable risks are needed.

The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised.

title: Brain-computer interfaces for traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury: Lesion-pattern matching, functional restoration, and clinical translation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment.

MAIN BODY: In SCI, motor intention and cortical activity may remain accessible despite disruption of descending pathways, supporting motor-intention decoding, brain-controlled functional electrical stimulation, neuroprosthetic control, and brain-spine interfaces. In TBI, diffuse and heterogeneous network dysfunction shifts the clinical emphasis toward detection of covert consciousness, assisted communication, neurofeedback, and multimodal rehabilitation. We compare non-invasive, endovascular, electrocorticographic, and intracortical recording approaches; summarize evoked-response, motor-imagery, and continuous decoding paradigms; and distinguish functional substitution from closed-loop restoration of an individual's own movements. Recent invasive systems have supported the restoration of grasping, standing, and walking in selected individuals with SCI, whereas evidence in TBI remains concentrated on brain-state assessment and low-bandwidth communication.

CONCLUSION: Clinical translation will require careful candidate selection, stable long-term recordings, effective bidirectional feedback, clinically meaningful real-world outcomes, ethical oversight, and sustained technical support. Disease-specific translational pathways, rather than a universal BCI model, are likely to provide the most practical route to routine clinical use after central nervous system injury.

However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. title: Sex-specific differences in patient-prosthesis mismatch following valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: Female sex is associated with increased rates of mortality and readmission following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and is a risk factor for patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM). Valve-in-valve (ViV) TAVI for treatment of degenerated bioprosthetic valves has a greater risk of PPM. We sought to determine if sex-specific differences exist in rates of PPM following ViV-TAVI. This retrospective study analyzed 77 patients who underwent ViV-TAVI at Kettering Health from 2015 to 2021, evaluating PPM incidence and bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) utilization. Indexed effective orifice area following ViV-TAVI was compared between females and males using an unpaired t test. Fisher exact test assessed the association between BVF and PPM for the overall cohort and within each sex. Statistical analyses were performed using R software. Males represented 57% of patients (body mass index = 28.8 kg/m2), while females comprised 43% (body mass index = 29.1 kg/m2). There was no significant difference in average indexed effective orifice area between females and males (P = .370). BVF rates were similar between sexes (33.3% in females; 29.6% in males), with an overall reduction in PPM (P = .028) and in females (P = .029). Cramér's V showed a moderate association between BVF and PPM in the overall cohort (0.305) and females (0.475), with a weaker association in males (0.183). Similar rates of PPM between sexes suggest that appropriate patient selection and valve sizing are crucial in PPM prevention. The significant reduction of PPM with BVF in females calls for further research into sex-specific outcomes and optimization of ViV-TAVI results.

title: Repeated nasal and gingival bleeding caused by high-flow maxillary arteriovenous malformation: A case report.
abstract:
RATIONALE: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are congenital vascular anomalies characterized by abnormal direct connections between arteries and veins due to arrested embryonic development. Although rare, maxillary AVMs may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage. The association of epistaxis with maxillary AVMs has been relatively underemphasized in the literature.

PATIENT CONCERNS: We report the case of a 21-year-old female presenting with recurrent, profuse left-sided nasal and gingival bleeding.

DIAGNOSES: Clinical evaluation, computed tomography angiography, and digital subtraction angiography were performed for diagnosis.

INTERVENTIONS: Endovascular embolization was performed as the primary treatment, with staged embolization treatment and a total follow-up of 14 months.

OUTCOMES: A high-flow maxillary AVM was confirmed. The initial embolization successfully controlled the hemorrhage. At the 8-month follow-up after the initial embolization, residual lesions were detected and treated with a second embolization. At the 6-month follow-up after the second embolization, no recurrent bleeding was observed.

LESSONS: Maxillary AVMs may present with both gingival bleeding and epistaxis and can easily mimic common dental conditions. Early recognition and timely endovascular intervention are essential to prevent life-threatening hemorrhage.

Although rare, maxillary AVMs may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage. The association of epistaxis with maxillary AVMs has been relatively underemphasized in the literature.

title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes.

RESULTS: Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially.

CONCLUSIONS: In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.

Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

title: Comparative evaluation of otolith function using vestibular evoked myogenic potentials and rotational chair testing.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Correspondence between off-vertical axis rotation (OVAR) responses and vestibular evoked myogenic potentials (VEMPs) remains unclear.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To relate VEMP findings to the gain difference between OVAR and earth-vertical axis rotation (EVAR).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We prospectively studied 11 VEMP-normal adults and 12 patients with abnormal cervical and/or ocular VEMPs (cVEMP/oVEMP). EVAR and OVAR were sinusoidal at 0.16 Hz. Wilcoxon rank-sum tests compared groups; exploratory Spearman analyses pooled healthy participants with corresponding VEMP-abnormal patients. P values and confidence intervals were unadjusted for multiplicity.

RESULTS: EVAR and OVAR gains did not differ significantly. Median gain differences were 0.308 in healthy participants and 0.109 in patients (p = 0.0489; Cliff's δ = 0.485, 95% CI 0.030-0.848). Compared with healthy participants, the difference was lower in the oVEMP-abnormal subgroup (n = 10; p = 0.0346), but not significantly different in the cVEMP-abnormal subgroup (n = 6; p = 0.1317). Correlations with absolute asymmetry ratios were ρ = -0.108 for cVEMP (n = 17; p = 0.6806) and ρ = -0.485 for oVEMP (n = 21; p = 0.0275).

CONCLUSIONS AND SIGNIFICANCE: Results suggest preliminary associations with oVEMP findings, without establishing utricular specificity. Larger cohorts with comparable age and sex distributions are needed.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We prospectively studied 11 VEMP-normal adults and 12 patients with abnormal cervical and/or ocular VEMPs (cVEMP/oVEMP).

title: Comparison of conventional logistic, random forest, and random forest-assisted models for 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model. The three models were compared in 251 patients with complete Model C predictors using 20 repeats of stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Mean AUCs (SD) were 0.9361 (0.0045), 0.8843 (0.0095), and 0.9301 (0.0089) for Models A, B, and C; corresponding Brier scores were 0.0886 (0.0033), 0.1246 (0.0026), and 0.0933 (0.0060). Model A showed slightly better average cross-validated discrimination and prediction error than Model C, whereas Model C performed better than Model B.

CONCLUSIONS: Random forest-assisted modeling did not improve cross-validated predictive performance over the simpler logistic model. External validation is required before clinical implementation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model.

title: Macroscopic evidence of regression of sinus dilatation inside the Florida sleeve.
abstract: The Florida sleeve procedure is a valve-sparing technique for aortic root aneurysms. Because redo surgeries are rare, macroscopic evidence of how the native aorta adapts inside the graft has never been reported. We report two reoperative cases performed for recurrent aortic regurgitation and infective endocarditis 12 and 14 months, respectively, after the initial Florida sleeve procedure. Intraoperatively, the previously folded, aneurysmal native aortic walls had neatly regressed and tightly adhered to the graft's inner surface, obliterating any potential dead space. These cases provide the first macroscopic evidence of true biological reverse remodeling inside the Florida sleeve.

title: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic clustering capture distinct clinically relevant aspects of carotid atherosclerosis.
abstract:
AIMS: Patients with carotid atherosclerosis exhibit substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation, plaque characteristics, and future cardiovascular risk, which do not always align. Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 1075 patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with matched clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data. Unsupervised clustering was applied separately to each data modality, and resulting clusters were evaluated for overlap and association with current symptom status and 3-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Clusters derived from different modalities showed limited overlap, but distinct associations with clinical outcomes. Clinical clusters were most strongly associated with 3-year MACE, whereas histological and transcriptomic clusters were more closely related to current cerebrovascular symptoms. Transcriptomic clusters further delineated molecular pathways and plaque biology. Integration of modalities provided modest improvement in outcome stratification, indicating that these data types capture complementary rather than redundant information.

CONCLUSION: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data capture distinct but complementary aspects of carotid atherosclerosis, reflecting systemic cardiovascular risk, local plaque phenotype, and underlying biology, with differing relevance to current cerebrovascular symptoms and future cardiovascular risk. The choice of data modality should therefore be guided by the intended clinical or biological question, rather than assuming a single approach can capture the full disease spectrum.

Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk.

title: Embolic stroke and breakthrough thrombosis on direct oral anticoagulants in Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a characteristic cardiac manifestation of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), but its presentation and management in the era of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are poorly characterised. We describe a 37-year-old man with obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and recurrent unprovoked deep vein thrombosis who developed multiple embolic strokes while taking rivaroxaban. Transoesophageal echocardiography showed a sessile aortic valve mass; repeated blood cultures and 18F-FDG PET-CT were negative, and lupus anticoagulant was the only antiphospholipid antibody detected (probable APS). He was switched to low-molecular-weight heparin and acenocoumarol and the mass was excised; histology showed an organised fibrinous thrombotic vegetation, although papillary fibroelastoma could not be fully excluded. Following the CABARET recommendations, we searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and DOAJ for reports published between January 2020 and September 2026 and included 62 case reports/series (63 patients) and four cohort studies. Median age was 40 years (range 19-78); 22/60 patients (37%) were men; 34/63 (54%) had primary APS and 6 (10%) catastrophic APS. When reported, the antibody profile was triple-positive in 22/39 (56%) and lupus-anticoagulant-only in 4/39 (10%). The mitral valve was involved in 41/62 (66%), the aortic in 19/62 (31%) and the tricuspid in 7/62 (11%). Ischaemic stroke occurred in 29/63 (46%) and heart failure or severe valve dysfunction in 31/63 (49%). Of 16 patients anticoagulated at diagnosis, 10 (63%) were receiving a DOAC. Valve intervention was performed in 35/63 (56%) and 4/63 (6%) died. LSE should be sought in patients with APS who have embolic events, particularly while on DOACs; the evidence remains observational.

Transoesophageal echocardiography showed a sessile aortic valve mass; repeated blood cultures and 18F-FDG PET-CT were negative, and lupus anticoagulant was the only antiphospholipid antibody detected (probable APS).

title: Pantothenate Metabolic Alterations in PROS1 Mutation Carriers and the Antithrombotic Effects of Pantethine.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1-mutation patients through integrated multi-omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models.

METHODS: Serum metabolomics, siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed.

RESULTS: Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM-1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL-1β-induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM-1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine-conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co-incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation-driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic-endothelial-platelet mode of interaction.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic-endothelial-platelet association in protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1-deficient in vivo models.

However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1-mutation patients through integrated multi-omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy for a Patient with Antithrombin Deficiency and Intraprocedural Thrombus Formation.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Antithrombin (AT) deficiency is a rare type of inherited thrombophilia that commonly increases the risk of venous thromboembolism. However, its association with ischemic stroke remains unclear. Herein, we report a case of intraprocedural thrombus formation during mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in a patient with known AT deficiency.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 49-year-old male patient presented with left hemiparesis and conjugate deviation. He had a history of embolic stroke and previously documented AT deficiency. Imaging revealed right middle cerebral artery M1 occlusion, and intravenous thrombolysis followed by MT was performed. During the procedure, extensive thrombus formation developed in the internal carotid artery, resulting in temporary occlusion. Additional heparinization and repeated thrombectomy were required to restore blood flow. Partial reperfusion was achieved, and the procedure was completed with expanded Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia grade 2a recanalization. Postoperatively, AT concentrate, heparin, and warfarin were administered. The patient regained his premorbid activities of daily living, and recurrent ischemic stroke was not observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: AT deficiency may have been one of several factors contributing not only to embolic stroke but also to intraprocedural thrombotic instability during MT. In patients with known AT deficiency, thrombus formation may be promoted by inadequate anticoagulation and procedural factors, such as device manipulation and prolonged intervention. Cautious perioperative assessment of AT activity, consideration of AT concentrate supplementation, and appropriate anticoagulation monitoring may be important for preventing secondary thrombus formation during reperfusion therapy.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Antithrombin (AT) deficiency is a rare type of inherited thrombophilia that commonly increases the risk of venous thromboembolism. However, its association with ischemic stroke remains unclear. Herein, we report a case of intraprocedural thrombus formation during mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in a patient with known AT deficiency.

title: Mobilizing the Critically Ill: The Central Role of Nurses in Preventing ICU Complications and Enhancing Recovery.
abstract: The intensive care unit (ICU) is a high-acuity environment where patients with severe illness receive comprehensive care. Immobility is common among patients with critical disease states and contributes to muscle atrophy, development of pressure ulcers, increased risk of thromboembolic events, and acute respiratory insufficiency. Similarly, delirium is another prevalent complication that further contributes to prolonged ICU stays, increased mortality, and long-term cognitive impairments. Reduced mobility, delirium, and other sequelae of critical illness pose significant challenges to patient recovery and often result in poor long-term outcomes. Early mobility has been shown to improve long-term outcomes of critically ill patients by reducing their length of hospital and ICU stay, reducing ICU-acquired weakness, improving functional outcomes, and improving long-term cognitive function. Given their direct patient contact, nurses are uniquely positioned to serve as the primary facilitators of patient mobility in the ICU. As frontline caregivers, nurses can assess a patient's readiness for mobility, monitor vital signs during activity, and provide hands-on support for safe mobilization. They are instrumental in coordinating interdisciplinary efforts, ensuring effective communication among health care team members, and advocating patient-centered mobility goals. Additionally, nurses contribute to delirium prevention and management by closely monitoring cognitive changes, facilitating family engagement, and promoting nonpharmacological interventions such as sleep hygiene and cognitive stimulation. Through their continuous presence and compassionate care, nurses not only address the physical aspects of recovery but also provide emotional support to patients and families, significantly enhancing psychological well-being in the ICU. By leveraging their clinical expertise and patient advocacy skills, nurses are essential in fostering a culture of mobility and comprehensive care in the ICU, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes and quality of life for critical illness survivors.

Immobility is common among patients with critical disease states and contributes to muscle atrophy, development of pressure ulcers, increased risk of thromboembolic events, and acute respiratory insufficiency. Similarly, delirium is another prevalent complication that further contributes to prolonged ICU stays, increased mortality, and long-term cognitive impairments.
