title: Why standardised performance-based ultrasound mastery training is needed now: a narrative review.
abstract: Difficult intravenous access is common in acute and emergency care and contributes to repeated peripheral intravenous cannulation attempts, delayed therapy and escalation to more invasive devices. Ultrasound-guided peripheral cannula placement is widely recommended as an escalation strategy, yet ultrasound education remains inconsistent across settings. Systematic reviews show heterogeneity in time spent in training, curricula, assessment methods, supervision, validation and competency pathways, while failure rates for peripheral intravenous catheters remain high. Performance-based mastery learning, particularly simulation-based mastery learning, addresses this gap by defining competence using a minimum passing standard score, structured checklists, deliberate practice and retesting until proficiency is demonstrated. Evidence supports the success of simulation-based mastery learning for ultrasound-guided vascular access, including improved performance, confidence and reduced use of midline devices in difficult intravenous access populations. This article outlines a standardised mastery curriculum and audit framework aligned with Association for Vascular Access clinical practice guidelines and Infusion Nurses Society standards and seal of approval.

title: Teaching the bigger picture - student perceptions on interprofessional teaching on the patient journey in vascular surgery.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ensuring drug safety is critical in comorbid vascular surgery patients and can be supported by interprofessional collaboration with clinical pharmacists. Thus, this project aimed to create an interprofessional seminar for medical students using real-life vascular surgery cases, highlighting medication risks and the value of interprofessional collaboration during the cross-sectoral medication process.

METHODS: A six-step model (Kern cycle) was used to develop a seminar integrating vascular surgery cases with the medication process from admission to discharge. The implementation was guided by a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT)-analysis to identify challenges and opportunities. After piloting the seminar, self-reported evaluation data were used to describe students' perception of acceptance, perceived learning, and practical relevance. A 14-item questionnaire and qualitative content analysis of free-text responses were used to analyze students' perceptions on the course.

RESULTS: Learning objectives included identifying medication risks, applying literature to solve drug-related problems, and developing interprofessional strategies to improve medication safety. The seminar, led by vascular surgeons and clinical pharmacists, employed various didactic methods (e.g., inverted classroom, small group learning). The seminar was evaluated by 142 of 240 students involved in the pilot phase (response rate 59.1%). Respondents rated the practical relevance, interprofessional approach, and interactive learning methods positively and reported perceived learning progress. The seminar is now part of the vascular surgery curriculum.

CONCLUSIONS: The seminar provides a practical framework for integrating cross-sectoral medication management into medical education. By linking clinical practice with collaborative patient care, it offers an opportunity for enhancing students' understanding of collaborative patient care and drug safety in the surgical patient journey. The seminar was successfully integrated into the vascular surgery curriculum and was positively perceived by participating students. This model may be adaptable to other medical specialties to promote interprofessional teaching in the medical curriculum.

Thus, this project aimed to create an interprofessional seminar for medical students using real-life vascular surgery cases, highlighting medication risks and the value of interprofessional collaboration during the cross-sectoral medication process. title: Dual Delayed Vascular Complications Following Total Hip Arthroplasty (Distal Arterial Thrombosis and Subsequent External Iliac Artery Pseudoaneurysm).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular injury following total hip arthroplasty (THA) is uncommon; however, it potentially threatens limb viability. Misplaced acetabular screws may damage or irritate the external iliac or common femoral arteries, leading to thrombosis or a pseudoaneurysm weeks to months after surgery. Prompt identification and imaging are crucial for facilitating timely intervention.

CASE PRESENTATION: The patient was a 65-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis who underwent right THA. Six months later, she developed severe ischemia in her right leg, indicated by a cold, pale foot and absent pedal pulses. Duplex ultrasonography revealed thrombosis in the distal popliteal and tibial arteries; CT angiography showed an acetabular screw in proximity to the lateral wall of the external iliac artery and a short-segment mural thrombus. A collaborative team performed limb thrombectomy and the extraction of the affected screws, resulting in rapid reperfusion. Serial postoperative imaging demonstrated a growing pseudoaneurysm of the external iliac artery. Endovascular exclusion with a balloon-expandable covered stent was performed, restoring perfusion. She completed dual antiplatelet therapy and remained asymptomatic, with sustained patency and improvement in hip function compared with preoperative status at late follow-up.

DISCUSSION: This dual, delayed presentation, consisting of distal arterial thrombosis followed by a subsequent external iliac artery pseudoaneurysm, is rare. The case underscores the importance of adherence to safe acetabular screw trajectories, a low threshold for vascular imaging (duplex or CTA), and coordinated orthopedic and vascular management. Covered stent grafting provides a minimally invasive option when anatomy and stability permit, while allowing staged or concurrent orthopedic revision.

CONCLUSION: New limb ischemia or groin symptoms following THA necessitate prompt vascular imaging to rule out screw-related damage.

Misplaced acetabular screws may damage or irritate the external iliac or common femoral arteries, leading to thrombosis or a pseudoaneurysm weeks to months after surgery. Prompt identification and imaging are crucial for facilitating timely intervention.

title: Public real-world data decision thresholds for hybrid vascular control in complex robot-assisted partial nephrectomy.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Hybrid endovascular balloon occlusion has been described during complex robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), but no reproducible public-data phenotype or access-risk-adjusted threshold has been validated. The selected public evidence was audited, and a hypothesis was formulated for future testing.

METHODS: A public-data quantitative evidence synthesis was combined with a conceptual decision model. ​Six selected reports of hybrid partial nephrectomy were rechecked. Possible patient overlap and incomplete reporting meant that the reported procedures could not be treated as a cohort of independent patients. A 20-patient branch-occlusion study provided a numerical illustration using Jeffreys-prior beta-binomial models and an additive expected-loss equation. KiTS23, C4KC-KiTS, TCGA-KIRC and MAUDE were mapped for possible future research; their individual patient or event records were not analysed.​ RESULTS: The illustrative cohort reported no conversion, one escalation from branch to main-artery balloon occlusion and one minor puncture-site bruise. The posterior median conversion probability was 1.1% (95% credible interval [CrI] < 0.1-11.7%). For each outcome with one reported event, the posterior median probability was 5.8% (95% CrI 0.5-21.1%). The median loss-equivalence boundary increased from 8.2% to 37.4% when the hypothetical access-harm weight increased from one to six. These values are not clinical thresholds. No anatomical model was trained or validated.

CONCLUSION: Hybrid vascular control in complex RAPN is best framed as a hypothesis for future testing, not as a patient-selection rule. Prospective outcome-labelled data and comparative clinical evaluation are required before performance, safety or utility can be assessed.

title: Saint-Bonnet classification performance for the critical limb threatening ischemia diagnosis with duplex ultrasonography.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critical limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) is the most advanced stage of lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) and is associated with an increased risk of amputation and mortality. The main means for CLTI diagnosis is the use of toe pressure (TP). Duplex ultrasonography (DUS) flow analysis by using the Saint-Bonnet classification could assess arterial impairment, but its relationship with CLTI defined by TP has not been evaluated. The first objective was to assess the relationship between Saint-Bonnet classification at ankle and hemodynamic CLTI, defined by TP≤30mmHg, and its diagnostic performance. The second objective was to study the correlation between systolic rise time and TP.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients undergoing lower-limb arterial DUS and TP at the University Hospital Center of Guadeloupe between June 2022 and November 2023. Statistical analyses included univariate and multivariable analyses, diagnostic performance assessment and Pearson correlation.

RESULTS: One hundred and fifty-three patients were included (276 lower limbs). CLTI was significantly associated with 0 and E categories of Saint Bonnet in univariate (P<0.001) and multivariable analysis (P<0.001), with 94% specificity and 65% positive predictive value. N, A or B categories appeared to rule out CLTI, with a 100% negative predictive value in a population at high risk of mediacalcosis. No significant correlation was found between Systolic rise time and toe pressure (P=0.0773).

CONCLUSION: Saint Bonnet Classification may help in the diagnosis of CLTI, but these findings need confirmation in a larger prospective diagnostic and prognostic study.

The main means for CLTI diagnosis is the use of toe pressure (TP). title: ASFNR Clinical State-of-Practice in Neuroimaging of Minor Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor ischemic stroke (MIS) with anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO) is a distinct stroke subtype in which mild neurological deficits may mask a substantial volume of threatened but salvageable brain tissue. Despite a baseline NIHSS≤5, nearly one-third of patients experience poor functional outcomes, often due to early neurological deterioration (END).

CURRENT EVIDENCE AND ONGOING TRIALS: Patients with LVO-MIS were markedly underrepresented in landmark thrombectomy trials, resulting in limited evidence to guide treatment. Retrospective studies have identified imaging biomarkers of END, including proximal occlusion, clot length, collateral status, and perfusion mismatch, but the benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains uncertain. Ongoing randomized controlled trials, including STEP and MOSTE, are expected to define the role of EVT and imaging-based patient selection in this population.

PURPOSE: To summarize the current state of neuroimaging in anterior circulation LVO-MIS and provide a practical imaging workflow and reporting checklist for diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment selection.

KEY POINTS: CTA remains the primary modality for LVO detection and collateral assessment, while CT and MR perfusion identify salvageable tissue and predict END beyond baseline NIHSS. MRI further refines infarct core, perfusion deficit, and thrombus characterization. Current AI-based LVO detection tools improve stroke triage but require careful human oversight because proximal M2 and non-terminus ICA occlusions may be missed.

CONCLUSION: Pending results from ongoing trials, tissue-based imaging with CTA, CT perfusion, and MR perfusion can complement clinical assessment to improve risk stratification and individualized treatment decisions. Advances in quantitative imaging and artificial intelligence are expected to further enable precision imaging-guided management of LVO-MIS.

title: A bridge too far? Is there a positive benefit/risk balance of distal embolic penetration in MMA embolization for cSDHs?
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Middle meningeal artery embolization for chronic subdural hematoma is rapidly expanding in practice, with growing interest in techniques that maximize distal penetration of liquid embolic agents within the meningeal branches to reach the neovascularized hematoma membrane. The clinical significance of distal embolic penetration beyond its radiographic associations has not been fully established, and reports of rare complications associated with more aggressive technique raise safety considerations. This State of Practice examines evidence for distal embolic penetration's clinical benefits, presents a case illustrating a risk associated with this approach, and outlines the evidence needed to determine its benefit/risk balance.

METHODS: The authors conducted a narrative review of randomized trials, retrospective studies, and case-based literature on middle meningeal artery embolization, comparing reported embolic penetration/grading frameworks and evidence for their association with radiographic and clinical outcomes, as well as evidence for proximal coil embolization as an alternative approach. We also report a case of inadvertent embolization through an occult middle meningeal artery anastomosis to illustrate a risk of distal embolic penetration.

KEY MESSAGE: As practice of middle meningeal artery embolization expands, evidence that maximizing distal liquid embolic penetration improves clinical outcomes beyond radiographic resolution remains limited. This approach may involve rare complications from occult vascular anastomoses not readily identified on preprocedural imaging, although their frequency is unknown. We urge operators to recognize that an unremarkable preprocedural angiogram may not exclude the dangerous anastomoses. Prospective multicenter studies involving both interventional neuroradiologists and endovascular neurosurgeons are needed to correlate 3D embolic distribution patterns with clinical outcomes, alongside randomized trials comparing distal and proximal embolization approaches using clinically meaningful endpoints.

title: Clinical characteristics associated with elevated serum adiponectin in patients with lower extremity artery disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Elevated circulating adiponectin has been associated with poor prognosis in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD). However, the clinical characteristics underlying elevated adiponectin in patients with LEAD remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify the clinical and computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition characteristics associated with elevated serum adiponectin and to evaluate the association between serum adiponectin and 2-year overall survival in patients with LEAD.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included 80 patients with LEAD who underwent lower extremity revascularization between May 2021 and December 2023. Serum adiponectin levels were measured at the time of revascularization. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, and CT-derived body composition parameters were compared between patients with high and low serum adiponectin levels, classified according to the median value. 2-year overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. The association between serum adiponectin and 2-year mortality was also evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression adjusted for age. Factors associated with serum adiponectin were assessed using univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among the 80 patients, 40 were classified into the high adiponectin group and 40 into the low adiponectin group. Patients with high adiponectin were significantly older and had lower body mass index (BMI), visceral fat area (VFA), subcutaneous fat area (SFA), and triglyceride levels than those with low adiponectin. 2-year overall survival was significantly lower in the high adiponectin group than in the low adiponectin group (78.6% vs 94.8%, p = .0330). After adjustment for age, high serum adiponectin remained significantly associated with 2-year mortality (HR = 2.22, 95% CI, 1.08 to 5.83, p = .0278). In multivariable linear regression analysis, VFA remained independently and inversely associated with serum adiponectin after adjustment for age, BMI, skeletal muscle area, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (β = -0.0126 per 10 cm2 increase, 95% CI, -0.0221 to -0.0032, p = .0096).

CONCLUSION: Elevated serum adiponectin was associated with poor 2-year survival in patients with LEAD. Reduced CT-derived VFA was independently associated with elevated serum adiponectin even after adjustment for BMI and other clinical factors. These findings suggest that elevated adiponectin may characterize a LEAD phenotype with reduced visceral adiposity and adverse prognosis.

title: Xa Inhibitors Are Associated with an Increased Risk of Manipulation after Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Compared to Aspirin in a Contemporary Cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aspirin is routinely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis following total knee arthroplasty (TKA), though some patients may require more aggressive chemoprophylaxis, now often with Xa inhibitors. There is concern Xa inhibitors may increase bleeding, leading to swelling and stiffness, which can lead to manipulation under anesthesia (MUA). This study compared rates of MUA following primary TKA for patients receiving Xa inhibitors versus aspirin and between Xa inhibitors in a contemporary cohort.

METHODS: A database identified 435,789 patients undergoing unilateral primary TKA from 2021 to 2023. During the perioperative window (30 days preoperatively to 3 days postoperatively), 32,778 (7.5%) received rivaroxaban, 53,504 (12.3%) apixaban, and 349,507 (80.2%) aspirin. The incidence of MUA was determined using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code 27570 within 90 days following TKA. Univariable associations between chemoprophylaxis and MUA were assessed using Chi-square tests. Multivariable associations adjusted for patient demographics, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, and body mass index were assessed using logistic regression with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) reported.

RESULTS: Overall, 13,142 (3.0%) underwent MUA, and this was more common in patients receiving Xa inhibitors versus aspirin (3.9 versus 2.8%, P < 0.001). After adjusting for patient characteristics, Xa inhibitors were associated with higher odds of MUA (OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.54 to 1.67). In univariable analysis, the rate of MUA was similar between rivaroxaban and apixaban (3.7 versus 3.9%, P = 0.11), though after adjusting for patient characteristics, rivaroxaban was associated with lower odds of MUA compared with apixaban (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.83 to 0.95).

CONCLUSION: Factor Xa inhibitors are associated with a significantly increased risk of MUA within 90 days of primary TKA compared to aspirin in a contemporary cohort. Unadjusted MUA rates were similar between rivaroxaban and apixaban. Adjusted odds were lower with rivaroxaban.

This study compared rates of MUA following primary TKA for patients receiving Xa inhibitors versus aspirin and between Xa inhibitors in a contemporary cohort.

title: Comparative Early Outcomes of Total Transfemoral vs. Upper Extremity Access for Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) Implantation.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.

METHODS: A retrospective review of consecutive patients undergoing TAMBE implantation at a single centre between April 2020 and January 2026 was performed. Patients were stratified by access strategy into TFA and UEA. The primary outcomes were thirty day mortality and major adverse events (MAEs).

RESULTS: One hundred patients underwent TAMBE implantation during the study period, of whom 32 underwent TFA and 68 UEA. The majority of aneurysms treated were thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (61%), and 45% of patients had a prior endovascular intervention with no significant difference between groups (all p > .050). Mean operative time (232.8 ± 92.4 minutes vs. 250.8 ± 77.3 minutes; p = .18) and fluoroscopy time (59.2 ± 28.4 minutes vs. 48.3 ± 21.6 minutes; p = .066) were not statistically different between groups. Technical success was 91% in the TFA group compared with 99% in the UEA group (p = .095). Thirty day mortality (3% vs. 3%; p = 1.0) and MAEs (16% vs. 13%; p = .76) were not statistically different between TFA and UEA groups. Spinal cord ischaemia rates were 16% for the TFA group and 7% for the UEA group (p = .16), with most cases mild and resolved by discharge (80%). No stroke events occurred in either group. At 6 months, overall branch patency was 92% (78 of 85 branches from 22 patients), including 83% (15 of 18 branches from five patients) in the TFA group and 94% (63 of 67 branches from 17 patients) in the UEA group (p = .16).

CONCLUSION: In this single centre experience, total transfemoral TAMBE implantation was performed in selected patients, and no statistically significant differences were detected in thirty day mortality, MAEs, and technical success between access strategies. Larger studies are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist.

The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.

title: Evaluating an Estimated Blood Volume-Based Enoxaparin Dosing Protocol in Emergency General Surgery Patients.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Low antifactor Xa (AFXa) levels are associated with venous thromboembolism (VTE), and prior research has shown that emergency general surgery (EGS) patients may be underdosed with enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis. The objective of this study was to describe our experience with utilizing an estimated blood volume (EBV)-based enoxaparin dosing protocol in EGS patients.

METHODS: This was a prospective cohort study of adult EGS patients. Patients eligible for VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin were dosed using an EBV-based protocol. The primary outcome was peak AFXa level obtained 2.5-6 h after the third dose of enoxaparin. The goal AFXa range was 0.2-0.4 IU/mL. Bleeding complications and in-hospital VTE events were assessed.

RESULTS: There were 121 patients in total, and 62% (n = 75) required an operation. The initial proportion of in-range AFXa levels was 61% (n = 74), and there were no differences between those in the operative versus nonoperative groups (operative in-range: 64%, n = 48, nonoperative: 57%, n = 26, P = 0.17). Bleeding complications occurred in 4.96% of patients, all of which were in the operative group. There were no VTE events.

CONCLUSIONS: An EBV-based enoxaparin dosing protocol led to over half of EGS patients having in-range AFXa levels, and there were no differences between those who required an operation and those who did not. A major barrier to protocol implementation included appropriate timing of lab collection. Further research is needed to directly compare EBV-based protocols to other dosing protocols in EGS patients to improve VTE prophylaxis protocols.

The objective of this study was to describe our experience with utilizing an estimated blood volume (EBV)-based enoxaparin dosing protocol in EGS patients. METHODS: This was a prospective cohort study of adult EGS patients.

title: Clinical evaluation of a novel artificial intelligence-based image processing algorithm for two-dimensional angiography.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical performance of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-based image processing algorithm for two-dimensional angiographic imaging compared with its predecessor across multiple imaging modes, anatomic regions, and endovascular specialties.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, comparative, randomized, paired, and blinded multicenter reader study included anonymized images acquired during clinically indicated endovascular interventions at 11 institutions in the United States and Europe. A total of 553 image series from 182 patients representing 51 procedure types across interventional radiology, neurointervention, cardiology, and pediatric cardiology were processed using both the AI-based and predecessor image processing algorithms. Thirteen board-certified physicians independently evaluated paired images using five-point Likert scales for overall image quality, contrast of clinically relevant details, noise reduction, and confidence in assessing device and vessel details. The primary endpoint was non-inferiority of overall image quality. Secondary endpoints evaluated superiority across image quality metrics using a predefined hierarchical testing strategy.

RESULTS: The AI-based image processing algorithm demonstrated non-inferior overall image quality in 98.9% of all evaluations (95% confidence interval [CI], 98%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint across all imaging modes, anatomic regions, and predefined subgroups. Superiority of the AI-based algorithm was demonstrated for overall image quality, contrast of clinically relevant details, noise reduction, and confidence in assessing device and vessel details across fluoroscopy, roadmap, overlay reference, and native acquisition imaging. Overall image quality superiority was not demonstrated for digital subtraction angiography, likely reflecting the intrinsically higher signal-to-noise characteristics of these acquisitions. Inter-reader agreement analysis demonstrated identical ratings in 49.3% of evaluations, with 94.7% of paired ratings differing by no more than one Likert category.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter blinded reader study, AI-based image processing demonstrated non-inferior overall image quality compared with its predecessor across all evaluated imaging modes and patient subgroups, with superior performance for multiple image quality metrics in fluoroscopy, roadmap, overlay reference, and native acquisition imaging. These findings support the clinical utility of AI-based image processing for endovascular imaging and provide a foundation for future studies evaluating its impact on radiation dose and procedural outcomes.

title: Limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To compare early and long-term outcomes of limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection.

METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed to pool risk ratios for early binary outcomes and hazard ratios for long-term outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-five reports were included in the updated systematic review. After endpoint-specific adjudication of potentially overlapping institutional cohorts, the number of reports contributing to each pooled analysis varied by outcome. EAR was associated with a higher risk of early mortality (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.01-1.70) and re-exploration for bleeding (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45). No statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.96-1.20) or dialysis (RR 1.21, 95% CI 0.99-1.49). HR-based analyses showed no statistically significant association with overall survival (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.91-1.92) or distal aortic reintervention (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.07-13.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In retrospective observational comparisons, EAR was associated with higher early mortality and re-exploration for bleeding, whereas no statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke or dialysis. No statistically significant associations were detected for overall survival or distal aortic reintervention. These findings do not establish causal effects of repair extent and remain limited by confounding by indication.

METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis.

title: Effect of multivitamin-mineral supplementation on cardiovascular-related functional health status in older adults: secondary findings from the COSMOS randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Declines in cardiovascular-related functional health status are common with aging, yet the long-term effects of multivitamin-mineral (MVM) and cocoa extract (CE) supplementation on patient-reported outcomes remain unclear in older adults. This prespecified secondary analysis of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) examined whether daily MVM or CE influenced Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores in generally healthy older adults and those with pre-existing heart conditions. COSMOS was a 2 × 2 factorial, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 21,442 US adults (men ≥ 60, women ≥ 65 years) without major cardiovascular disease at baseline. All participants were included in intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses of physical ability score (PAS), symptom burden (SB), and clinical summary score (CSS), representing KCCQ outcomes over 3 years. Linear mixed-effects models estimated treatment effects, with prespecified subgroup analyses among participants with cardiac conditions. Among a total cohort of over 21,000 participants, those taking a daily MVM versus placebo had small but statistically significant improvements in SB (MD 0.44, 95% CI 0.13-0.74) and CSS (MD 0.33, 95% CI 0.09-0.57) (both P < 0.05), with no significant effect on PAS, compared to placebo. CE supplementation had no overall effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity in MVM effects according to carotid stenosis status, with year 3 ITT differences of 5.13 points for PAS and 4.95 points for CSS (P-interaction = 0.012 and 0.009, respectively). For CE, the primary ITT analysis provided limited evidence of subgroup benefit. This is the first large randomized clinical trial to evaluate the long-term effects of MVM and CE supplementation on KCCQ-assessed cardiovascular functional health in older adults. Our findings provide new evidence that daily MVM supplementation, but not CE, is associated with small improvements in cardiovascular-related functional health status among older adults, warranting further investigation. The trial was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02422745 ; unique identifier: NCT02422745.

title: Hospital Volume, Stroke Severity, and In-Hospital Mortality after Basilar Artery Thrombectomy in the United States.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hospital volume is associated with outcomes after anterior-circulation thrombectomy, but its relationship with mortality after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is uncertain. We examined trends, hospital volume, and the influence of coded stroke severity on mortality after BAO thrombectomy.

METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-2023. Adults with a principal ischemic stroke diagnosis and a basilar artery infarction code (ICD-10-CM I63.02, I63.12, I63.22) were included; the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) was derived from R29.7xx codes. Hospital volume was measured within each year as BAO-specific and all-stroke EVT volume. Analyses used survey-weighted regression, interrupted time series, and propensity matching with and without NIHSS.

RESULTS: Among 9,049 BAO admissions (weighted 45,245), 2,335 (25.8%) received EVT. EVT use rose from 16.4% to 32.0%, and EVT-recipient mortality declined from 33.3% to 27.2%, without a robust change at trial publication. Highest-volume centers treated more severe and more often transferred patients and had lower NIHSS-adjusted mortality (BAO-specific volume: odds ratio [OR] 0.76, 95% CI 0.56-1.02; all-stroke volume: OR 0.82, 0.61-1.10; sensitivity analyses 0.73-0.83), without a monotonic gradient. NIHSS adjustment attenuated the matched mortality OR for EVT from 2.46 (2.16-2.80) to 1.31 (1.12-1.53); by severity stratum, ORs ranged from 7.74 (NIHSS 0-4) to 0.80 (NIHSS 21-42).

CONCLUSION: US basilar thrombectomy use doubled across the trial era while in-hospital mortality declined gradually. Highest-volume centers had consistently but imprecisely lower severity-adjusted mortality. Coded NIHSS materially changes treatment associations and should be standard in administrative stroke research.

We examined trends, hospital volume, and the influence of coded stroke severity on mortality after BAO thrombectomy. METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-2023.

title: Economic burden of hospital-requiring infections and venous thromboembolism in the last year of life in advanced breast cancer: a complication-specific cost analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: End-of-life healthcare costs in advanced breast cancer (ABC) are substantial, yet the contribution of acute, life-threatening complications, hospital-requiring infections and venous thromboembolism (VTE), remains uncharacterised. We quantified adjusted complication-specific costs. Patient/material and methods: Population-based cohort study of 1,363 women who died with ABC in the Stockholm Region (2015-2023). Healthcare costs during the last 12 months of life were estimated using the Region Stockholm simulated cost (SIM) model and stratified by complication status, age group, and Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). Generalised linear models estimated the independent associations between hospital-requiring infections, VTE and total costs, adjusting sequentially for age, frailty risk, and systemic therapy.

RESULTS: Overall mean costs were 597 thousand SEK (tSEK; 95% CI: 578-616). Hospital-requiring infections occurred in 18% of patients and were independently associated with 29% higher costs after full adjustment (cost ratio 1.29, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.20-1.39). VTE occurred in 8% of patients, of whom 80% had pulmonary embolism; it was associated with higher costs unadjusted (1.16, p = 0.010) but not after adjustment for frailty risk (1.08, 95% CI: 0.97-1.21). Concomitant VTE (27 patients, 11% of those infected) gave costs similar to infection alone. High frailty risk showed the strongest independent association with cost in the infection model (cost ratio 1.54, 95% CI: 1.34-1.78).

INTERPRETATION: Hospital-requiring infections were independently associated with higher end-of-life costs in ABC; VTE was not, once frailty risk was adjusted for. These findings add a complication-specific dimension to frailty-based risk stratification and support targeted prevention in end-of-life care.

title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes.

METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change.

RESULTS: Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.

Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes. METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database.

title: A VAPG Incorporating Targeted Self-Assembling Peptides for Efficient VSMC Restoring and Imaging in Abdominal Aortic Models.
abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) dysfunction is closely associated with vascular remodeling during abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression, making VSMC repair a vital therapeutic strategy. Although peptides capable of VSMC recruitment have been reported, their application is severely limited by poor accumulation in AAA lesions because of rapid clearance following systemic administration. The enzyme-triggered self-assembling peptide strategy has emerged as a safe and effective approach to prolong local retention while enabling specific responsiveness. In this study, we identified ADAMTS4 and MMP-2 as highly expressed proteases in AAA lesions, serving as ideal targets for in situ retention. We developed a Targeted Responsive Assembly Peptide (TRAP) strategy by incorporating the VSMC-recruitment peptide VAPG, an ADAMTS4 recognition motif for AAA targeting, and an MMP-2-responsive cleavage motif that triggers self-assembly of the Fmoc-FF fragment. Following enzymatic activation, VAPG-containing fragments undergo self-assembly into hydrogels, significantly enhancing VSMC recruitment. The secondary structure transitioned from random coils to β-sheets upon MMP-2 cleavage. The assembled hydrogels exhibited moderate viscoelastic behavior, with stable elastic properties, favorable mechanical strength, and shear resistance. Moreover, PET/CT imaging revealed that 68Ga-labeled peptide enables non-invasive monitoring of peptide accumulation and retention at AAA sites. Ultimately, this TRAP strategy potentially serves as an efficient approach for AAA treatment through long-acting VSMC repair.

Although peptides capable of VSMC recruitment have been reported, their application is severely limited by poor accumulation in AAA lesions because of rapid clearance following systemic administration. The enzyme-triggered self-assembling peptide strategy has emerged as a safe and effective approach to prolong local retention while enabling specific responsiveness.

title: Cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in acromegaly-associated diabetes: a Swedish nationwide study.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Secondary diabetes mellitus occurs in 30% to 50% of patients with acromegaly despite a lean phenotype, whereas type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with adiposity.

OBJECTIVE: We compared mortality, morbidity, and treatment patterns between patients with acromegaly-associated diabetes (ACRO-DM) and T2DM.

DESIGN: Nationwide, retrospective, matched-cohort study in Sweden.

METHODS: The ACRO-DM group included patients with an acromegaly diagnosis in the Patient Register, with diabetes registered in the National Diabetes Register (NDR) or a dispensed glucose-lowering drug in the Prescribed Drug Register. Controls with T2DM from the NDR were matched 10:1 for sex, age, calendar year, and diabetes duration. We derived mortality and morbidity outcomes from the Death and Patient Registers.

RESULTS: We included 348 patients with ACRO-DM and 3480 with T2DM. Mean (SD) age was 60.3 (13.2) and 59.5 (15.6) years, whereas diabetes duration was 2.8 (5.8) and 3.0 (7.1) years in ACRO-DM and T2DM, respectively. Baseline cardiovascular morbidity was more common in ACRO-DM than T2DM group (61% vs 43%), including hypertension (48% vs 29%), heart failure (11% vs 5%), arrhythmia (13% vs 9%), and stroke (8% vs 5%).The hazard ratio (HR) for overall mortality was 1.18 (95% CI, 0.96-1.46) in ACRO-DM compared with T2DM group. The ACRO-DM group had a higher risk of cardiovascular morbidity (HR = 1.55; 95% CI, 1.24-1.94), with increased hazards for venous thromboembolism, specifically pulmonary, and arrhythmia, whereas cardiovascular mortality was not increased (HR = 1.12; 95% CI, 0.78-1.60).

CONCLUSION: The risk of cardiovascular morbidity was increased in patients with ACRO-DM compared to T2DM.

title: Mortality After Emergency versus Elective Ventral Hernia Repair: A Propensity-Matched ACHQC Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Outcomes of ventral hernia repair (VHR) differ substantially between elective and emergency settings. Prior population-based studies have demonstrated increased morbidity and mortality with emergency repair, but limited data exist from disease-specific hernia registries incorporating detailed anatomical and operative variables.

METHODS: Records from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative (ACHQC) registry spanning 2013 through 2023 were reviewed retrospectively. Adult patients undergoing VHR were identified. Emergency cases were paired with elective cases in a 1:2 ratio through propensity score matching built on demographics, comorbidities, and hernia characteristics. We judged the groups balanced when the standardized mean difference (SMD) for every covariate fell below 0.1. Death within 90 days was the primary endpoint. Length of stay (LOS), surgical site infection (SSI), and systemic complications were examined as secondary endpoints.

RESULTS: Among 36,788 patients, 965 (2.6%) underwent emergency repair. After matching, 955 emergency and 1,906 elective patients were analyzed with excellent covariate balance (SMD < 0.1). Within 90 days, 1.6% of emergency patients had died versus 0.3% of elective patients (P < .001). Emergency patients stayed a median of 4 days (interquartile range [IQR] 1-6), 4 times the 1 day (IQR 0-5) recorded for elective patients (P < .001). SSI developed in 9% of emergency and 6% of elective patients (P = .02), and surgical site occurrence requiring procedural intervention in 11% and 8%, respectively (P = .003). The emergency group also had more deep vein thrombosis (1% vs 0.2%, P < .001), postoperative respiratory failure (1% vs 0.4%, P = .01), and septic shock (0.4% vs 0.1%, P = .03).

CONCLUSION: In this registry-based propensity-matched analysis, 90-day mortality and postoperative morbidity were both higher after emergency than after elective VHR. These findings highlight the association between emergency presentation and adverse outcomes and underscore the potential importance of timely elective evaluation and preoperative optimization in appropriately selected patients.

Prior population-based studies have demonstrated increased morbidity and mortality with emergency repair, but limited data exist from disease-specific hernia registries incorporating detailed anatomical and operative variables. METHODS: Records from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative (ACHQC) registry spanning 2013 through 2023 were reviewed retrospectively.

title: Pancreatic Ischemic Necrosis Caused by Cholesterol Crystal Embolization Following Total Arch Replacement: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute pancreatitis is a recognized but uncommon complication of cardiovascular surgery. Cholesterol crystal embolization (CCE), a systemic ischemic disease, is a rare and potentially overlooked cause of pancreatic injury after cardiovascular surgery. Pancreatic involvement is uncommon, particularly when it progresses to extensive pancreatic necrosis requiring surgery. In this study, we report a case of CCE presenting as recurrent pancreatitis after total arch replacement that progressed to extensive pancreatic ischemic necrosis requiring total pancreatectomy.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 56-year-old man underwent total arch replacement for thoracic aortic aneurysm and subsequently developed acute pancreatitis with hepatic and renal dysfunction. Although his condition initially improved with conservative management, the pancreatitis recurred approximately 2 months after surgery and progressed to extensive, treatment-refractory pancreatic necrosis. He was referred to our institution approximately 4 months after surgery. CT revealed marked diffuse pancreatic enlargement with patchy low-attenuation areas, findings suggestive of extensive pancreatic necrosis. Because of persistent inflammation, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and deterioration of his general condition, total pancreatectomy was performed as a life-saving measure. Histopathological examination revealed widespread pancreatic necrosis and numerous cholesterol crystal emboli in small intrapancreatic arteries, thus establishing the diagnosis of pancreatic ischemic necrosis caused by CCE. On POD 20, the patient developed hemorrhage from the gastroduodenal artery. Although hemostasis was achieved by transcatheter arterial embolization, the patient subsequently developed septic shock and died on POD 22. Autopsy revealed ascending colon necrosis with cholesterol crystal emboli in small arteries and widespread CCE in other organs, including liver, kidneys, stomach, small intestine, and adrenal glands, demonstrating multiorgan involvement of CCE.

CONCLUSIONS: CCE should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained, recurrent, or progressive pancreatitis following cardiovascular surgery or endovascular intervention. Furthermore, multiorgan involvement demonstrated at autopsy highlights that CCE presenting predominantly with pancreatic involvement may also affect other organs, warranting careful assessment for additional organ involvement.

Cholesterol crystal embolization (CCE), a systemic ischemic disease, is a rare and potentially overlooked cause of pancreatic injury after cardiovascular surgery. Pancreatic involvement is uncommon, particularly when it progresses to extensive pancreatic necrosis requiring surgery.

title: Safety of home treatment for incidental pulmonary embolism in cancer patients.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) is increasingly detected in computed tomography (CT) scans for scheduled cancer staging, but the safety of outpatient management in these patients with active cancer remains uncertain, as current guidelines usually do not define patients with pulmonary embolism and cancer as low risk.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival. Events were unscheduled consultations or emergency department presentations, progression of venous thromboembolism, clinically relevant bleeding or death.

RESULTS: Of 212 patients included, 89.2% were managed as outpatients. Patients treated at home were less likely to have bilateral pulmonary embolism, evidence of right ventricular dysfunction, an elevated troponin or hypoxemia. 90-day all-cause mortality was 5.2%, deaths occurred usually while the patient was receiving hospice care. For patients treated at home clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1.6% and progression of thromboembolism in 2.1%.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients diagnosed with iPE, most patients were treated at home. With 90-day mortality likely being mainly caused by the malignancy, home treatment appears safe if cancer is the only risk factor present.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) is increasingly detected in computed tomography (CT) scans for scheduled cancer staging, but the safety of outpatient management in these patients with active cancer remains uncertain, as current guidelines usually do not define patients with pulmonary embolism and cancer as low risk. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and incident peripheral artery disease in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherogenic, prothrombotic lipoprotein linked to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but prospective data on its association with peripheral artery disease (PAD) in large, diverse U.S. cohorts are limited. We characterized the association of Lp(a) with long-term incident PAD risk in a diverse, community-based U.S.

METHODS: We included Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study participants attending Visit 4 (1996-98) with measured Lp(a) and no prevalent PAD. Lp(a) was natural logarithm (ln)-transformed and categorized as <30, 30-50, and >50 mg/dL. Incident PAD was identified from hospitalization and procedure codes through 2019. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for confounders; Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions accounted for competing mortality.

RESULTS: Among 9727 participants (mean age 63.1 years, 53.9% women, 20.4% Black), 825 incident PAD events occurred over a median 22.5 years of follow-up. Lp(a) was <30 mg/dL in 69.7%, 30-50 in 11.7%, and >50 in 18.6%. Fully adjusted HRs were 1.27 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.57) for 30-50 mg/dL and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.11-1.57) for >50 mg/dL versus <30 mg/dL; each unit increase in ln(Lp(a)) was associated with an HR of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.07-1.20). Estimates were similar accounting for competing mortality, and cumulative incidence differed across categories (p < 0.001). The association did not differ by baseline statin use.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with greater long-term PAD risk in a community-based cohort, supporting Lp(a) as a risk factor for lower-extremity atherosclerotic disease and its value for risk stratification.

title: Post-Traumatic Abdominal Aortic Dissection Associating Solid Organ Injury in a Child.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Handlebar injuries are frequent events in children, often perceived as minor, but may result in severe intra-abdominal damage.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 13-year-old boy who sustained a blunt abdominal trauma following impact against a bicycle handlebar. In this case, the trauma produced an unusual and potentially life-threatening combination of lesions, including massive hemoperitoneum, a deep hepatic laceration, a severe pancreatic injury with disruption of the main pancreatic duct, and a post-traumatic dissection of the infrarenal abdominal aorta.

RESULTS: The patient was admitted in critical condition and underwent prompt clinical, laboratory, and radiological evaluation. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed the extent of the abdominal injuries and confirmed the vascular involvement. Given the complexity and severity of the findings, management required a rapid multidisciplinary approach involving pediatric surgeons, interventional radiologists, vascular surgeons, and gastroenterologists. The infrarenal aortic dissection was treated urgently with an endovascular approach using the placement of a covered stent, allowing successful exclusion of the lesion and stabilization of the vascular injury while avoiding open surgery. The hepatic injury was managed conservatively with close hemodynamic and radiological monitoring. During the subsequent clinical course, the patient developed a large post-traumatic pancreatic pseudocyst related to the pancreatic duct disruption. This complication was successfully treated with endoscopic ultrasound-guided drainage using a lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS), which allowed effective internal drainage and progressive resolution of the collection.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the potentially severe nature of bicycle handlebar injuries in children and emphasizes the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for occult intra-abdominal and vascular injuries. Early diagnosis and timely multimodal management are crucial to optimize outcomes in these complex traumatic scenarios.

title: An MRI-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Mechanics Assessment.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop and validate a patient-specific Bayesian inverse modeling framework for the simultaneous estimation of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) wall and intraluminal thrombus (ILT) material properties using in vivo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

METHODS: Finite element models (FEMs) of four AAA patients were constructed from MRI geometries. Bayesian optimization combined with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was applied to identify nonlinear anisotropic material parameters minimizing the discrepancy between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements. Validation was performed against equibiaxial mechanical tests on tissues excised from the same patients. Sensitivity analyses assessed the impact of wall thickness and ILT inclusion on stress predictions.

RESULTS: Bayesian-identified parameters closely matched experimental equibiaxial responses, reproducing both displacement magnitudes and anisotropy. RMSE values between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements were low, confirming high model fidelity. Peak wall stresses (PWS) distributions revealed that ILT significantly attenuates wall stress, with stress concentrations localized in ILT-free regions. Moderate variations in wall thickness or ILT material properties had limited impact on PWS locations, while exclusion of ILT markedly increased predicted stresses.

CONCLUSION: The proposed Bayesian framework provides a robust, patient-specific methodology for accurate estimation of AAA wall and ILT mechanical properties, enabling reliable prediction of wall stress distributions and highlighting the protective role of ILT. This approach has potential to improve individualized rupture risk assessment and inform clinical decision-making.

title: Improving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in hospitalized pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Youth hospitalized with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin is routine in adults hospitalized with IBD, but standardized pediatric protocols are rare. Using quality improvement methods, we aimed to increase the rate of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst select hospitalized patients with IBD by reaching 90% algorithm adherence by June 2023 and sustaining.

METHODS: Current evidence, external institutional algorithms, and multidisciplinary collaboration (hematology, pharmacy, surgery) were used to create an algorithm for providing pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin. The algorithm was implemented in February 2023 for all patients admitted with active IBD to a large, tertiary care children's hospital. Rates of algorithm adherence and rates of enoxaparin receipt during the project period were compared to baseline rates. Patient and provider education, electronic data tracking, and regular data auditing and review with providers were used to improve algorithm adherence. Reasons for non-adherence to the algorithm and rates of VTE, bleeding complications, and medication side effects during hospitalization were tracked.

RESULTS: The proportion of patients who appropriately followed the algorithm reached 94%, increased from 50% when the algorithm was retrospectively applied to the pre-project period (p < 0.001). The total proportion of hospitalized patients who received pharmacologic prophylaxis increased from 1% to 31% (p < 0.001). Following algorithm introduction, there were no VTEs or reported complications from enoxaparin during hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS: The introduction of a standardized algorithm was associated with significantly increased rates of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst children hospitalized with IBD with no recorded adverse in-hospital events.

title: Suture-Only vs Hybrid Closure Techniques for Vascular Access Haemostasis in Percutaneous Cardiovascular Procedures: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular complications and bleeding increase morbidity and mortality after percutaneous cardiovascular procedures, including transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVR) and percutaneous endovascular aneurysm repair (pEVAR), often from vascular closure device (VCD) failure. We compared suture-only (SO) with suture and plug-based hybrid (HSP) vascular closure technique for vascular access haemostasis after percutaneous procedures such as TAVR and pEVAR.

METHOD: We performed a systematic literature search of randomised controlled trials (RCT) and observational studies using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and ClinicalTrials.gov following the PRISMA guidelines. The study protocol was registered at PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024627875). We calculated the relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) for individual end points of vascular complications, bleeding risk, VCD failure, and mortality, using random-effects models to report overall effect sizes.

RESULTS: Nine studies, including two RCTs and seven observational studies, comprising 3,765 patients (SO, 1,971; HSP, 1,790), were analysed. The SO strategy was associated with a significantly higher risk of vascular complications (RR 1.95; p<0.01), bleeding (RR 2.14; p=0.01), and VCD failure (RR 4.00; p<0.01) compared with the HSP technique. No significant difference was noted in all-cause mortality (RR 1.61; p=0.11) between the two groups, although the analysis was limited by the relatively small number of observed events and wide CIs.

CONCLUSIONS: Use of the HSP technique for vascular access haemostasis after TAVR or pEVAR was associated with significantly lower rates of vascular complications, bleeding, and VCD failure compared with SO closure, without a significant difference in mortality.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Vascular complications and bleeding increase morbidity and mortality after percutaneous cardiovascular procedures, including transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVR) and percutaneous endovascular aneurysm repair (pEVAR), often from vascular closure device (VCD) failure. We compared suture-only (SO) with suture and plug-based hybrid (HSP) vascular closure technique for vascular access haemostasis after percutaneous procedures such as TAVR and pEVAR. METHOD: We performed a systematic literature search of randomised controlled trials (RCT) and observational studies using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and ClinicalTrials.gov following the PRISMA guidelines.

title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).

CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates.

title: Survival and Aortic Reintervention Following Hemiarch vs. Extended Arch for Acute Type A Dissection in Patients Over Age 65.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ascending hemiarch replacement is considered standard, some have advocated extended arch reconstruction as the preferred strategy in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined.

METHODS: Patients aged ≥65 years undergoing non-elective hemiarch or extended arch for ATAAD in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services linkage (July 2017-2023,N=3,562;2,442[68.6%] hemiarch;1,120[31.4%] extended arch) were compared. Primary endpoints were long-term mortality and aortic reintervention beyond 30 days and were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence functions, followed by multivariable regressions.

RESULTS: Hemiarch patients tended to be slightly older (73.8±6.1vs.73.1±5.9 years), female (46.6%vs.39.6%), and hyperacute ATAAD (80.1%vs74.7%). Malperfusion was more frequent in extended arch (27.8% vs 20.6%). Extended arch patients had: i) longer cardiopulmonary bypass, cross-clamp, and circulatory arrest times and ii) more frequent antegrade and/or retrograde cerebral perfusion. Short-term outcomes and rates of concomitant procedures were similar between groups. Risk-adjusted analysis showed no treatment effects for survival, aortic reintervention, operative mortality, and stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Extended arch for treatment of ATAAD in patients aged ≥65 years was not associated with improved mortality or aortic reintervention compared to hemiarch at intermediate followup. Absent patient-specific indications, hemiarch may be sufficient in patients aged ≥65 years with ATAAD.

Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined.

title: Variation in Inferior Vena Cava Filter Retrieval Across U.S. Veterans Health Administration Facilities.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters prevent pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients unable to receive anticoagulation but require prompt retrieval once protection is no longer needed. Despite national safety advisories and multidisciplinary guidelines, IVC filter retrieval remains low in the United States. How much variation underlies low retrieval across Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities has not been studied.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study included Veterans who underwent IVC filter implantation at VA facilities between 2016 and 2023. Veterans who died within 90 days of implantation or lacked 1 year of follow-up were excluded. IVC filter implantation and retrieval were identified using procedure codes in the VA Corporate Data Warehouse. A multivariable Bayesian mixed-effects model estimated risk-adjusted retrieval rates across facilities. Logistic regression was performed to identify specific patient- and facility-level factors associated with non-retrieval.

RESULTS: Among 3,670 Veterans (median age 69 years; 95.9% male), retrieval occurred in 10.5% within 90 days, 22.2% within 1 year, and 24.7% overall. Risk-adjusted 1-year retrieval varied widely across facilities: 0-60%. Older veteran age (> 75 years), facility academic affiliation, and Southern census region were associated with lower retrieval, whereas implantation at higher-complexity facilities and pre-COVID years were associated with higher retrieval.

CONCLUSIONS: IVC filter retrieval rates among Veterans remain low but exceed those reported in non-VA Medicare cohorts. Substantial inter-facility variation highlights opportunities to standardize structured device surveillance, with clear responsibility for follow-up.

Despite national safety advisories and multidisciplinary guidelines, IVC filter retrieval remains low in the United States. How much variation underlies low retrieval across Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities has not been studied.

title: Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair as a Salvage Strategy after Failed Chimney Endovascular Aortic Repair: An International Multicentre Cohort.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 29 consecutive patients (median age 81.0 years, interquartile range [IQR] 66.0, 83.0) treated across 13 European centres (2013 - 2025) for failed chEVAR using branched endografts. The primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day clinical success, and procedure related complications. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, freedom from re-intervention, and target visceral vessel (TVV) patency.

RESULTS: The median interval from index chEVAR to BEVAR re-intervention was 48.5 months (IQR 30.0, 80.8). Acute urgent or emergent procedures accounted for 17% of cases (n = 5), while 31% (n = 9) underwent expedited repair for large aneurysms. Off the shelf devices were utilised in 41% of cases. A total of 106 TVVs were incorporated through branches, with a mean of 3.7 vessels per patient. Technical success was achieved in 97% (28 of 29). There was no peri-operative mortality or open surgical conversion. Significant complications included two cases (7%) of severe spinal cord ischaemia. The thirty day clinical success rate was 90%. At a median follow up of 19 months (IQR 9, 40), the Kaplan-Meier estimate for overall survival was 92% at 1 year. TVV patency was 100%, with only one renal artery re-intervention for in stent re-stenosis. Freedom from branch related re-intervention was 96% at 1 year.

CONCLUSION: Salvage of failed chEVAR using branched endografts is technically demanding but yields excellent early results. In experienced centres, BEVAR appears feasible and offers one potential salvage option in selected patients with suitable anatomy, particularly when an off the shelf solution is required.

Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.

CONCLUSION: A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

title: Dissecting the molecular machinery of CRISPR-associated transposons.
abstract: CRISPR-associated transposons (CASTs) are naturally occurring mobile genetic elements that combine programmable RNA-guided DNA recognition with transposase-mediated integration, enabling site-selective insertion of kilobase-scale DNA without nuclease-induced double-strand breaks. Current structural and biochemical knowledge can be viewed in terms of three functional modules: the transposase module, which performs DNA cleavage and strand transfer; the AAA+ ATPase TnsC, which forms a recruitment and regulatory platform; and TnsD or CRISPR effector-TniQ targeting complexes, which position this platform at selected DNA sites. Here, we synthesize recent structural and biochemical advances in target recognition, recruitment, donor-end pairing, and strand transfer. Comparisons with Tn7 and phage Mu highlight conserved transposase and ATPase functions and system-specific differences in how these components are organized and regulated. We discuss the implications of these advances for engineering programmable DNA-insertion systems and highlight unresolved questions in CAST transposition.

title: Three-dimensional longitudinal morphometric outcomes following minimally invasive surgery and helmet therapy in single-suture craniosynostosis.
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical and three-dimensional morphometric outcomes following minimally invasive strip craniectomy combined with postoperative helmet therapy in children with single-suture craniosynostosis and to identify subtype-specific parameters suitable for objective outcome assessment. Fifty-seven patients with single-suture craniosynostosis treated between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively analysed. Serial three-dimensional cranial photographs were obtained preoperatively, postoperatively, during helmet therapy, and at treatment completion. Morphometric assessment included cephalic index (CI), anterior arc angle (AAA), circumference index (CFI), and symmetry ratios (ASR, PSR), depending on synostosis subtype. Fifty-seven children (37% female) with single-suture craniosynostosis were included (31 sagittal, 17 metopic, 9 coronal suture synostosis). The mean age at operation was 12.3 weeks, and the average duration of helmet therapy was 9.7 months (SD 4.4 months). In sagittal craniosynostosis, significant improvements in the CI were observed (p < 0.001). In metopic craniosynostosis, AAA and CFI showed significant improvements (p < 0.001). In coronal synostosis, anterior volume ratios demonstrated stabilization during follow-up. Minimally invasive strip craniectomy combined with postoperative helmet therapy results was associated with improvements of morphometric outcomes in single-suture craniosynostosis. Subtype-specific indices such as CI, AAA, CFI, and symmetry ratios enable standardized and objective longitudinal assessment in routine clinical practice.

title: Urban-Rural Disparities in Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis: A Nationwide Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of hospital location on clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis (AP).

METHODS: We used the National Inpatient Sample database (2016-2022) to identify adult patients with AP. Patients were stratified by hospital location into urban and rural groups. Data on demographics, comorbidities, infections, and clinical outcomes were collected. Multivariate regression was used to assess the association between hospital setting and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 2 467 234 patients hospitalized with AP, 246 820 (10%) received care in rural hospitals. Patients in urban settings had a higher incidence of in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.35-1.62), sepsis (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.24), shock (aOR 1.77, 95% CI 1.64-1.92), acute kidney injury (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.29), intensive care unit admission (aOR 1.63, 95% CI 1.51-1.75), pulmonary embolism (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.05-1.47), and deep vein thrombosis (aOR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.09); (all P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that patients with AP treated in urban hospitals experience worse clinical outcomes and greater health care utilization than those in rural settings. These results underscore the importance of early diagnosis and risk stratification, particularly in high-volume urban hospitals, to improve patient outcomes.

METHODS: We used the National Inpatient Sample database (2016-2022) to identify adult patients with AP. Patients were stratified by hospital location into urban and rural groups.

title: Predictors and Mid-Term Outcomes of Vascular Complications After Large-Bore Plug-Based Access-Site Closure in Patients Undergoing Transfemoral TAVI: A CHOICE-CLOSURE Substudy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The plug-based MANTA (Teleflex, Pennsylvania, USA) vascular closure device (VCD) is an alternative to suture-based VCDs for large-bore arterial closure after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but has been associated with higher rates of vascular complications. Predictors and outcomes of these complications are not well-analyzed, especially regarding the self-resorbing characteristics of the MANTA VCD.

OBJECTIVES: To identify predictors of access-site related vascular complications following transfemoral TAVI with the MANTA VCD, and to assess mid-term outcomes and late-onset events (after 30 days) in affected patients.

METHODS: This prospective substudy of the CHOICE-CLOSURE trial included all patients randomized to vascular closure with the MANTA VCD at the Leipzig Heart Center. Patients with vascular complications, defined according to the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-2 criteria, underwent additional clinical and ultrasound follow-up, at least 6 months after the index procedure. Predictors of vascular complications were assessed through multivariable analysis.

RESULTS: Of 237 patients treated with the MANTA VCD, 46 (19.4%) had an access-site related vascular complication. Pre-procedural dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was the only independent predictor in multivariable analysis (Odds ratio 4.27, 95% confidence interval 1.58-11.59, p = 0.004). At a mean follow-up of 13.5 months, no new vascular complications occurred. Patients with an over-stented MANTA VCD (n = 5) had no in-stent stenosis, and stent diameters further expanded by 12.5% to 20.0%.

CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural DAPT independently predicted vascular complications after TAVI in MANTA patients. Patients with vascular complications had no further access-site late-onset events, and endovascular stenting of a MANTA VCD appeared safe.
