title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion.

RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak.

title: Description of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing endovascular revascularization for lower extremity peripheral artery disease (DATE-PAD).
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe real-world antithrombotic prescribing patterns following endovascular revascularization for lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD), and to compare short-term efficacy and safety outcomes between dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and single antiplatelet therapy plus oral anticoagulant (SAPT+OAC) regimens.

METHODS: A retrospective, multi-center descriptive study was conducted on patients 18 years or older with acute limb ischemia (ALI) or chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) who underwent endovascular intervention of the lower extremity between January 2023 and August 2024 and were discharged on DAPT or SAPT+OAC. Patients with surgical interventions for PAD during the same admission were excluded. Primary outcome was the frequency of DAPT compared to SAPT+OAC discharge regimens. Secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day readmissions, bleeding, ischemic events, and amputations all within 90 days.

RESULTS: Of 221 patients, 86% were discharged on DAPT and 14% on SAPT+OAC. Low dose aspirin and clopidogrel was the predominant DAPT regimen (94%). Apixaban was the most common anticoagulant (71%), with 75% of patients receiving 5 mg twice daily dosing. SAPT+OAC was more frequently used in ALI (50%) than CLTI (10%). No significant differences were observed in 30- or 90-day readmissions, bleeding rates, amputations, or ischemic events.

CONCLUSIONS: DAPT remains the predominant regimen post-revascularization despite recommendations for low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin. Apixaban was the predominant anticoagulant despite the paucity of data for use in this population. Comparable short-term outcomes suggest both DAPT and SAPT+OAC regimens may be viable, though further research is needed to clarify optimal anticoagulant of choice and dosing, particularly for apixaban.

METHODS: A retrospective, multi-center descriptive study was conducted on patients 18 years or older with acute limb ischemia (ALI) or chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) who underwent endovascular intervention of the lower extremity between January 2023 and August 2024 and were discharged on DAPT or SAPT+OAC. Patients with surgical interventions for PAD during the same admission were excluded.

title: Incidence, diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes of abdominal aortic aneurysms in Ontario: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) management substantially changed in 2003 when endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) became readily available in Canada. The long-term implications to routine practice in Ontario are unknown. We therefore sought to estimate trends in stable (sAAA) and ruptured (rAAA) incidence, treatment (EVAR or open surgical repair [OSR]), and postoperative mortality.

METHODS: We constructed a population-based cohort study of patients with incident sAAA and rAAA in Ontario using administrative health data from April 2012 to March 2023. To assess patterns in incidence, autoregressive integrated moving average models were fit. Three population-level interventions were incorporated: a Canadian Society of Vascular Surgery (CSVS) position statement, sent to Ontario physicians in early 2018, about the Canadian AAA screening recommendations published in 2017; the COVID-19 pandemic onset in 2020; and publication of the CSVS screening guidelines for AAA in 2021.

RESULTS: In total, 24 619 patients were included. Patients were predominantly male (77.2%), from urban settings (87.1%), with low comorbidity (82.3%). There was a small month-over-month increase in reported sAAA identified following the CSVS position statement in 2018. Conversely, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a steep drop in sAAA reported, which remained thereafter. Publication of the CSVS screening guidelines in 2021 was not associated with a change in sAAA trends. Incidence of rAAA was also reduced during the pandemic but was not affected by either publication. Treatment with EVAR for rAAA increased from 10.2% to 18%, whereas treatment with OSR declined from 40.8% to 31.3%. Untreated sAAA increased from 28.2% to 42.7%. Thirty-day (54.7%) and 1-year (61.7%) postoperative mortality from rAAA was stable, whereas mortality from sAAA increased slightly (30-d: 5% to 6.5%; 1-yr: 14% to 16.5%).

CONCLUSION: Overall reporting of cases of sAAA and rAAA is decreasing in Ontario. The 2018 position statement on AAA screening guidelines led to slightly increased reported sAAA, while reporting of rAAA was not affected. As expected, the volume of patients with rAAA who received EVAR increased, while the volume of those who received OSR decreased.

The long-term implications to routine practice in Ontario are unknown. We therefore sought to estimate trends in stable (sAAA) and ruptured (rAAA) incidence, treatment (EVAR or open surgical repair [OSR]), and postoperative mortality.

title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion.

title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net (2D and 3D), and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet (2D and 3D). We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

title: Association of autoimmune diseases and transient risk factors with clinical outcomes in patients with venous thromboembolism: COMMAND VTE registry insights.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transient provoking factors are generally associated with a lower risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE). Whether this association also applies to patients with autoimmune diseases, which constitute persistent risk factors, remains uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed 6022 patients with acute symptomatic VTE without active cancer from the retrospective, multicenter COMMAND VTE Registries, including 734 with and 5288 without autoimmune diseases. Within each subgroup, clinical outcomes were compared across major, minor, and no transient provoking factor categories, using the no transient factor category as the reference.

RESULTS: Compared with patients without autoimmune diseases, those with autoimmune diseases had higher risks of recurrent VTE [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.73; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.31-2.28] and major bleeding (adjusted HR 1.45; 95% CI 1.14-1.83). In analyses stratified by autoimmune disease status, major transient provoking factors, compared with no transient provoking factors, were associated with a lower risk of recurrent VTE among patients without autoimmune diseases (adjusted HR 0.30; 95% CI 0.19-0.48). This association was less clear among patients with autoimmune diseases (adjusted HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.36-2.35). A similar pattern was observed in the landmark analysis after anticoagulation discontinuation.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between transient provoking factors and a lower recurrence risk was less clear in patients with autoimmune diseases. These findings suggest that transient provoking factor status alone may provide limited guidance for recurrence risk assessment in this population, although imprecise estimates preclude firm conclusions.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Transient provoking factors are generally associated with a lower risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE). Whether this association also applies to patients with autoimmune diseases, which constitute persistent risk factors, remains uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed 6022 patients with acute symptomatic VTE without active cancer from the retrospective, multicenter COMMAND VTE Registries, including 734 with and 5288 without autoimmune diseases.

title: Ascending Aorta Dilation in the Fontan: To Intervene or Not.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation.

WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

DISCUSSION: There are case reports of aortic dissection, but true risk remains unknown. Weighing the risks of surgery versus conservative management in patients with single ventricle physiology is challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Surgical intervention on dilated aortas in patients with single ventricle physiology is perilous but possible in the correct circumstances.

WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

title: Thrombolysis and thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: A RAND/UCLA consensus.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The treatment of acute ischemic stroke in the pediatric population involves considerable uncertainty due to the limited evidence on intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. The objective was to assess the contribution of different scenario variables to the appropriateness of thrombolysis and thrombectomy in children and adolescents, as an aid to clinical decision-making.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method was applied. A multidisciplinary panel assessed theoretical clinical scenarios, differentiating two age groups: ≥30 days to 2 years, and >2 to <18 years. The scenarios were rated in two rounds, one of which was face-to-face. Multinomial logistic regression was performed to estimate the contribution of the variables, and CART analysis was used to synthesize the appropriateness criteria in the form of decision trees.

RESULTS: A total of 128 clinical scenarios were assessed per age group. In the multivariable analysis, all the variables contributed significantly. Lesion location contributed most to the fit of the model in patients aged≥30 days to 2 years, as opposed to symptom onset in patients aged>2 to <18 years. The models showed a good overall fit, with Nagelkerke pseudo-R2 values of 0.833 and 0.784, respectively, which allowed summarizing the criteria in the form of decision trees.

CONCLUSIONS: Appropriateness criteria were established to support decision-making regarding thrombolysis and thrombectomy in pediatric ischemic stroke. Lesion location and symptom onset were the variables that contributed most to model fit, depending on the age group. These criteria may support decision-making in contexts of clinical uncertainty, although they cannot replace clinical judgment.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The treatment of acute ischemic stroke in the pediatric population involves considerable uncertainty due to the limited evidence on intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. The objective was to assess the contribution of different scenario variables to the appropriateness of thrombolysis and thrombectomy in children and adolescents, as an aid to clinical decision-making. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method was applied.

title: Aortic valve disease associated inlet flow affects blood flow and nitric oxide transport: a potential role in ascending aortic dilation.
abstract: Aortic valve disease is associated with an increased risk of ascending aortic dilation and is characterized by abnormal inlet jet characteristics, which can regulate endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS)-mediated nitric oxide (NO) production through mechanobiological signaling. This study used computational fluid dynamics to quantify the effects of inlet jet tilt and axial rotation on aortic hemodynamics and NO response in a thoracic aortic model. Increasing inlet tilt shifted the jet toward the outer aortic wall, progressively altered helical flow from right-to left-handed, and increased time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), transverse WSS (transWSS), and time-averaged WSS gradient (TAWSSG) while reducing oscillatory shear index (OSI) and relative residence time (RRT). Axial rotation primarily reorganized the spatial topology of helical flow and redistributed high-shear regions. Increasing inlet tilt elevated time-averaged NO (TANO) in the ascending aorta, with a marked increase along the right-anterior wall even at small tilt angles, whereas axial rotation increased TANO along the left wall. Notably, regions of increased TANO broadly corresponded to anatomical locations previously reported to be associated with ascending aortic aneurysm. These findings indicate that abnormal inlet jet characteristics can alter the aortic WSS and NO transport, suggesting a potential mechanobiological link to ascending aortic dilation.

title: Indirect versus combined bypass for perfusion-defined high-risk adult moyamoya disease: a propensity score overlap-weighted analysis of revascularization and postoperative stroke.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adult patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and extensive preoperative perfusion delay may be at increased risk for postoperative stroke after combined bypass (CB). We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024. The cohort wasrestricted to hemispheres with a preoperative tissue volume of at least 59.5 mL showing time-to-maximum (Tmax) >6 seconds (6s). Revascularization was assessed by 6-month angiography using the Matsushima grading system, and perfusion improvement was evaluated using postoperative CT perfusion. Baseline imbalance was addressed using overlap-weighted propensity score analysis. Factors associated with postoperative stroke were evaluated using overlap-weighted logistic regression, with sensitivity analyses using patient-clustered robust standard errors and Firth penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 124 hemispheres were analyzed (CB, 88; IB, 36). Before weighting, PCA involvement was more frequent in the IB group (86.1% vs. 61.4%; standardized mean difference = 0.586), but all prespecified covariates were balanced after overlap weighting. Good revascularization was comparable between CB and IB before weighting (93.2% vs. 94.4%, p = 1.000) and after overlap weighting (90.6% vs. 98.1%, p = 0.102). Postoperative perfusion outcomes were also similar. Postoperative stroke occurred less frequently after IB both before weighting (5.6% vs. 23.9%, p = 0.021) and after overlap weighting (5.2% vs. 34.6%, p < 0.001). In the overlap-weighted multivariable model, IB was associated with lower odds of postoperative stroke, whereas larger preoperative Tmax>6s volume was associated with higher odds. These findings remained significant after adjustment for intra-patient correlation and were directionally consistent in Firth analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: In this perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort, IB achieved angiographic and perfusion outcomes comparable to CB, with a lower observed postoperative stroke. IB may be a reasonable risk-adapted option for selected high-risk hemispheres, although non-randomized treatment allocation warrants cautious interpretation.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Adult patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and extensive preoperative perfusion delay may be at increased risk for postoperative stroke after combined bypass (CB). We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024.

title: Accuracy and Concordance of Agitated Saline Bubble-Enhanced Ultrasound versus Chest Radiography by Internal Jugular Insertion Site.
abstract: Non-tunneled hemodialysis catheters (HDCs) are commonly used to initiate renal replacement therapy in hospitalized patients, especially those with acute kidney injury. HDC malposition is associated with delayed therapy and inadequate dialysis. Agitated saline bubble-enhanced ultrasound (SBUS) has emerged as a method for visualizing catheter position at the time of insertion. This study aimed to analyze the accuracy and concordance of SBUS and chest radiography (CXR) for assessing HDC positioning according to the internal jugular vein (IJV) insertion site. A total of 152 hospitalized patients undergoing IJV catheter insertion were assessed from December 2019 to May 2021. Time from puncture to CXR result, procedure-related complications, blood flow during dialysis, and the accuracy and concordance of SBUS compared with CXR for determining HDC position adequacy were evaluated. The median time between catheter insertion and CXR was 191 min [interquartile range (IQR), 93-288 min], with no difference between insertion sites. The main complication after catheter insertion was arterial puncture (2% overall), with a similar incidence at both sites. Inadequate catheter blood flow was more frequent with left IJV insertion than with right IJV insertion. For right IJV catheters, concordance between SBUS and CXR was high (Gwet's AC1 = 0.95; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.915-0.992), with an accuracy of 95.6%. For left IJV catheters, concordance was low (Gwet's AC1 = 0.37; 95% CI, -0.21-0.94), with an accuracy of 64.3%. Compared with CXR, SBUS was suitable for assessing catheter placement following right IJV insertion but may be less suitable following left IJV insertion.
englishSummary: Non-tunneled hemodialysis catheters (HDCs) are commonly used to initiate renal replacement therapy in hospitalized patients, especially those with acute kidney injury. HDC malposition is associated with delayed therapy and inadequate dialysis. Agitated saline bubble-enhanced ultrasound (SBUS) has emerged as a method for visualizing catheter position at the time of insertion.

title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition.

RESULTS: Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p < 0.001), as were length of stay (8 vs 5 days; p < 0.001), thromboembolic events (6.5% vs 1.8%; p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.
englishSummary: AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

METHODS: Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences.

RESULTS: Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

title: Feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for preoperative planning in bicondylar tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective case series.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Schatzker type V and VI tibial plateau fractures have complex three-dimensional patterns that complicate surgical planning and coronal alignment restoration. This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024. Preoperative CT data enabled fragment segmentation, color coding, virtual reduction, and fabrication of patient-specific physical models. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, articular depression, and tibial plateau width were compared pre- and postoperatively. Rasmussen functional and radiological scores and Knee Society Scores were assessed at 3 and 6 months, 1 year, and final follow-up; complications were recorded.

RESULTS: All 22 patients completed follow-up (mean, 30.73 ± 3.20 months). A mean of 24.41 ± 2.26 tibial fragments were identified and segmented per patient. Mean articular depression decreased from 6.70 ± 3.07 to 1.74 ± 0.48 mm. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, and tibial plateau width improved significantly after surgery (all P < 0.001). Mean postoperative coronal alignment was within the predefined normal range in both preoperative varus and valgus subgroups. All three scores differed significantly across follow-up (all P < 0.001). At final follow-up, mean Rasmussen functional and Knee Society Scores were 27.18 ± 1.84 and 87.55 ± 4.92, respectively, with excellent-or-good rates of 100% and 95.45%. Mild post-traumatic knee osteoarthritis, superficial infection, and deep-vein thrombosis occurred in 5, 1, and 2 patients, respectively. No secondary varus or valgus deformity was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In complex bicondylar tibial plateau fractures, patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models provided a practical three-dimensional reference for fragment identification, reduction sequencing, and planning of combined medial and lateral approaches. Satisfactory articular reduction, maintenance of proximal tibial coronal alignment, and favorable functional outcomes at final follow-up were observed in this cohort. These findings support the feasibility of incorporating 3D-printed fragment models into preoperative planning for these fractures.

This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024.

title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.

METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.

title: Deep vein thrombosis-primed neutrophils reshape the brain microenvironment to promote brain metastasis.
abstract: Brain metastasis (BrM) is a devastating complication of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet how host macroenvironmental conditions influence brain metastatic susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a common complication in patients with cancer, on TNBC brain metastasis. Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer. Using two syngeneic TNBC models, we demonstrated that DVT selectively enhanced brain metastasis without significantly affecting primary tumor growth or lung metastasis. Mechanistically, DVT increased neutrophil accumulation in the brain metastatic microenvironment, and neutrophil depletion completely abrogated the metastasis-promoting effect of DVT. Single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45+ cells in peripheral blood revealed that DVT reprogrammed circulating neutrophils toward migratory and inflammatory transcriptomic profiles characterized by neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. DVT increased CXCR2 expression on circulating neutrophils and enhanced neutrophil recruitment in brain. Moreover, DVT significantly increased circulating NETs. Collectively, our findings identify DVT as a systemic driver of TNBC brain metastasis and reveal that DVT primes circulating neutrophils toward enhanced vascular recruitment and NET formation, providing a mechanistic link between cancer-associated thrombosis and brain metastatic susceptibility.

Here, we investigated the impact of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a common complication in patients with cancer, on TNBC brain metastasis. Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer.

title: Global trends and intellectual structure in war surgery and combat casualty care: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis (2000-2026).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: War surgery and combat casualty care (CCC) research has expanded rapidly, yet its growth dynamics, collaboration structure, thematic evolution and citation-based intellectual architecture remain incompletely characterised. This study mapped war surgery and CCC literature to identify dominant, emerging and declining themes and influential actors.

METHODS: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis used Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved on 15 February 2026. Articles published between 2000 and 2026 were identified through a topic search combining war/CCC terms with conflict-setting anchors and refined to English-language journal publications in relevant clinical categories. Performance indicators and network analyses were implemented in bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and CiteSpace. The corpus was partitioned into three time slices to assess thematic evolution and temporal keyword dynamics.

RESULTS: The final corpus comprised 413 WoSCC records indexed as Article. Production rose markedly after 2009 and remained sustained, while mean citations per article declined in recent cohorts, consistent with shorter citation windows. Thematic mapping showed a stable core around trauma/CCC and haemorrhage, alongside diversification towards capability-oriented themes. Burst detection and frequency-ratio analyses identified prolonged field care, readiness, and endovascular and transfusion-related innovations as accelerating topics, while earlier intervention-specific terms declined. The collaboration network was hub-dominated, indicating a concentrated knowledge-production structure organised around limited high-intensity bilateral links.

CONCLUSIONS: War surgery and CCC research is organised around a durable clinical core but is increasingly oriented towards system resilience under evacuation delays and resource constraints. Strengthening multi-country collaboration and sustaining inter-conflict research capacity are key levers for preparedness and civilian-military knowledge transfer.

This study mapped war surgery and CCC literature to identify dominant, emerging and declining themes and influential actors. METHODS: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis used Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved on 15 February 2026.

title: Anticipatory anxiety as a factor associated with the experience of venipuncture: a prospective study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anticipatory anxiety may affect how children experience invasive procedures, although its role in pain and procedural anxiety has not been fully established. The aim of our study was to analyze its association with the experience of venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheterization and assess whether the association remained significant after accounting for other procedural factors.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study in a pediatric emergency department between October 2023 and October 2024. The sample consisted of children aged 3-12 years undergoing venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheter insertion. Anticipatory anxiety, procedural anxiety, and pain were assessed. We analyzed the correlations between these variables and fitted multivariable logistic regression models to identify factors associated with severe pain and severe procedural anxiety.

RESULTS: A total of 140 patients were included; 39.3% had severe anticipatory anxiety, 39.3% severe pain, and 55.7% severe procedural anxiety. Anticipatory anxiety was significantly correlated to procedural anxiety (ρ=0.611) and pain (ρ=0.382), with stronger correlations in the group of patients aged 8-12 years (ρ=0.776 and ρ=0.603, respectively). Severe anticipatory anxiety was associated with a higher likelihood of severe procedural anxiety and severe pain, and these associations remained significant after the different adjustments.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe anticipatory anxiety was independently associated with a worse experience during venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheter insertion. The stronger association observed in children aged 8-12 years suggests that assessing the emotional state of the child before the procedure may help identify patients at greater risk of severe pain and procedural anxiety.

The aim of our study was to analyze its association with the experience of venipuncture or peripheral intravenous catheterization and assess whether the association remained significant after accounting for other procedural factors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study in a pediatric emergency department between October 2023 and October 2024.

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049).

CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.

Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

title: Delayed Internal Iliac Artery Pseudoaneurysm after Kidney Transplantation Successfully Treated With a Covered Stent: A Case Report.
abstract: Vascular complications after kidney transplantation are uncommon but may threaten graft survival. Pseudoaneurysms involving the iliac vessels can present years after transplantation with nonspecific symptoms, making early diagnosis essential. We report a 32-year-old woman who developed a delayed, partially thrombosed pseudoaneurysm of the right internal iliac artery four years after kidney transplantation. She presented with right groin pain, severe worsening hypertension (170/150 mmHg), oliguria, and an increase in serum creatinine from a post-transplant baseline of approximately 1.0 mg/dL to 2.8 mg/dL. During hospitalization, her hypertension was difficult to control despite losartan and Valzamikis. Following covered stent placement, blood pressure progressively normalized, and antihypertensive medications were discontinued. Renal function also improved, with serum creatinine decreasing to 1.4 mg/dL two days after the intervention, accompanied by recovery of urine output to approximately 2.5 L/day. Doppler ultrasonography and CT angiography confirmed the diagnosis and guided treatment planning. The patient underwent successful endovascular covered stent placement, resulting in exclusion of the pseudoaneurysm and preservation of renal graft perfusion. This case highlights the importance of considering delayed vascular complications in transplant recipients. It also demonstrates the feasibility of covered stent placement for exclusion of a delayed internal iliac artery pseudoaneurysm while preserving renal graft perfusion, with confirmed stent patency and preserved graft perfusion at approximately one-year follow-up.

Pseudoaneurysms involving the iliac vessels can present years after transplantation with nonspecific symptoms, making early diagnosis essential. We report a 32-year-old woman who developed a delayed, partially thrombosed pseudoaneurysm of the right internal iliac artery four years after kidney transplantation.

title: Identification of the Nature of Acute Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion and Preferred Strategy for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Acute middle cerebral artery occlusion is a common and critical cerebrovascular disease in clinical practice, characterized by its sudden onset and severe clinical symptoms, posing a substantial threat to neurological function and survival. Therefore, clinicians need to quickly and accurately identify the occlusion type and develop appropriate treatment plans accordingly. In recent years, with the development of neuroimaging technology and a deeper understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of acute middle cerebral artery occlusion, various diagnostic methods have been applied to determine the occlusion type. The core treatment goal of acute ischemic stroke is to minimize irreversible neuronal injury and restore effective brain tissue perfusion as soon as possible. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of multiple randomized controlled trials have consistently confirmed that mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has significant clinical efficacy in acute anterior circulation stroke patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO). Therefore, domestic and international evidence-based guidelines list it as a first-line endovascular intervention for LVO stroke in the early stage of onset (within 6 h; expandable to 24 h with imaging screening). This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic approaches for different types of acute middle cerebral artery occlusion and mechanical thrombectomy strategies tailored to the presumed occlusion mechanism, with the aim of informing mechanism-based diagnostic assessment and endovascular treatment decisions.

title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events.

METHODS: We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk.

RESULTS: At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher-versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher-versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792).

CONCLUSIONS: Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

CENTRAL PICTURE: Multidimensional digital twin model stratifies aortic event-free survival in AUTBAD.

CENTRAL MESSAGE: Combining patient-specific 3D aortic morphology and wall stress may improve identification of medically managed AUTBAD patients at high risk for aortic intervention or aortic-related death.

PERSPECTIVE: TBAD geometry is highly patient specific, and one-dimensional measurements may not fully reflect patient risk. Digital twin modeling incorporating 3D morphology and wall mechanics may provide a more complete basis for risk stratification. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating multidimensional shape and stress data into a risk-stratification model to identify high-risk AUTBAD patients.

METHODS: We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed.

title: Central Venous Stenosis: Etiology, Risk Factors, and Strategies for Prevention.
abstract: Central venous stenosis (CVS) is a common and clinically significant problem that can compromise effective hemodialysis. Understanding the etiologies and risk factors of CVS is essential for interventional radiologists involved in the care of patients with dialysis access. Although CVS is frequently associated with prior central venous catheterization, it can also be caused by diseases such as thrombophilias, fibrosing mediastinitis, and cancer. Regardless of the etiology, CVS can affect patients with all types of hemodialysis access. Herein, we review the causes and risk factors for CVS, current management approaches, and state-of-the-art strategies for its prevention.

title: Endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs).

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms and neurological signs, baseline and follow-up imaging findings (including digital subtraction angiography), procedural details (e.g., access route, embolic agents, technical success), and clinical outcomes-including angiographic occlusion status, symptom resolution, procedure-related complications, and functional recovery.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients were diagnosed with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). Twelve underwent endovascular treatment following definitive diagnosis by digital subtraction angiography (DSA); two declined intervention despite confirmed diagnosis. Thirteen presented with predominant ocular manifestations-such as proptosis, chemosis, and ophthalmoparesis-while one was diagnosed incidentally on cranial MRI performed for headache and dizziness. All 12 patients underwent the procedure successfully: seven underwent arterial-access embolization and five underwent venous-access embolization. Onyx liquid embolic agent was used as the sole embolic material in seven cases; in the remaining five cases, detachable coils were employed as adjunctive agents. Immediate post-procedural DSA demonstrated complete occlusion in nine patients and subtotal occlusion in three. Procedure-related complications occurred in five patients: visual acuity reduction (n = 2), ipsilateral facial hypoesthesia (n = 2), and isolated impairment of abduction and downward gaze (n = 1). Symptomatic improvement was observed in seven patients. At 1-year clinical and imaging follow-up, all 12 treated patients remained under surveillance. Ten exhibited no recurrence; notably, one patient with initial subtotal occlusion achieved complete angiographic occlusion during follow-up. In the remaining two, residual lesions remained stable in size, symptoms improved, and no secondary intervention was required. Among the five patients with procedure-related complications, two developed persistent facial hypoesthesia after intra-arterial embolization; subjective numbness gradually improved but did not fully resolve during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for craniospinal dural arteriovenous fistula (CSDAVFs) is associated with favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. Although procedure-related complications occur in a subset of patients, most are transient and resolve spontaneously or improve to partial remission during follow-up. Collectively, these findings support endovascular therapy as a safe and effective treatment modality for CSDAVFs.

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms and neurological signs, baseline and follow-up imaging findings (including digital subtraction angiography), procedural details (e.g., access route, embolic agents, technical success), and clinical outcomes-including angiographic occlusion status, symptom resolution, procedure-related complications, and functional recovery.

title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and clinical outcomes in acute atherosclerotic ischaemic stroke patients following endovascular thrombectomy: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and unfavourable clinical outcomes in patients with atherosclerotic acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: Patients with AIS who underwent EVT between January 2019 and September 2024 were enrolled. The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at three months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at three months. The TyG index was analysed continuously and in quartiles by logistic regression, restricted cubic splines and receiver operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: Among 670 patients, 269 (40.1%) had an unfavourable functional outcome at three months, 91 (13.6%) died at three months for all-cause, and 85 (12.7%) developed sICH. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest TyG quartile was independently associated with unfavourable functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.91, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-3.56) and mortality (aOR 5.15, 95% CI 2.06-12.86). The overall spline association was significant for all endpoints; only mortality was non-linear (P = 0.032), with risk rising above a TyG index of approximately 8.9. Discrimination was modest, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.583 for unfavourable functional outcome and 0.612 for mortality. No significant interactions were found across prespecified subgroups, except for blood glucose level.

CONCLUSION: An elevated TyG index is independently associated with three-month unfavourable functional outcome, mortality and sICH after EVT, and may aid prognostic risk stratification, although further validation is required based on the existing predictive indicators.

METHODS: Patients with AIS who underwent EVT between January 2019 and September 2024 were enrolled. The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at three months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at three months.

title: Open Repair of a Superior Mesenteric Artery Aneurysm With Interposition Graft.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior mesenteric artery aneurysm (SMAA) is a rare but potentially life-threatening vascular pathology. The 2020 Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend repair of all true SMAA regardless of size.

CASE SUMMARY: A 56-year-old man was found to have an incidental 2.1-cm saccular mid-superior mesenteric artery aneurysm discovered during trauma evaluation. Angiography confirmed mid-to-distal superior mesenteric artery involvement extending to the ileocolic, jejunal, and ileal branches, precluding endovascular repair. He underwent elective open aneurysmectomy with reversed great saphenous vein interposition grafting and branch reconstruction.

DISCUSSION: Open repair remains an important option for managing complex SMAA involving essential tributaries. Our case demonstrates the successful use of the reversed great saphenous vein as an interposition graft during open surgical repair for an anatomically complex SMAA.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Open repair remains essential for SMAA extending to major tributaries, and autogenous great saphenous vein is a durable conduit for complex branch reconstruction.

title: Noninvasive electrical impedance tomography monitoring during total aortic arch replacement: incremental value for prediction of postoperative neurological deficit.
abstract: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR. Methods: A 16-electrode EIT system and NIRS were utilized for intraoperative cerebral neuromonitoring during TAAR. Correlations between intraoperative EIT and NIRS variables and postoperative ND were comprehensively analyzed. Results: The overall incidence of postoperative ND was 39.1% (59/151), including a 15.2% incidence of postoperative stroke. The time integral of absolute resistivity asymmetry index during hypothermic circulatory arrest (TRAIHCA), the maximum absolute resistivity asymmetry ratio during HCA (MRARHCA), age, body mass index, supra-aortic branch involvement, and operative duration were independent predictors of postoperative ND. Incorporation of EIT parameters into the clinical prediction model significantly improved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.752 to 0.817 (P = 0.027). Moreover, the incremental prognostic value of EIT was further validated by improved risk reclassification and discriminatory ability for ND, with a net reclassification index of 0.510 (P = 0.002) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.072 (P < 0.001). Conclusion: The EIT parameters have been demonstrated to be an effective means of predicting ND following TAAR. Cerebral EIT may represent a potential alternative for intraoperative noninvasive multimodal neuromonitoring options.
englishSummary: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR.

title: Intraoperative measurement of the ascending aortic diameter at the onset of aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although prior studies have associated aortic size with dissection risk, none have corrected for dissection-related aortic expansion. This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection.

METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation. In this study, the intimal lumen diameter measured at its maximal stretching state was used as a reliable surrogate for the pre-dissection aortic diameter. Subsequently, the relationship between this surrogate and the aortic diameter measured on post-dissection CT at the corresponding levels was further analyzed.

RESULTS: Using this method, the pre-dissection ascending aortic diameter was measured as 37.5 ± 6.6 mm, whereas the post-dissection CT measurement at the same level increased to 43.9 ± 7.0 mm. After excluding patients with non-A-non-B aortic dissection, the mean ascending aortic diameter increased by approximately 20% after dissection compared with the pre-dissection value, corresponding to an absolute increase of 7.5 mm in diameter.

CONCLUSIONS: Although aortic diameter remains a robust indicator for prophylactic surgery in the study population, acute aortic dissection is seldom associated with true ascending aortic aneurysms and occurs with normal or near-normal aortic dimensions in most patients. When dissection occurs in the setting of a small aortic diameter, it likely reflects a profound functional vulnerability of the aortic tissue to catastrophic aortic events.

This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection. METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation.

title: Case Report: Splenorenal shunt management after liver transplantation in a recipient with situs inversus totalis.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) alters graft positioning and vascular reconstruction during liver transplantation. A 56-year-old man with SIT, decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma received a 558-g deceased-donor whole-liver graft, with a graft-to-recipient weight ratio of 0.60%. The graft was implanted in the native left-sided hepatic fossa in a reversed orientation. Postoperative CT showed a large splenorenal shunt and heterogeneous graft enhancement. Portal vein velocity fell from 44.7 cm/s on postoperative day (POD) 1 to 25 cm/s on POD3-4 and was 32 cm/s on POD5. Endovascular occlusion was abandoned on POD5 because venography showed aneurysmal dilatation and the procedural risk was judged excessive. Open ligation of the approximately 3-cm shunt was performed on POD6, preserving the main renal vein. Portal vein velocity was 30 cm/s after ligation, 37 cm/s on POD7 and 42 cm/s on POD9. Total bilirubin decreased from 158.6 μmol/L on POD4 to 70.5 μmol/L on POD13; the international normalized ratio was 1.49 on POD6 and 1.02 on POD14. The patient was discharged on POD27. Imaging showed no tumor recurrence at approximately 19 months, and alpha-fetoprotein was 7.32 ng/mL at approximately 23 months. This case describes surgical treatment of suspected portal steal in an SIT recipient when endovascular shunt occlusion was unsuitable.

A 56-year-old man with SIT, decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma received a 558-g deceased-donor whole-liver graft, with a graft-to-recipient weight ratio of 0.60%. The graft was implanted in the native left-sided hepatic fossa in a reversed orientation.

title: Oral anticoagulants and the risk of acute kidney injury: a retrospective real-world cohort study using overlap propensity score weighting.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University. Overlap propensity score weighting, with weights derived from a generalized boosted model incorporating 81 baseline covariates, balanced the treatment groups. Weighted logistic regression compared the risk of AKI within 30 days of OAC initiation, defined by KDIGO criteria. Sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and logistic regression-derived overlap weighting, each with or without doubly robust covariate adjustment.

RESULTS: Among 6 876 patients (5 048 DOAC users; 1 828 warfarin users), DOAC initiation was associated with a higher risk of AKI than warfarin after overlap weighting (OR: 1.346, 95% CI: 1.057-1.715; p = 0.016), and with severe AKI (stage 2-3; OR: 1.694, 95% CI: 1.013-2.832; p = 0.044), whereas stage 1 AKI did not differ significantly. The association persisted after additional covariate adjustment (OR: 1.363, 95% CI: 1.068-1.740; p = 0.013) and across alternative propensity score models, although the unadjusted IPTW model did not. By indication, the association was significant for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) (OR: 1.566, 95% CI: 1.034-2.369; p = 0.034) but not for venous thromboembolism (VTE) treatment or prophylaxis. Among individual DOACs, rivaroxaban was associated with an elevated risk (OR: 1.392, 95% CI: 1.075-1.804; p = 0.012), whereas edoxaban, dabigatran, and apixaban were not. Lower-dose rivaroxaban initiation was associated with an increased risk (OR: 2.792, 95% CI: 1.524-5.114; p = 0.001), whereas higher-dose and off-label use were not. In prespecified subgroup analyses, ORs were above 1 in most strata, but most comparisons were not significant, and no significant interactions were detected.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that DOACs, particularly rivaroxaban, may be associated with a higher short-term risk of AKI than warfarin. Given the expanding use of DOACs, medication-specific renal effects warrant further investigation, and close monitoring of renal function may be advisable in high-risk patients after anticoagulation initiation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University.

title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis identifies a PLAUR-centered macrophage-associated programmed cell death signature in type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening aortic emergency characterized by inflammatory remodeling, extracellular matrix disruption, and programmed cell death (PCD). The cell-specific transcriptional features associated with immune activation and PCD-related aortic wall injury remain incompletely defined. This study investigated PCD-associated immune remodeling in TAAD and evaluated PLAUR as a macrophage-associated marker linked to these pathological changes.

METHODS: Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing, curated PCD-related gene sets, immune deconvolution, pathway enrichment, in silico perturbation analysis, and histological assessment of human aortic specimens.

RESULTS: TAAD tissues exhibited marked transcriptomic alterations, with 2,217 genes meeting the exploratory differential-expression criteria, accompanied by increased PCD-related transcriptional activity. Single-cell analysis indicated that macrophage-enriched clusters showed relatively high PCD-related gene-set activity, while PLAUR transcripts were predominantly detected in macrophage-enriched clusters. PLAUR was upregulated in TAAD in both training and external validation datasets and strongly correlated with sample-level PCD scores. In the training dataset, PLAUR expression showed exploratory discrimination between TAAD and control tissue samples, with an AUC of 0.858. PLAUR-high samples showed enrichment of HIF-1, JAK-STAT, necroptosis, and apoptosis-related pathways. Immune deconvolution indicated relatively higher neutrophil- and M0 macrophage-associated signatures in TAAD, with PLAUR expression positively associated with myeloid-cell-related features. In silico perturbation analysis identified cytoskeletal and actin-related transcriptional changes associated with predicted PLAUR perturbation. Histological assessment demonstrated aortic wall disorganization, collagen remodeling, elastic fiber disruption, increased TUNEL positivity, and elevated PLAUR protein expression in TAAD lesions.

CONCLUSIONS: PLAUR is associated with macrophage-enriched inflammatory, proteolytic, and PCD-related remodeling in TAAD and may serve as a candidate marker of these pathological features. The present findings are associative and do not establish a causal role for PLAUR in aortic wall degeneration or dissection initiation. Spatially resolved and functional studies are required to determine whether PLAUR-positive macrophage states contribute mechanistically to TAAD pathogenesis.

The cell-specific transcriptional features associated with immune activation and PCD-related aortic wall injury remain incompletely defined. This study investigated PCD-associated immune remodeling in TAAD and evaluated PLAUR as a macrophage-associated marker linked to these pathological changes.

title: Molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers of Type B aortic dissection risk in Marfan syndrome: a scoping review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused primarily by pathogenic FBN1 variants, with aortic dissection a leading cause of mortality. Improved surgical thresholds have reduced Type A dissection mortality, but Type B dissection remains poorly predicted. This review maps current human evidence on molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers for Type B aortic dissection risk stratification in Marfan syndrome and identifies gaps that inform a future research agenda.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and the framework of Arksey and O'Malley. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for articles published between January 2010 and October 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and scored each study for evidence certainty across six domains.

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies met criteria, derived from 14 independent source populations; eight came from a single Dutch cohort network. Only two studies reported Type B dissection as a specified outcome; the remainder addressed dissection of unspecified type, aortic diameter or growth, or mechanistic endpoints. Four thematic evidence streams emerged. TGF-β pathway biomarkers show associations with aortic phenotype and disease severity across several cohorts, but their value for prospective prediction of Type B dissection remains unvalidated. Variants in TGFBR2 and TGFB2, and FBN1 cysteine-loss variants, are associated with severe aortic phenotypes yet are not integrated into the Ghent nosology. Losartan shows heterogeneous efficacy, and a predefined randomized trial substudy suggests that benefit may depend on FBN1 variant class, although no trial has stratified outcomes by dissection type. No tool exists to stratify Type B risk in the 5 to 10 percent of clinically diagnosed patients without an identifiable FBN1 variant. Evidence certainty was moderate for the pharmacologic stream and low to very low for the other three, and the biomarker evidence is associational rather than causal.

CONCLUSIONS: A competing-risks multimodal model integrating imaging, genotype, and treatment-adjusted biomarker trajectory, developed and externally validated in multicentre prospective cohorts, represents the next research frontier.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused primarily by pathogenic FBN1 variants, with aortic dissection a leading cause of mortality. Improved surgical thresholds have reduced Type A dissection mortality, but Type B dissection remains poorly predicted. This review maps current human evidence on molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers for Type B aortic dissection risk stratification in Marfan syndrome and identifies gaps that inform a future research agenda.

title: Application of endovascular stent graft in ABO-incompatible living donor kidney transplantation: a case report.
abstract: Severe iliac arteriosclerosis is a contraindication for kidney transplantation (KT). This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively. Routine pre-transplant therapy including rituximab 200mg, triple immunosuppressants included tacrolimus (7mg/d, tacrolimus concentration was between 3.8 and 9.2 ng/mL), mycophenolate mofetil (1500mg/d), methylprednisolone (16mg/d). Following one session of double filtration plasmapheresis, anti-blood group antibody titers were reduced 1:4 and 1:8 for IgG and IgM. Two days prior to surgery, patient underwent one session of plasma exchange and antibody titers were IgG 1:4 and IgM 1:8 on the day of KT. Basiliximab was administered for immune induction. The initial routine was performed with conventional end-to-side anastomosis between the renal graft artery and the right external iliac artery. However, pulsation of the transplant renal artery disappeared shortly. Upon opening the anastomosis, thrombosis at the anastomotic site was identified due to plaque embolism from the external iliac artery. Consequently, a self-expandable endovascular covered stent was implanted into the external iliac artery via the right femoral artery under intervention. Because part of the external iliac artery wall was defective, the endovascular stent was partially exposed, used the prosthetic graft for coverage and reinforcement. Finally, the renal allograft artery was anastomosed end-to-side to the stent-prosthetic complex. The anti-blood group antibody titers were 1:2 and 1:4 for IgG and IgM and serum creatinine was 124 μmol/L at 1 month. During the 2 years follow-up, graft function remained satisfactory, the serum creatinine levels were 116, 107, and 113 μmol/L at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years postoperatively, and no signs of right lower limb ischemia were evident. This study demonstrates that renal graft implanted on the endovascular stent is a feasible therapeutic option for recipients with severe iliac arteriosclerosis.

The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively.
