title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R.

RESULTS: BAFF-R on CD20- (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797-0.926, P = 7.17 × 10-5) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843-0.961, P = 1.57 × 10-3) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs.

CONCLUSION: This multi-omics genetic-toxicology study provides causal genetic evidence for immune-metabolite regulatory axes in AA pathogenesis. Notably, Adrenate presents dual biological effects: it transmits immune-protective signals but exerts direct vascular cellular toxicity. Our findings highlight the utility of MR-assisted precision toxicity prediction for disease risk evaluation and therapeutic target mining for AA.

title: Occult Patent Foramen Ovale Causing Severe Refractory Hypoxemia After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: After surgery for acute type A aortic dissection, pulmonary function can be reduced because of several possible causes. It is necessary to identify the main cause.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient experienced refractory hypoxemia following type A aortic dissection repair. Despite proper respiratory and inotropic support, and near-normal chest imaging, severe hypoxia persisted. Echocardiography revealed an occult patent foramen ovale (PFO) with significant right-to-left shunting, driven by positive-pressure mechanical ventilation and elevated right-sided cardiac pressures. Percutaneous transcatheter closure immediately improved oxygenation, enabling successful ventilator weaning.

DISCUSSION: Occult PFO should be suspected in unexplained postsurgical hypoxemia. Early echocardiographic evaluation and prompt percutaneous closure can rapidly reverse hypoxia, preventing prolonged mechanical ventilation and secondary complications.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent refractory hypoxemia after acute type A aortic dissection repair is not always pulmonary in origin. Occult PFO should be suspected and early echocardiographic confirmation with prompt PFO closure can produce immediate clinical improvement.

title: Hemodynamic changes after artificial vessel reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm: a case report.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Isolated iliac artery aneurysms (IIAA) frequently coexist with abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), yet their causal association remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed an aneurysm involving the entire left common iliac artery (48 mm × 55 mm × 81 mm). The patient was hemodynamically stable, with unremarkable physical examination and laboratory findings. He underwent aneurysm resection and aortoiliac reconstruction with a synthetic graft. Intraoperatively, arterial tortuosity and marked dilation at the bifurcation were noted. Postoperative CTA confirmed graft patency, and the patient recovered uneventfully. Preoperative and postoperative CTA scans were used for three-dimensional vascular reconstruction, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to assess hemodynamic parameters including wall shear stress (WSS), blood pressure, and flow velocity.

CONCLUSION: Prosthetic vascular reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) may produce dual hemodynamic effects on the abdominal aorta. While the causal link between CIAA and AAA is unproven, the surgery eliminates rupture risk of the target aneurysm. These exploratory results may provide hemodynamic references to optimize surgical planning for iliac artery aneurysms.

title: Social-biological misalignment modulates the prognostic impact of infarct volume after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT. Misalignment was quantified using a composite score incorporating occupational shift exposure and symptom onset timing. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the interaction between misalignment and final infarct volume on favorable 90-day outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2).

RESULTS: Misalignment was not independently associated with favorable outcome. However, a significant interaction was observed (OR = 9.70, 95% CI 1.74-54.10, LRT p = 0.008), remaining significant after FDR correction (q = 0.034), stable across profile likelihood and Firth penalized regression. The interaction improved model fit (AIC 124.35 → 119.38) and provided modest incremental net benefit. Exploratory threshold analysis suggested a potential inflection point approximating 25 mL, but this is hypothesis-generating and requires validation.

CONCLUSION: Misalignment does not exert a uniform adverse effect but acts as a state-dependent modifier, modifying the association between final infarct volume and favorable outcome. The interaction between chronobiological state and infarct burden offers a novel framework for understanding outcome heterogeneity.

We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT.

title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio.

title: Triglyceride-glucose index and the incidence of peripheral artery disease: a dose-response meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to June 28, 2026. Longitudinal observational studies evaluating the association between the conventional TyG index and incidents PAD in adults were eligible. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing the highest versus lowest TyG categories were calculated using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models. Linear and nonlinear dose-response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models.

RESULTS: Five longitudinal studies involving 417,499 participants and 7,800 incident PAD events were included. Compared with the lowest TyG category, a high TyG index was associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.49, 95% CI 1.06 to 2.10; p = 0.02), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 88.4%). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings. In the linear dose-response meta-analysis, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a 22% higher risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.37; p = 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall dose-response association (p = 0.001) with no evidence of nonlinearity (p for nonlinearity = 0.367), indicating an approximately linear relationship between the TyG index and PAD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher TyG index is associated with an increased risk of incident PAD in a dose-dependent and approximately linear manner.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261470450.

However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

title: Efficacy and safety of flow diverters for middle cerebral artery bifurcation aneurysms: a retrospective dual-center study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of flow diverters (FDs) for the treatment of middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation aneurysms.

METHODS: This retrospective, dual-center study enrolled 29 patients with unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysms treated with flow diverters (FDs) between January 2021 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), where scores of 0-2 indicated a favorable functional outcome. Aneurysm occlusion was evaluated at the 6-month follow-up using the O'Kelly-Marotta (OKM) grading scale on digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Procedure-related complications, including in-stent stenosis (ISS), were systematically recorded.

RESULTS: All 29 aneurysms were successfully treated with FD, with no technical failures, in-stent thrombosis, cerebral hemorrhage, or ischemic events observed during the perioperative period. No patients developed new neurological deficits before discharge. All patients were followed up via telephone and outpatient visits after discharge. Six-month angiographic follow-up was performed in all 29 patients by DSA. The follow-up duration ranged from 6 to 43.2 months. At the final follow-up, one patient developed vertigo and a transient episode of left limb weakness more than 2 months after treatment. The mRS score was 0 in 28 patients and 1 in one patient. The 6-month angiographic outcomes were: OKM Grade A in 1 patient (3.4%), Grade B in 5 (17.3%), Grade C in 7 (24.1%), and Grade D in 16 (55.2%). ISS was observed in 3 patients (10.3%): one moderate proximal, one moderate mid-stent, and one diffuse severe stenosis. The overall procedure-related complication rate was 3.4% (1/29), with a mortality rate of 0%. The probability of achieving complete occlusion was >88.8% for necks ≤ 3.0 mm, compared to >53.3% for necks between 3.0-5.0 mm.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that the use of FDs is an effective and safe therapeutic option for MCA bifurcation aneurysms. A neck diameter ≤ 5.0 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of complete occlusion; this association requires external validation.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of flow diverters (FDs) for the treatment of middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation aneurysms. METHODS: This retrospective, dual-center study enrolled 29 patients with unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysms treated with flow diverters (FDs) between January 2021 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), where scores of 0-2 indicated a favorable functional outcome.

title: Design of Monolithic Microcavities for Enhancing Organic Quantum Emitters.
abstract: Single organic molecules are a well-established platform for high-quality single-photon generation: they can emit lifetime-limited photons with high purity and indistinguishability. However, their emission is accompanied by a pronounced red-shifted phonon sideband and higher-order vibrational peaks, which reduce the fraction of photons emitted into the desired narrowband zero-phonon line. The standard approach to suppressing this unwanted emission is to integrate the emitter into a monolithic photonic nanostructure that provides Purcell enhancement. However, incorporating organic materials using clean-room techniques has proven challenging and has, in fact, so far prevented the integration of single molecules in crystalline hosts into monolithic microcavities. As a result, efficient, narrowband organic single-photon sources for applications in quantum information processing have remained elusive despite their considerable promise. Here, we propose three monolithic microcavity designs tailored to provide sufficient Purcell enhancement for organic quantum emitters. The Purcell effect induced by these cavities preferentially enhances emission into the 0-0 zero-phonon line, increasing spectral purity, photon extraction, and shortening the excited-state lifetime, which in turn relaxes the requirements for generating indistinguishable photons. The cavities have been optimized using Bayesian optimization and the adaptive Antoulas-Anderson (AAA) algorithm for rational approximation, which offer global optimization and the efficient reconstruction of spectra from scattering simulations, respectively. These structures are compatible with both standard clean-room processing and single-molecule preparation techniques. Therefore, they offer a clear route to realizing high-quality, practically monochromatic organic single-photon light sources.

The standard approach to suppressing this unwanted emission is to integrate the emitter into a monolithic photonic nanostructure that provides Purcell enhancement.

title: Emphysematous osteomyelitis of the lower extremity: Prevalence, imaging features, interobserver agreement and clinical outcomes in a 16-hospital cohort.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate emphysematous osteomyelitis (EO) observed prevalence, compare 3-month major adverse events (death or major amputation) between EO and nonemphysematous osteomyelitis (NEO), and assess interobserver agreement for key imaging features.

METHODS: In this retrospective 16-hospital study, radiology-report text screening followed by manual report review identified CT and MRI examinations demonstrating lower-extremity osteomyelitis. EO was defined as intraosseous gas without direct bone-to-air communication. Forty-five EO cases met criteria, and 180 NEO cases were randomly sampled in a 4:1 ratio for prognostic comparison. Associations with 3-month major adverse events were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Three radiologists independently reviewed 90 cases (45 EO, 45 NEO) to assess interobserver agreement.

RESULTS: Of the 1417 imaging examinations that identified lower-extremity osteomyelitis, 45 (3.2%) met the study's EO inclusion criteria. Major adverse events occurred within 3 months in 33.3% (15/45) of EO cases and 12.8% (23/180) of nonemphysematous osteomyelitis cases. EO (adjusted OR, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.46-7.12; p = .004) and peripheral artery disease (adjusted OR, 3.11; 95% CI, 1.38-7.03; p = .006) were independently associated with higher odds of death or major amputation within 3 months. Agreement for intraosseous gas was substantial on CT (κ = 0.71) and almost perfect on MRI (κ = 0.81).

CONCLUSION: EO is uncommon but associated with worse 3-month outcomes. Our findings support consideration of EO as a potential imaging marker of short-term adverse outcomes in patients with lower-extremity osteomyelitis.

METHODS: In this retrospective 16-hospital study, radiology-report text screening followed by manual report review identified CT and MRI examinations demonstrating lower-extremity osteomyelitis. EO was defined as intraosseous gas without direct bone-to-air communication.

title: Pipeline embolization device with adjunctive coiling for ruptured blood blister-like aneurysms: a multicenter study focusing on Hunt-Hess grade I-III patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood blister-like aneurysms (BBAs) of the internal carotid artery are rare and inherently unstable lesions that carry a high risk of rebleeding. Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of PED combined with adjunctive coil embolization using a deliberate loose-scaffolding strategy.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. Immediate complete angiographic occlusion (modified Raymond-Roy class I) was observed in 67.9% (19/28), increasing to 75.0% (21/28) overall at 12 months and reaching 95.5% (21/22) among those with available imaging follow-up. Notably, all seven patients with residual neck filling on immediate postoperative angiography who completed follow-up subsequently achieved complete occlusion. Favorable clinical outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) was recorded in 92.9% (26/28) at last follow-up. Perioperative complications occurred in 39.3% (11/28), predominantly neurological, including symptomatic vasospasm (21.4%, 6/28) and cerebral infarction (14.3%, 4/28); perioperative mortality was 3.6% (1/28).

CONCLUSION: PED-assisted coil embolization with a loose-scaffolding strategy is technically feasible and may yield favorable outcomes in selected patients with mild-to-moderate neurologic deficits. However, given the retrospective, single-arm design and modest sample size, these results are hypothesis-generating; prospective comparative studies are warranted.

Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs.

title: "Inflammation-Thrombosis Dissociation": a retrospective study of early DVT differences after UKA between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of early lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude, to analyze the relationships of inflammatory, hematologic, and coagulation indices with DVT, and to explore whether an "inflammation-thrombosis dissociation" phenomenon exists across ethnic groups.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3. Demographic characteristics, platelet count, hemoglobin, D-dimer, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were collected. Propensity score matching was used to control differences in age, sex, and body mass index, and Firth logistic regression was used to analyze factors associated with DVT.

RESULTS: Among the 147 patients, 14 developed postoperative DVT, for an overall incidence of 9.52%. The DVT incidence was 4.30% (4/93) in Tibetan patients, lower than the 18.52% (10/54) observed in Han Chinese patients (P = 0.007). Platelet count, D-dimer, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were all higher in Tibetan than in Han Chinese patients; however, these higher values did not correspond to a higher DVT incidence. After 1:1 matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 16 matched pairs were obtained; DVT incidences were 18.8% in Han Chinese patients and 0% in Tibetan patients. The difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.250), although the direction of the association was consistent with that before matching. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression showed that increasing age was associated with higher odds of DVT in Model 2 (OR = 1.110, 95% CI: 1.028-1.211, P = 0.007). In the primary model adjusted for age and BMI (Model 3), Tibetan ethnicity was associated with lower odds of DVT than Han Chinese ethnicity (OR = 0.206, 95% CI: 0.038-0.948, P = 0.042). However, this association was no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for sex (Model 4: OR = 0.243, 95% CI: 0.040-1.376, P = 0.109). In exploratory models separately incorporating postoperative platelet count, D-dimer, systemic immune-inflammation index, or aggregate index of systemic inflammation (Models 5-8), the association between ethnicity and DVT remained statistically significant (all P < 0.05), whereas none of these laboratory indices showed a statistically significant association with DVT (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Among high-altitude UKA patients receiving a uniform aspirin prophylaxis regimen, Han Chinese patients had a higher incidence of early postoperative DVT than Tibetan patients. Although Tibetan patients had higher platelet counts and composite inflammatory indices, these measures did not increase in parallel with DVT events, suggesting a possible dissociation between inflammatory phenotype and clinical thrombotic risk among different ethnic groups at high altitude. Age and ethnicity were relatively stable DVT-associated factors in this cohort, whereas platelet count, D-dimer, and platelet-inflammation composite indices were insufficient to explain the between-ethnicity difference in risk. Given the single-center retrospective design and the limited number of outcome events and matched patients, these findings require further validation in multicenter, large-sample prospective studies.

All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3.

title: Evaluating the Society for Vascular Surgery 90-Min Door-to-Intervention Target for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (rAAAs) are a life-threatening condition requiring rapid surgical intervention for survival. Guidelines from the Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) in 2018 advised a door-to-intervention time of ≤90 min. We hypothesized that door-to-intervention time would not predict outcomes following rAAA repair, as treatment timelines may reflect differences in physiological severity, diagnostic assessment and operative modality, including the use of endovascular repair (EVAR).

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 29 patients presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth who underwent surgical intervention for rAAA between February 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving the SVS-recommended door-to-intervention time of ≤90 min. Secondary outcomes were the rates of EVAR compared to open repair and the associated mortality and morbidity.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were included, of whom only three (10.3%) met the SVS target. Median door-to-intervention time was 182 min. Arrival-to-diagnosis time was associated with the greatest delay, with a median time of 84 min. Twenty-three patients (79.3%) underwent open repair, with a 60.9% (14/23) mortality rate compared to 16.7% (1/6) for EVAR cases. Shorter door-to-intervention time was associated with higher 30-day mortality, although no association was observed with overall mortality. Morbidity rates were 95.6% (22/23) for open cases and 50.0% (3/6) for EVAR cases. No statistically significant association was identified between overall morbidity rates and door-to-intervention time. However, higher grade complications were statistically significantly associated with both shorter arrival to diagnosis time (P = 0.011) and shorter arrival to knife-to-skin time (P = 0.039).

CONCLUSION: Overall, 89.7% (26/29) of rAAAs presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth between February 2018 and December 2024 exceeded the recommended SVS door-to-intervention target of ≤90 min. Shorter timelines were observed among patients with higher grade complications and who subsequently died. Mortality was higher following open repair. This study is limited due to its small sample size and retrospective methodology. Earlier identification of rAAAs could reduce door-to-intervention time; education, prealerting and optimized imaging pathways are potential methods for achieving this. These findings suggest that the SVS 90-minute threshold may have limited value as a standalone outcome-based quality metric and should be interpreted alongside measures of physiological severity and pathway performance. Expedited treatment is likely influenced by underlying hemodynamic instability. The development of validated risk stratification tools may be beneficial in determining modality of operation and timing.

Guidelines from the Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) in 2018 advised a door-to-intervention time of ≤90 min. We hypothesized that door-to-intervention time would not predict outcomes following rAAA repair, as treatment timelines may reflect differences in physiological severity, diagnostic assessment and operative modality, including the use of endovascular repair (EVAR).

title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database.

METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE.

This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database.

title: Evaluation of Total Patent Branch Vessel Ostial Area at Preoperative CT Angiography for Predicting Type II Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: Background Type II endoleak (T2EL) is a common complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) that may lead to aneurysm sac enlargement. Although guideline-based criteria are used to identify high-risk patients, their predictive accuracy remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the predictive value of preoperative total branch vessel ostial area at CT angiography (CTA) for T2EL after EVAR. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients undergoing EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) between January 2010 and December 2020. After exclusion of other endoleak types, CTA-derived anatomic parameters and outcomes were compared by isolated T2EL status. Total branch vessel ostial area was evaluated using prespecified Cox models and Cox-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis. Discrimination and reproducibility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Of 216 patients in this study (mean age, 66 years ± 7.6 [SD]; 190 male; median follow-up, 4.7 years), 86 (39.8%) developed T2EL. Total branch vessel ostial area showed excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.98-1.00) and was larger in patients with T2EL than in those without T2EL (median, 24.5 vs 11.7 mm2; P < .001). Sac enlargement was more frequent with T2EL (45.3% [39 of 86] vs 12.3% [16 of 130]; P < .001) and was associated with reintervention (hazard ratio [HR], 2.83; P = .003) but not overall survival (HR, 1.76; P = .28). In the fully adjusted Cox model, total branch vessel ostial area was associated with T2EL (HR, 1.06 per 1-mm2 increase [95% CI: 1.04, 1.08]; P < .001). Total branch ostial area showed better discrimination for T2EL than guideline-based criteria (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.82 vs 0.64; P < .001), with a Youden index-derived cutoff of 15.55 mm2. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive continuous association in T2EL risk with increasing ostial area (P < .001). Conclusion Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Liddell in this issue.

title: Hemorrhage Risk in Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations before and after Stereotactic Radiosurgery.
abstract: Background Whether stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is associated with lower hemorrhage risk for unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) during the latency period (ie, from SRS to complete AVM obliteration) remains controversial. Purpose To evaluate whether SRS is associated with lower hemorrhage risk in unruptured brain AVMs during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included 511 patients with unruptured brain AVMs at diagnosis treated with single-session SRS between June 1990 and May 2024. Hemorrhage rates before and after SRS were calculated using the person-year method. A time-dependent Cox proportional hazards model was used to assess the association between SRS and hemorrhage risk. The pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was calculated using the interval between diagnosis and SRS. Results For the 511 patients (median age, 39 years [IQR, 28-52 years]; 306 male patients), the total observation period from diagnosis to SRS or any prior treatment was 1009 person-years, and the pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was 3.4 per 100 person-years (34 hemorrhages). Among 477 patients who underwent SRS without a pre-SRS hemorrhage, 75 patients were lost to follow-up during the latency period, and the median latency period was 33 months, with a total of 1711 person-years. Hemorrhage occurred in 24 patients during the latency period, yielding an overall latency-period hemorrhage rate of 1.4 per 100 person-years. After adjustment for age, nidus volume, and venous drainage, time-dependent Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk in the post-SRS latency period compared with the pre-SRS period, corresponding to a 53% lower hazard (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47 [95% CI: 0.27, 0.83]; P = .009). SRS was also associated with lower hemorrhage risk in lesions treated with SRS following prior surgery or endovascular therapy (hazard ratio, 0.20; P = .01). Conclusion In patients with unruptured brain AVMs, SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Metabolic Equivalents and Cardiac Metrics Predict Delisting Better Than Traditional Frailty Measures and Enhance the Nationally Utilized Kidney Transplant Decision Aid.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular disease is the most common cause of death among kidney transplant waitlist patients. Cardiac and frailty information are not included in the scientific registry of transplant recipients kidney transplant decision aid (SRTR-KTDA) used to predict outcomes during transplant evaluation. We compared the predictiveness of an expanded model of kidney waitlist drop-off with the nationally utilized SRTR-KTDA.

METHODS: 239 variables related to patient demographics, frailty, and cardiac history/testing were collected for 312 Veterans consecutively listed for kidney transplant between 2015 and 2020. Analysis compared transplanted/listed patients versus delisted patients using bootstrapped stepwise logistic regression and Fine-Gray competing risk modeling that identified variables most consistently predictive of delisting for comparison with the SRTR-KTDA.

RESULTS: Predictors of delisting included treadmill METs, BNP, pulse, systolic blood pressure, history of angina, history of heart failure, calcium channel blocker use, angiotensin receptor blocker use, clonidine use, glomerulonephritis causing renal failure, > 70% left anterior descending artery stenosis on cardiac catheterization, and troponin. Within our population, the SRTR-KTDA model (age, sex, race, height, weight, blood type, cPRA, years on dialysis, diabetes, cancer history, peripheral artery disease) produced an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.65-0.716. Adding significant bootstrap variables to the SRTR-KTDA increased the AUC to 0.78-0.80.

CONCLUSIONS: All the information needed to predict delisting in our cohort can occur during a single evaluation visit including a robust history/physical exam, measurement of treadmill METs, and blood draw. The addition of cardiac information and METs significantly improved the predictiveness of the SRTR-KTDA. Optimally modeling waitlist outcomes is crucial since its 2025 introduction as a national transplant performance metric.

title: Bovine Pericardial Patch-Assisted Renal Artery Reconstruction in Living-Donor Kidney Transplantation: Technical Features, Vascular Safety, and Five-Year Outcomes in 88 Recipients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex renal arterial anatomy, short or small-caliber arteries, and procurement-related arterial injury can complicate living-donor kidney transplantation. We evaluated selective bovine pericardial patch-assisted reconstruction as a bench optimization strategy for anatomically unfavorable grafts.

METHODS: In a retrospective single-center cohort of 160 living-donor kidney transplants performed from December 2015 to October 2025, bovine pericardial patch-assisted reconstruction was used in 88 recipients when direct implantation or conventional reconstruction was considered less favorable. Technical indications, reconstruction configuration, vascular events, renal function, and survival were analyzed.

RESULTS: Twenty-six grafts had at least 2 anatomical renal arteries. Additional indications included early arterial division, short artery, small-caliber artery, polar artery, unfavorable ostial geometry, and procurement-related arterial injury. A single final recipient arterial anastomosis was achieved in 87 recipients (98.9%) and 25 of 26 multiple-artery grafts (96.2%). Clinically relevant vascular events occurred in 2 recipients (2.3%): one stenosis treated by stenting and one pseudoaneurysm requiring endovascular exclusion and graft nephrectomy. Model-estimated mean eGFR increased from 54.2 to 60.4 mL/min/1.73 m2 between 1 month and 5 years. Five-year patient, death-censored graft, and overall graft survival were 97.7%, 93.1%, and 90.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: In selected living-donor grafts with unfavorable arterial anatomy, bovine pericardial patch reconstruction provided an immediately available biological platform for Carrel-like inflow creation and simplified recipient implantation. The technique should be viewed as one option among established reconstructive strategies and selected according to anatomy, local tissue availability, and surgical expertise.

We evaluated selective bovine pericardial patch-assisted reconstruction as a bench optimization strategy for anatomically unfavorable grafts. METHODS: In a retrospective single-center cohort of 160 living-donor kidney transplants performed from December 2015 to October 2025, bovine pericardial patch-assisted reconstruction was used in 88 recipients when direct implantation or conventional reconstruction was considered less favorable.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for the detection of acute aortic syndrome in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic disorders with a wide range of presentations that are easily misdiagnosed in the emergency department (ED). The 2024 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines recommended focused transthoracic echocardiography as the first-line imaging tool for the detection of aortic dissection, but the performance of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in detecting AAS in ED varies considerably in the existing literature. We aim to gather and synthesize existing studies to provide a more comprehensive overview of the diagnostic accuracy and value of POCUS for the detection of AAS and its generalizability in the ED setting. METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2025. Diagnostic accuracy studies of POCUS in the ED for the detection of AAS were included. For included studies, the diagnostic accuracy of POCUS for detecting AAS was revealed by calculating the sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratio, and diagnostic odds ratio, with 95% credible intervals (CrI). The diagnostic performance of POCUS was evaluated by summary receiver operator curve (SROC). RESULTS: A total of 4,855 patients from seven studies were included in the meta-analysis. For any sonographic signs for detecting AAS, the pooled sensitivity and specificity of POCUS were 88.3% (95%CrI: 85.1% -91.2%) and 80.3% (95%CrI: 63.4%-92.9%), respectively. The area under the SROC of any sonographic signs for detecting AAS was 0.91 (95%CrI: 0.65-0.96). CONCLUSION: This systematic review provides support that POCUS may be a useful early imaging tool for ruling in AAS in the ED due to its high specificity for direct sonographic sign. While the overall certainty of evidence is moderate to low, larger-scale prospective studies on the use of POCUS with other diagnostic tools for detecting AAS are necessary in ED settings.

title: Stable In-Hospital Mortality Despite Increasing Thrombectomy Use in Young Adults With Ischemic Stroke: A Nationwide Study in Spain (2016-2022).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) in young adults is increasing in incidence and carries a disproportionate socioeconomic burden. The adoption of reperfusion therapies, particularly mechanical thrombectomy, has transformed stroke care; however, their impact on mortality in this low-risk population remains uncertain.

METHODS: We performed a nationwide, population-based retrospective study using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS), including all hospital admissions for IS in patients aged 18-50 years from 2016 to 2022. Temporal trends in admissions, reperfusion therapies, and in-hospital mortality were assessed. Independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 20,533 admissions, the number of hospitalizations increased over time, accompanied by a rise in reperfusion therapies. Mechanical thrombectomy rates nearly doubled from 6.3% in 2016 to 12.1% in 2022 (p < 0.001). Despite this expansion, in-hospital mortality remained low and stable throughout the study period (2.8%). Mortality was independently associated with malignant neoplasm (OR 8.45), followed by orotracheal intubation (OR 4.85), coma (OR 3.73), cerebral edema (OR 2.16), acute kidney injury (OR 1.85), acute respiratory failure (OR 1.38), posterior circulation stroke (OR 1.42), and All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Groups (APR-DRG) mortality risk level (all p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In young adults with IS, the expansion of reperfusion therapies was not associated with reduced in-hospital mortality, which remained low over time. Malignant neoplasm was the strongest independent predictor of death, followed by acute neurological complications and organ dysfunction. These findings highlight the need for further multicentre clinical research to better understand the causes of death in young adults with IS.

The adoption of reperfusion therapies, particularly mechanical thrombectomy, has transformed stroke care; however, their impact on mortality in this low-risk population remains uncertain. METHODS: We performed a nationwide, population-based retrospective study using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS), including all hospital admissions for IS in patients aged 18-50 years from 2016 to 2022.

title: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience in Pediatric Thromboembolism: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020. Incidentally detected asymptomatic thromboses and cases without imaging confirmation were excluded. Venous and arterial events were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 51,025 pediatric admissions, 70 patients had thromboembolism, corresponding to an admission-based rate of 13.7 per 10,000 admissions. Venous thromboembolism accounted for 51 cases (72.9%) and arterial thromboembolism for 19 cases (27.1%). Median age at diagnosis was 6 years (range, 1 day-18 years), and 49 patients (70.0%) were male. The central nervous system was the most frequent anatomical region involved. Central venous catheterization was the leading modifiable acquired risk factor. Active antithrombotic or interventional treatment was used in 68 patients (97.1%); low molecular weight heparin containing regimens were used in 46 patients (65.7%). Complete recovery was documented in 55 patients (78.6%), recurrence in 12 (17.1%), and mortality in 3 (4.3%). Recurrence was more frequent after venous than arterial events (23.5% vs 0%; p = .028).

CONCLUSION: In this 10-year cohort, venous events predominated and catheter related thrombosis remained a major preventable contributor. Recurrence was confined to venous events, supporting careful long term follow up and individualized secondary prevention for high risk children. Standardized catheter care practices and selective, appropriately timed thrombophilia testing are practical priorities.

This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020.

title: Frailty as a Modifier of Revascularization-Associated Outcomes in Diabetic Foot Ulcer: A Nationwide Inpatient Study.
abstract: We examined whether frailty modifies the association between revascularization and major amputation among hospitalizations for diabetic foot ulcer. We identified adult hospitalizations in the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 through 2022 and classified frailty using the 109-code Hospital Frailty Risk Score. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed major amputation and in-hospital mortality across four frailty strata, adjusting for demographic and clinical characteristics. Among 2 588 159 diabetic foot ulcer hospitalizations, frailty burden exceeded that of diabetes hospitalizations without foot ulcers. The association between revascularization and major amputation weakened with increasing frailty: adjusted odds ratios were 0.30 (95% confidence interval, 0.26-0.35) for low frailty, 0.68 for intermediate frailty and 0.82 for intermediate-high frailty. No statistically significant association was observed for high frailty (adjusted odds ratio, 1.05; 95% confidence interval, 0.86-1.29; interaction p < 0.001). Revascularization was associated with lower in-hospital mortality across frailty strata without significant interaction (p = 0.413). Frailty modified the observed association with major amputation, whereas mortality associations showed limited heterogeneity. Treatment selection and unmeasured clinical differences preclude causal interpretation.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.

title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ. Methods: This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results. Results: The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%CI:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase. Conclusions: The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

Methods: This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026.

title: ChatGPT's and Claude's responses to patient questions on deep vein thrombosis.
abstract:
AIM: To compare ChatGPT's and Claude's responses to frequently asked patient questions about deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in terms of expert-rated accuracy, comprehensibility, and unnecessary detail.

METHODS: We compiled 33 Turkish questions about DVT from online sources and clinical experience. The questions were posed to ChatGPT and Claude in separate sessions, and the models' unedited responses were collected. Three blinded cardiovascular surgeons independently evaluated each answer on a 1-5 Likert scale across three domains: accuracy, comprehensibility, and unnecessary detail. We compared average answer lengths and domain scores using paired statistical tests.

RESULTS: The mean lengths of the responses did not differ significantly between the models (139.7±49.4 words vs 145.67±25.41 words; P=0.490). ChatGPT had a higher median rater-averaged comprehensibility score (4.33 vs 4.00; raw P=0.002). In the principal rater-averaged analyses, the models did not significantly differ in accuracy (Holm-adjusted P=0.085), whereas ChatGPT received significantly higher scores for comprehensibility and unnecessary detail (Holm-adjusted P=0.006 for both).

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest potential differences in the presentation of patient-facing information rather than overall clinical superiority of any model. AI-generated medical information should continue to be reviewed by qualified health care professionals.

title: Techniques for Sharp Recanalization of Thoracic Central Venous Occlusions.
abstract: Although the majority of Thoracic Central Venous Occlusions (TCVOs) can be successfully crossed using conventional recanalization techniques, refractory lesions may require sharp recanalization techniques (SRT) to achieve technical success. This article presents a practical, step-by-step approach to sharp recanalization of TCVOs, with emphasis on patient selection, procedural planning, device selection, and strategies to minimize complications. SRT methods are discussed, highlighting technical principles that underpin safe and effective procedures. Technical pearls, bailout strategies, and complication prevention and management are reviewed, along with expected outcomes and follow-up considerations. This manuscript serves as a practical "how-to" guide for interventionalists managing complex TCVOs.

title: Nurse-led, multidisciplinary strategies to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections: Parenteral nutrition stewardship and central venous access device maintenance.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs) remain a major source of preventable patient harm and are associated with increased mortality, longer hospital stays, and higher health care costs. Reducing central venous access device (CVAD) utilization and improving line maintenance practices are key strategies for prevention.

PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care.

METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, an interprofessional team implemented a PN clinical decision tree, standardized PN administration kit, targeted nursing education, daily multidisciplinary line rounds, and real-time escalation processes. Outcomes included CLABSI Standardized Infection Ratio (SIR), Standardized Utilization Ratio (SUR), PN-related CLABSIs, and adherence to line care practices.

RESULTS: The initiative was associated with a 46% reduction in CLABSI SIR (1.165-0.632), an 11.7% reduction in CVAD utilization (SUR 0.479-0.423; P < .001), and a decrease in PN-related CLABSIs from 45% to 12.5% of all CLABSI cases. Process-related issues identified during rounds decreased from 32.73% to 26.11%.

CONCLUSIONS: A nurse-led, multidisciplinary approach combining PN stewardship, standardized CVAD care, and real-time feedback improved patient safety and reduced CLABSI risk. The model offers a sustainable, replicable strategy for infection prevention.

Reducing central venous access device (CVAD) utilization and improving line maintenance practices are key strategies for prevention. PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care.

title: Midterm outcomes with extended follow-up of open and endovascular repair of visceral artery aneurysms using a target-artery preservation strategy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of visceral artery aneurysms is heterogeneous, and sacrifice of the target vessel is frequently accepted. This study reports a single-center experience of visceral artery aneurysm treatment aiming for target-artery preservation.

METHODS: All consecutive elective open and endovascular visceral artery aneurysm repairs performed with the intent of aneurysm exclusion and target-artery preservation between January 2016 and April 2025 were retrospectively analyzed; minimum follow-up was 1 year. The primary end point was treatment success (visceral artery aneurysm exclusion + target-artery patency). Secondary end points included primary treatment failure and analysis of associated factors. Time-to-event outcomes were survival, freedom from reinterventions, and freedom from loss of treatment success; patients exceeding 5 years were described separately.

RESULTS: Forty patients were included; the splenic artery was the most frequent location (45%). Primary treatment success was achieved in 36 of 40 patients (90%): 10 of 10 (100%) after open and 26 of 30 (87%) after endovascular repair; after 4 conversions (3 splenic artery), assisted treatment success was 37 of 40 (93%). No organ ischemia, splenectomy, or 30-day death occurred. Splenic failures were associated with moderate-to-severe calcification (P = .011) and severe tortuosity (P = .027). At median follow-up of 48 months, 5-year survival was 90 ± 6%, freedom from reintervention was 94 ± 4%, and freedom from loss of treatment success was 100%. Whole-cohort 7-year survival was 79 ± 9%; no reintervention occurred beyond 2 years.

CONCLUSION: Visceral artery aneurysm exclusion with target-artery preservation is feasible, safe, and durable at midterm after open and endovascular repair, with encouraging long-term observations. In this small series, severe tortuosity and calcification of the proximal splenic artery were associated with endovascular failure.

This study reports a single-center experience of visceral artery aneurysm treatment aiming for target-artery preservation. METHODS: All consecutive elective open and endovascular visceral artery aneurysm repairs performed with the intent of aneurysm exclusion and target-artery preservation between January 2016 and April 2025 were retrospectively analyzed; minimum follow-up was 1 year.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Thrombin Injection for Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysms: Predictors of Failure and Recurrence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided thrombin injection (UGTI) is effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, but factors associated with early failure and recurrence remain incompletely defined. We evaluated treatment outcomes and their predictors.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients treated with UGTI between November 2023 and May 2026. Technical success was defined as immediate complete thrombosis after the first injection, clinical success as complete thrombosis at 24-hour Doppler follow-up, and recurrence as recanalization at 24 hours after technical success. Independent associations with clinical failure and recurrence were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 204 patients (94.4%), clinical success in 176 (81.5%), and recurrence occurred in 31 of 204 patients (15.2%). Overall success without surgical or endovascular repair was 94.0%. Therapeutic index procedures (odds ratio [OR], 6.368; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.037-19.910), international normalized ratio (INR) >1.5 (OR, 5.286; 95% CI, 1.681-16.625), shorter neck length (OR per mm, 0.879; 95% CI, 0.802-0.964), a longer procedure-to-UGTI interval (OR per day, 1.041; 95% CI, 1.008-1.074), and platelet count <150,000/μL (OR, 3.407; 95% CI, 1.174-9.884) were independently associated with clinical failure. Therapeutic procedures (OR, 7.670; 95% CI, 2.094-28.090) and INR >1.5 (OR, 3.653; 95% CI, 1.114-11.982) independently predicted recurrence. No procedure-related complications occurred.

CONCLUSION: UGTI was highly effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, with high immediate and overall success and no observed complications. Procedural, anatomical, temporal, and hemostatic factors were associated with outcomes, while clinical failure and recurrence represented distinct treatment phases. These findings may support risk-adapted surveillance.

We evaluated treatment outcomes and their predictors. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients treated with UGTI between November 2023 and May 2026.

title: Effect of a Nurse-Driven Early Mobilization Protocol on Biomarker Levels and Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower Extremity Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023 to June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n = 107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n = 98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff. Outcomes included postoperative DVT incidence, changes in D-dimer and C-reactive protein (CRP), bed rest duration, pain scores, length of stay, and complications. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) compared biomarker changes; binary logistic regression identified DVT risk factors.

RESULTS: The early mobilization group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative DVT than the control group (7.14% vs. 19.63%, P = 0.009), with an absolute risk reduction of 12.49% and a relative risk reduction of 63.6%. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant between-group effects (F = 22.33, P < 0.001) and interaction effects (F = 6.36, P < 0.001) for CRP levels. After Bonferroni correction, the early mobilization group had significantly lower D-dimer and CRP levels at 1 week postoperatively and at discharge than the control group (P < 0.0125). The early mobilization group also had significantly better outcomes in terms of bed rest duration (5.86 ± 1.69 days vs. 6.38 ± 1.54 days, P = 0.021), numerical rating scale score on postoperative day 3 (3.27 ± 1.15 vs. 4.54 ± 1.47, P < 0.001), and length of hospital stay (median 11.00 days vs. 13.00 days, P < 0.001), as well as a lower complication rate (6.12% vs. 14.95%, P = 0.041). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the early mobilization protocol (odds ratio [OR] = 0.27, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.10-0.73, P = 0.009), age (OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08, P = 0.001), and postoperative day 1 D-dimer level (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.47, P = 0.011) as independent factors influencing postoperative DVT.

CONCLUSION: A nurse-driven early mobilization protocol effectively reduces the incidence of DVT after lower extremity fracture surgery, improves coagulation and inflammatory biomarker levels, shortens hospital stay, and does not increase complication risks. The protocol is safe and feasible and can be recommended as an adjunctive measure for venous thromboembolism prevention after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023 to June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n = 107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n = 98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff.

title: Intraoperative estimated blood loss and perioperative transfusion are independently associated with postoperative morbidity and mortality after lower-extremity bypass.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower-extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve, 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite end point. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.

RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL, and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 1.26; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.59], MI (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.48-2.39), stroke (aOR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.09-2.29), and the composite outcome (aOR 1.51, 95% CI, 1.29-1.78). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.46; 95% CI, 1.95-3.10), MI (aOR, 6.57; 95% CI, 5.26-8.21), stroke (aOR, 2.75; 95% CI, 1.84-4.12), and the composite outcome (aOR, 4.08; 95% CI, 3.48-4.78). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.09-3.08), MI (aOR, 7.39; 95% CI, 6.08-8.98), stroke (aOR, 3.79; 95% CI, 2.76-5.21), and the composite outcome (aOR, 4.42; 95% CI, 3.87-5.05). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower-extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

title: Carotid endarterectomy versus transcarotid artery revascularization for asymptomatic carotid stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method that involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.

METHODS: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/MEDLINE, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy," "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR." Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.

RESULTS: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method that involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system.

title: Use and Safety of Peripherally Inserted Venous Catheters Versus Central Venous Catheters for Patients With Lymphoma Receiving Frontline Anthracycline-based Chemotherapy.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVs) for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy have the potential risk of vascular and tissue injury due to extravasation of vesicant agents. Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.

METHODS: We conducted a RWA across 9 US medical centers, including adults with newly diagnosed lymphoma who received anthracycline-based chemotherapy via PIV or CVC between 2010 and 2025. Detailed baseline characteristics and safety outcomes were collected, applying standard definitions for extravasation and other recognized complications. Incidence rates of safety outcomes were calculated, and multivariable Poisson regression models were applied to adjust for confounders.

RESULTS: In total, 1776 patients were included: 1077 with CVCs, 886 with PIVs, and 187 with both. The most common diagnoses were large B-cell lymphomas, followed by Hodgkin lymphoma, and then T-cell lymphoma. In total, there were 5464 and 4049 treatment cycles in the CVC and PIV cohorts, respectively. There was one definite case of extravasation with PIV use (incidence rate 0.19 events per 1000 infusion-cycles), compared to no cases with CVC use. PIV use was more commonly associated with flare, phlebitis, and pain, whereas CVC use was more commonly associated with deep vein thrombosis; other complications were not different between cohorts. Rates of extravasation and other complications were low in both PIV and CVC cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Altogether, PIVs represent a viable modality for patients with lymphoma requiring anthracycline-based chemotherapy.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVs) for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy have the potential risk of vascular and tissue injury due to extravasation of vesicant agents. Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.
