title: Machine learning assisted thermal reperfusion mapping reveals real-time changes in foot microcirculation during endovascular revascularisation.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test the feasibility of a novel thermal perfusion imaging and mapping system to show microcirculatory changes of plantar foot angiosomes during endovascular procedures.

METHODS: A prospective, exploratory MedTech development study was designed to test the system in a series of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Intraprocedural video thermography was performed using a 320 × 240 pixel resolution, thermal camera. Initial analysis was manual, re- positioning regions of interest (ROIs) within each of five plantar foot angiosomes. Subsequent automation using deep learning segmentation allowed ROI tracking from initial frame to procedure end. Isotherms (thermal contours) created and applied to the segmented surface provide quantitative, real-time changes in the percentage distribution of isotherms overlying both treated and contralateral foot angiosomes during the procedure.

RESULTS: Of 23 participants recruited, video thermography was obtained in 21 patients admitted with moderate-severe disease complexity; femoral-popliteal segment only (n = 13), femoral-popliteal and infrapopliteal disease (n = 5) and infrapopliteal disease only (n = 3). Changes in percentage distribution of each isotherm overlay revealed two broad groups; plantar foot thermal perfusion responders (n = 12) and non-responders (n = 9). In responders, revascularisation led to a series of 'dynamic' phases where temperature increased in one, or more, angiosomes; 'hottest' isotherms expanded significantly (p = .002) in response to endovascular procedures. In thermal perfusion non-responders, no significant change in isotherm percentage distribution was observed.

CONCLUSION: Thermal perfusion imaging is feasible using the novel implemented deep learning system. Clinicians can gain insight about microcirculatory changes at foot angiosomes in response to treatment based on three parameters; (i) temporal temperature profiles of each angiosome, (ii) real-time changes in the percentage distribution of isotherms across the plantar surface during the intervention, (iii) angiosome-specific cutaneous perfusion responses to balloon inflation and/or stent deployment. For patients with diabetes, locating the site of improved skin reperfusion has potential to predict treatment success for healing outcomes at the ulcer/woundosome.

METHODS: A prospective, exploratory MedTech development study was designed to test the system in a series of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Intraprocedural video thermography was performed using a 320 × 240 pixel resolution, thermal camera.

title: Maternal Mortality Across a Multi-Hospital Health System in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study (2016-2024).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains a pressing global health challenge and is a vital indicator of healthcare quality. Despite improvements in Saudi Arabia, preventable maternal fatalities continue to occur, with insufficient research on regional disparities.

OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to assess the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and its causes across five hospitals within the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs in Saudi Arabia and evaluate it is main causes,thereby addressing a gap in maternal mortality data in the Gulf region.

METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, descriptive study included all maternal deaths occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days postpartum between 2016 and 2024 across five National Guard hospitals in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam. Data were extracted from hospital records and analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 28.

RESULTS: Eighteen maternal deaths were identified over the nine-year period, yielding an overall MMR of 6.2 per 100,000 live births (mean age at death 29.8 ± 6.3 years). MMR varied considerably by year, from 0.00/100,000 in 2017 to 37.5/100,000 in 2020. Pregnancy-related complications accounted for 50% of deaths (9/18), most commonly venous thromboembolism (66.7%). Non-obstetric causes included COVID-19 (16.7%), unknown cause (16.7%), brain tumor (5.6%), and myocarditis (5.6%). Most deaths occurred in women with parity 1-3 (61.1%), split evenly between vaginal and caesarean delivery (50% each). Geographic variation was marked: Riyadh recorded deaths in most years with a peak in 2020; Dammam and Al-Ahsa each showed sporadic extreme spikes; Jeddah showed intermittent elevations; no deaths occurred in Madinah.

CONCLUSION: The overall MMR at these hospitals is comparatively low to global figures, significant variations across different cities and years, alongside a notable number of deaths with unspecified causes, underscore the need for standardized mortality reviews, autopsy confirmations for suspected embolic deaths, and continuous targeted monitoring.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: An NHANES Cohort Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥ 40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI ≤ 0.90. An NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up 10 steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment.

RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (odds ratio [OR] 1.748, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.218-2.510; P = 0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (hazards ratio [HR] 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P = 0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P = 0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P = 0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability.

CONCLUSION: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥ 40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI ≤ 0.90.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD).

METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs. 6.6% vs. 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend = 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively).

CONCLUSION: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short-term and long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

title: Guideline-to-Practice Gap in Ankle-Brachial Index Screening Among Inpatients with Newly Documented Lower Extremity Wounds.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to 2 hospitals within a single urban academic health system in 2025 with a new lower extremity wound documented in nursing wound flowsheets. Recent screening was defined as ABI testing performed during the index hospitalization or within 1 year prior to admission. Patient and admission characteristics were compared by screening status, and logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with screening. Wound location and noninvasive vascular testing results were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 2,244 inpatients with newly documented lower extremity wounds, 343 patients (15.3%) were screened with ABIs. Screened patients were younger (65 vs.69 years; P < 0.001) and had a higher burden of atherosclerotic or diabetic comorbidities. After multivariable adjustment, pre-existing PAD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.79; P < 0.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR, 2.72; P < 0.001), and end-stage renal disease (aOR, 1.60; P = 0.021) were independently associated with ABI screening. Female sex was associated with lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.73; P = 0.045). Compared with medicine or hospitalist services, admission to general surgery/acute care surgery (aOR, 2.15; P = 0.002) and vascular surgery (aOR, 4.29; P < 0.001) was associated with higher odds of screening. Screening proportions were 23.6% for toe wounds, 20.6% for ankle/Achilles wounds, 19.9% for foot/heel wounds, and 12.8% for lower leg wounds. Among screened patients with available measurements, 50.4% had an abnormal ABI, 63.8% had an abnormal TBI, and 69.0% had at least 1 abnormal ABI or TBI.

CONCLUSION: PAD screening was performed in a minority of hospitalized patients with newly documented lower extremity wounds and was associated with recognized vascular risk factors and admitting service. Abnormal physiologic testing was common among screened patients. Standardized wound-triggered screening pathways may reduce missed opportunities for vascular evaluation.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Primary Femoropopliteal Stents: A Retrospective Multicenter Experience and the Role for a Doppler Ultrasound Surveillance Program.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularization is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating reintervention, remains a challenge. This study performs a retrospective outcomes analysis to suggest which patient populations may benefit from a Doppler ultrasound (DUS) surveillance program in improving primary patency and amputation-free survival following femoropopliteal stenting in patients with PAD.

METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients who underwent femoropopliteal stenting between January 2015 and April 2023 within a vascular network with 6 hospital sites. Data were collected from 238 stents in 220 patients. Demographics, stent characteristics, and surveillance protocols were analyzed. Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models were used to identify risk factors for primary patency and amputation-free survival. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated for both outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to compare outcomes between suprapopliteal and infrapopliteal stents.

RESULTS: A total of 238 stents were inserted in a population in which 28.6% were women, with the median age of 72.5 ± 11.5 years. In 74.8% (178) of cases, patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Primary patency rates at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years were 90%, 67.7%, 51.2%, 26.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. The average amputation-free survival was 3.2 years. Cox regression identified CLTI (hazard ratio, 6.37, P = 0.001), type 1 diabetes mellitus (hazard ratio, 3.16, P = 0.006), and female sex (hazard ratio, 1.69, P = 0.037) as significant predictors of loss of primary patency. Drug-eluting stents and diabetes were associated with poorer amputation-free survival.

CONCLUSION: The study illustrates a cohort of high-risk patients, particularly those with CLTI and diabetes, who may benefit from future enrollment in an enhanced DUS surveillance program targeted to improve long-term outcomes. However, further research is required to explore the clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and implementation feasibility of such programs in clinical practice.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularization is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating reintervention, remains a challenge.

title: Five-Year Outcomes of Covered Stent-Graft Repair for Traumatic and Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Injuries.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular repair with covered stent grafts offers a prompt and effective strategy to manage lower-extremity arterial trauma and catheterization-related iatrogenic vascular complications. However, long-term durability and late complication profiles of covered stent grafts in the femoral segments remain poorly defined. The aim of the study was to evaluate the long-term outcomes of covered stent-grafting for traumatic and iatrogenic injuries of the common, superficial, and deep femoral arteries over a 5-year follow-up period.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 58 consecutive patients (40 males [69.0%]; mean age: 57 ± 13.6 years) who underwent endovascular repair for femoral arterial injuries between August 2011 and August 2021 were analyzed. The primary outcome was the 5-year primary patency rate. Secondary outcomes included primary-assisted and secondary patency rates and subgroup comparisons of patency based on stent-graft type, lesion type, and injury type.

RESULTS: Etiologies included iatrogenic injury in 36 patients (62.1%) and traumatic injury in 22 patients (37.9%). Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. The overall 5-year Kaplan-Meier estimates for primary, primary-assisted, and secondary patency rates were 72.4%, 91.4%, and 94.8%, respectively, with a mean primary patency duration of 52 months. Log-rank tests demonstrated no statistically significant differences in primary patency rates across stent-graft types (P = 0.942), lesion types (P = 0.751), or injury types (P = 0.864).

CONCLUSION: In appropriately selected patients, covered stent-graft repair was associated with high technical success, low observed complication rates, and favorable long-term patency for traumatic and iatrogenic femoral arterial injuries.

However, long-term durability and late complication profiles of covered stent grafts in the femoral segments remain poorly defined. The aim of the study was to evaluate the long-term outcomes of covered stent-grafting for traumatic and iatrogenic injuries of the common, superficial, and deep femoral arteries over a 5-year follow-up period.

title: Brachial Plexus Injuries from Overhead Arm Positioning During F/BEVAR: A Case Series and Call for Standardized Technique.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR.

METHODS: All consecutive patients undergoing F/BEVAR performed with bilateral overhead arm positioning at Uppsala Univerity Hospital between 2023 and 2025 were included in this retrospecive cohort study. Neutral head position, padded overhead support, and abduction limited to ≤90° were used in accordance with standardized positioning protocols. Demographic, comorbidity, and procedural data were accessed from the clinical records. The primary aim was to evaluate the rate of postoperative UES and brachial plexus injury (BPI). In cases with BPI, neurological consultation and rehabilitation outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 67 patients who underwent F/BEVAR with bilateral overhead arm position, 6 patients (9.0%) developed postoperative UES. Two patients (3.0%) had neurologist-confirmed BPI; one developed bilateral palsy with partial recovery after 8 weeks, whereas the other developed unilateral palsy with complete recovery by 3 months. Neither patient required surgical intervention, The remaining 4 patients (6.0%) experienced minor transient UES. There was no difference in baseline parameters between patients with and without UES. Urgent repair was more frequent among patients experiencing any UES than among those without UES (50.0% vs. 9.8%; P = 0.028). Both patients with BPI underwent procedures lasting >180 min. Procedural technical success was 98.5%, and in-hospital mortality 1.5%.

CONCLUSION: Bilateral overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR was associated with a measurable incidence of UES. Although most symptoms were transient and resolved without intervention, clinically significant BPI occurred in a small proportion of patients despite standardized positioning. These findings support cautious and selective use of prolonged overhead arm positioning and warrant prospective evaluation of safe positioning duration and patient-related susceptibility.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR.

title: Comparative Perioperative Outcomes of Rescue Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair Versus Open Repair for Failed Endovascular Aortic Repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Redo aortic repair following previous endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is often technically challenging and associated with significant morbidity. Technologic advances in custom-modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there are limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches.

METHODS: The National Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients undergoing elective open abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair or fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) with a physician-modified endografts (PMEG) or custom manufactured devices (CMD) following a previous EVAR from 2010 to 2024. A univariate analysis to compare groups was completed with chi square and Fisher's exact t-test, and outcomes were compared using multivariate logistic and linear regression. Data were analyzed using STATA.

RESULTS: A total of 900 patients underwent open repair, and 651 patients underwent FEVAR following previous EVAR. Using multivariate linear regression, patients undergoing open repair had an increased risk of postoperative pneumonia (odds ratio [OR] 6.23, P = 0.001), postoperative reintubation (OR 2.01, P = 0.005), and major adverse cardiac events (OR 2.16, P = 0.001) compared to patients undergoing FEVAR. Patients undergoing open repair had a higher risk of mortality (OR 2.02, P = 0.018) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR 0.47, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Complex endovascular rescue of previously failed EVAR is associated with a decreased rate of perioperative complications compared to an open approach. FEVAR using PMEGs or CMDs may be considered as a viable option in patients who are undergoing elective redo AAA repair following a failed EVAR.

Technologic advances in custom-modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there are limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches.

title: Long-Term Patency and Clinical Outcomes after Retrograde Mesenteric Bypass for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic mesenteric ischemia is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centers, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass.

METHODS: We evaluated 34 patients treated with retrograde mesenteric bypass for chronic mesenteric ischemia between 2009 and 2024. Patency rates were measured with Kaplan-Meier analysis. Thrombosis was classified as early (≤30 days), mid-term (31-365 days), or late (>365 days).

RESULTS: Superior mesenteric artery bypass was performed in 33 patients (97.1%), celiac bypass in 25 (73.5%), and dual-vessel reconstruction in 24 (70.6%). Median follow-up was 2,737 days (interquartile range, 1,760-4,353), approximately 7.5 years. No early thrombosis occurred. Two mid-term and three late occlusions were observed. Primary patency rates were 93.3% at 1 and 3 years, 89.4% at 5 years, and 85.0% at 10 years. Clinical symptoms resolved after revascularization in all patients surviving the perioperative period, and no recurrent symptoms were documented during follow-up. No patient required reintervention.

CONCLUSION: Retrograde mesenteric bypass was associated with stable long-term patency, sustained symptom resolution, and low perioperative mortality. It remains a durable open surgical option for chronic mesenteric ischemia, particularly when endovascular revascularization is not feasible or is unlikely to provide durable results.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Chronic mesenteric ischemia is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centers, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass.

title: A Scoping Review on Artificial Intelligence for Image-Based Analysis in Aortic Aneurysm Care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance automated image analysis, quantitative assessment, and clinical decision-making in aortic aneurysm care. This scoping review aims to summarize the current cumulative body of evidence.

METHODS: A systematic PubMed search identified 661 records, with 59 studies ultimately included after deduplication and multistage screening based on predefined eligibility criteria, focusing on original research applying AI to medical imaging in aortic aneurysm care. Data were extracted on study design, imaging modality, AI methodology, validation, and dataset characteristics.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Deep learning approaches, particularly U-Net-based architectures, were the most frequently applied methods, with AI primarily used for automated segmentation and quantitative analysis of aortic pathology. AI models achieved high technical performance across applications, including vessel segmentation, aneurysm detection, endoleak identification, and risk prediction, with reported improvements in efficiency and diagnostic accuracy. However, external validation, multimodal data integration, and prospective clinical evaluation remained uncommon.

CONCLUSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential to enhance aortic aneurysm disease assessment through accurate image analysis, automated quantification, and improved procedural support. However, current limitations include a lack of external validation, reporting transparency, and clinical integration.

This scoping review aims to summarize the current cumulative body of evidence. METHODS: A systematic PubMed search identified 661 records, with 59 studies ultimately included after deduplication and multistage screening based on predefined eligibility criteria, focusing on original research applying AI to medical imaging in aortic aneurysm care.

title: One-Year Sac Regression after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated with Favorable Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression.

METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent nonruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5 mm), stable sac (<5 mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5 mm). The primary outcome was late reintervention, including endovascular reintervention and open conversion (OC).

RESULTS: A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late reintervention compared to sac regression (hazard ratio [HR], 2.335; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.048-5.191; P = 0.047). However, the rate of late reintervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383-1.258; P = 0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak (EL), and 3.2% (4/126) needed OCs.

CONCLUSION: Late reintervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.

The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression. METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent nonruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020.

title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n = 120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n = 13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (interquartile range [IQR], 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 2.2-3.7; P < 0.001). Completion duplex ultrasonography (DUS) confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; P = 0.015).

CONCLUSION: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n = 120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n = 13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months.

title: Antiplatelet Therapy and Bleeding, Cardiovascular Events, and Aneurysm Growth in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed. Demographics and outcomes were compared by antiplatelet status, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with mortality, major adverse cardiac event (MACE), bleeding, and AAA growth.

RESULTS: Among 886 (73% male) patients studied, 511 (57.7%) were prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Those prescribed antiplatelet therapy had higher rates of atherosclerotic disease than those not on antiplatelets. Patients not prescribed antiplatelet therapy were more likely to be female, have atrial fibrillation, and be prescribed anticoagulation. At a mean follow up of 1.8 years, there were no differences in bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism events, or growth rate associated with antiplatelet prescription. Adjusted analyses showed statins (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.73, P = 0.02), but not antiplatelets or anticoagulants, were associated with reduced risk of mortality. Diabetes was associated with decreased AAA growth rate, while larger initial diameter was associated with increased growth rate as well as mortality.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with AAA, antiplatelet therapy was not observed to be associated with an increase in bleeding risk, but was also not associated with decreased mortality, thrombosis, or aneurysm growth. Statins were observed to be associated with reduced mortality. Aneurysmal growth rate was not associated with any medical therapies studied, including statins, and was only influenced by the presence of diabetes.

This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs. METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed.

title: Early and Midterm Outcomes of the Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Within and Outside the Instructions for Use for Aortoiliac and Iliac Artery Aneurysms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate perioperative and midterm outcomes of endovascular aneurysm repair using the Gore Excluder iliac branch endoprosthesis (IBE) for aortoiliac and iliac artery aneurysms treated within and outside the instructions for use (IFU).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent IBE implantation for nonruptured aortoiliac or iliac artery aneurysms between April 2017 and December 2022. Outcomes were analyzed at the patient, procedure, or IBE-treated-side level, as appropriate. The primary end points were technical success, IBE-related complications, and reinterventions. Secondary end points included internal iliac artery (IIA) branch patency, aneurysm sac status, and freedom from reintervention or aneurysm-related death.

RESULTS: A total of 56 unique patients underwent 58 procedures involving 73 IBE-treated sides; 24 sides were within-IFU and 49 were outside-IFU. Technical success was achieved in 100% of within-IFU procedures and 95.0% of outside-IFU procedures. At 36 months, freedom from reintervention was 79.1% and 94.0% in the within-IFU and outside-IFU groups, respectively (P = 0.24), and IIA branch patency was 88.8% and 85.5%, respectively. No significant between-group difference in IIA branch patency was detected after accounting for within-patient clustering (hazard ratio, 1.53; 95% confidence interval, 0.28-8.35; P = 0.62). Seven IIA branch occlusions occurred during follow-up, none of which was associated with buttock claudication. In exploratory univariable analysis, type II endoleak was associated with common iliac artery aneurysm sac growth (odds ratio, 7.86; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-57.0; P = 0.04).

CONCLUSION: IBE use outside the IFU was feasible in carefully selected patients. No significant differences in midterm clinical outcomes were detected between the within-IFU and outside-IFU groups.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent IBE implantation for nonruptured aortoiliac or iliac artery aneurysms between April 2017 and December 2022. Outcomes were analyzed at the patient, procedure, or IBE-treated-side level, as appropriate.

title: Vascular surgery is over-represented by multiple medical societies compared with its peers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical societies play an important role in representing physicians and their interests. The study aimed to compare the number, size, and fiscal strength of vascular societies with those of other cardiovascular specialties.

METHODS: Information was found via a systematic Internet search and with publicly available data (ie, www.aamc.org). Medical societies representing vascular surgery (VS), cardiology (CARD), cardiothoracic surgery (CTS), and interventional radiology (IR) in the United States were compared. Board-certified physicians (www.abms.org) and publicly available financial information (www.ProPublica.org) were tabulated.

RESULTS: Board-certified vascular surgeons (n = 4464) could join 30 VS societies (4 national, 10 regional, 12 city/state, and 4 other). In comparison, 12 societies (2 national) represent CTS (n = 5869) and 16 (1 national) represent IR (n = 4032) physicians. Cardiologists (n = 22,843) are represented by 14 societies (5 national) and an additional 27 chapters of a parent national society. The available number of vascular surgeons per national society was markedly lower than that of the comparative specialties. Vascular societies generated $23 million in revenue compared to $52 million for CTS, $6 million for IR, and $1.03 billion for CARD. CARD societies accounted for 93% of the total revenue across the four specialties and generated 52 times the revenue of VS societies.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with similar specialties, VS has relatively few surgeons, but a high number of medical societies. This segmentation may dilute the educational, governmental, societal, and patient advocacy impact of VS compared with that of its peers.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Medical societies play an important role in representing physicians and their interests. The study aimed to compare the number, size, and fiscal strength of vascular societies with those of other cardiovascular specialties. METHODS: Information was found via a systematic Internet search and with publicly available data (ie, www.aamc.org).

title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided SNB (n = 72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n = 91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P < .001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, whereas a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P < .001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P < .001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs 35%; P = .002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided SNB promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular access clinical follow-up database.

title: Neutrophil extracellular traps drive immunoinflammatory remodeling in abdominal aortic aneurysm: from inflammatory amplification to precision therapy.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a chronic vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall dilation, extracellular matrix degradation, and an increased risk of catastrophic rupture. Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration. In the AAA microenvironment, local inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbances, altered mechanical forces, and platelet activation collectively contribute to the induction of NETosis. Persistent NET formation promotes immunoinflammatory remodeling of the aortic wall by activating inflammatory sensing pathways, including TLR9, cGAS-STING, and NLRP3, modulating macrophage responses, inducing vascular smooth muscle cell ferroptosis and phenotypic switching, and exacerbating proteolytic degradation, oxidative injury, and immunothrombotic responses. During disease progression, NETs may transition from early drivers of inflammatory amplification to sustained regulators of vascular remodeling, while in advanced AAA they may synergize with intraluminal thrombus formation and structural destabilization to accelerate disease progression. Circulating NET-associated biomarkers represent promising candidates for complementing conventional imaging-based risk assessment; however, their specificity and predictive value require further validation. Therapeutic strategies targeting PAD4-mediated NET formation, the oxidative metabolic environment, NET-associated effector molecules, DNase I-mediated NET degradation, and nucleic acid sensing pathways have demonstrated potential in preclinical studies. This review systematically summarizes the emerging roles of NETs in AAA pathogenesis and discusses future precision strategies integrating biomarkers, multi-omics profiling, and imaging-based risk stratification with stage-specific therapeutic interventions.
englishSummary: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a chronic vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall dilation, extracellular matrix degradation, and an increased risk of catastrophic rupture. Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration.

title: Who Gets Feedback? Predictors of Receiving Narrative Feedback in Vascular Surgery Entrustable Professional Activities.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical residents and fellows require high-quality feedback to guide skill development. Entrustable professional activity (EPA) assessments allow for frequent feedback in all phases of care. However, feedback is optional. We sought to understand predictors of feedback provision in a national, multi-institutional study of EPA assessments.

METHODS: EPA assessments were collected in the multi-institutional Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. EPAs were rated on a scale of limited participation, direct supervision, indirect supervision and practice ready. Assessments included entrustment rating, postgraduate year (PGY), phase of care, and narrative feedback. Self-reported demographic information was collected. A mixed effects logistic regression was performed examining the effect of entrustment ratings, PGY, trainee and faculty gender and gender concordance, trainee underrepresented in medicine (URiM) identification, and phase of care on the probability of receiving narrative feedback.

RESULTS: In total, 1,998 assessments were collected across 19 institutions (n = 17 residencies, n = 13 fellowships). Faculty submitted 983 assessments with 759 (77%) containing feedback. Fifty-eight percent of trainees were men, 54% White, and 65% of faculty were men. Phase of care, PGY, faculty gender, trainee gender, faculty-trainee gender concordance, and URiM identification were not associated with likelihood of feedback. However, higher entrustment ratings were associated with lower odds of receiving feedback (odds ratio 2.76 [95% confidence interval: 1.25-6.10]).

CONCLUSION: In this national, multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, demographic characteristics were not associated with likelihood of receiving or giving feedback. However, higher performing trainees are less likely to receive feedback. This may limit high-performing trainees' ability to reach their full potential.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Surgical residents and fellows require high-quality feedback to guide skill development. Entrustable professional activity (EPA) assessments allow for frequent feedback in all phases of care. However, feedback is optional.

title: Sex-Based Outcomes after Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a 10-year period in 3 stroke centers.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within 6 months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite end point. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging.

RESULTS: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs. 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs. 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs. 23.5%, P = 0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs. 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, P < 0.01), high density lipoprotein (56.8 ± 18.1 vs. 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, P < 0.01), and low density lipoprotein (101.5 ± 45.4 vs. 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, P < 0.01); however, the low density lipoprotein/high density lipoprotein ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, P < 0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs. 48.6%, P = 0.91), TIA (32.0% vs. 33.5%, P = 0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs. 20.7%, P = 0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs. 4.0%, P = 0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.61), TIA (0.7% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.23), MI (0.5% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs. 1.2%, P = 0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs. 24.3%, P = 0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs. 5.2%, P = 0.32), TIA (5.1% vs. 4.0%, P = 0.50), MI (2.6% vs. 3.6%, P = 0.45), mortality (17.5% vs. 19.1%, P = 0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs. 7.2%, P = 0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs. 4.8%, P = 0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N = 182), the 30-day (3.3% vs. 2.2%, P = 1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs. 31.9%, P = 0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI, and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs. 7.7%, P = 0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs. 6.6%, P = 0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a 10-year period at 3 high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a 10-year period in 3 stroke centers. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026.

title: Plasma Proteomics Enhances Genetic Risk Prediction and Biological Understanding of Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and the third most common vascular cause of death globally. While clinical and genetic risk factors have improved VTE risk stratification, they do not fully capture underlying disease biology. We hypothesized that integrating large-scale plasma proteomics with a validated polygenic risk score (PRSVTE) would reveal novel biological understanding and improve risk stratification. In 44,138 UK Biobank participants, we examined associations between PRSVTE and 2911 plasma proteins using multivariable linear regressions. We evaluated proteins as predictors of incident VTE using Cox regression models. We employed bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (cis-pQTLs) instruments and genome-wide association summary statistics to infer potential causality. A protein-based risk score (ProteinRS) was developed with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) logistic regression and compared against a clinical risk model. PRSVTE associated with 265 proteins after false discovery rate correction (FDR <0.01). Pathway enrichment analysis of these proteins highlighted cell adhesion, cell-junction organization, and transmembrane receptor signaling. Time-to-event analyses identified 354 proteins that predicted incident VTE (FDR <0.01). MR implicated 14 proteins in potential causal pathways to VTE, while genetic liability to VTE affected the levels of 44 proteins. A 60-protein ProteinRS improved discrimination beyond clinical factors (area under the curve (AUC) 0.664 versus 0.647; p = 0.024). Participants above the 80th percentile of ProteinRS had a 49% higher hazard of VTE (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.49, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.17-1.90) and those below the 20th percentile had a 48% lower hazard (HR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79) relative to the 20-80th percentile. Integrating genetic and proteomics data uncovered molecular pathways that link genetic susceptibility to VTE, highlighted actionable protein targets, and modestly enhanced risk prediction. Plasma proteomics therefore hold promise for precision prevention of VTE.

While clinical and genetic risk factors have improved VTE risk stratification, they do not fully capture underlying disease biology. We hypothesized that integrating large-scale plasma proteomics with a validated polygenic risk score (PRSVTE) would reveal novel biological understanding and improve risk stratification.

title: One-Year Outcomes and Additive Risk of Restenosis After Rotational Atherectomy Plus Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Calcified Femoropopliteal Lesions in a Japanese Population.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate 1-year clinical outcomes and identify predictors of restenosis after rotational atherectomy and drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty for calcified femoropopliteal lesions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, single-arm study included 241 patients (178 men [73.9%] and 63 women [26.1%]) treated with rotational atherectomy (JETSTREAM Atherectomy System; Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA) atherectomy and DCB angioplasty at 8 Japanese centers. Mean lesion length was 16.5 cm, 28.6% were chronic total occlusions, and 91.3% had Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System Grade 3/4 calcification. Primary patency was freedom from restenosis (duplex ultrasound [US]-derived peak systolic velocity ratio > 2.4 or occlusion) and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR). At 1 year, 220 patients (91.3%) completed follow-up.

RESULTS: One-year primary patency and freedom from CD-TLR were 85.5% and 91.3%, respectively. Exploratory multivariable analysis identified hemodialysis (hazard ratio [HR], 2.70; 95% CI, 1.27-5.77; P = .01), chronic total occlusion (HR, 2.85; 95% CI, 1.39-5.83; P < .01), prior endovascular therapy (HR, 5.08; 95% CI, 2.48-10.4; P < .01), and popliteal artery involvement (HR, 3.62; 95% CI, 1.76-7.46; P < .01) as independently associated with patency loss. Patency declined from 94.1% with ≤1 factor to 38.1% with ≥3 factors. Neither severe nor nodular calcifications were associated with patency loss. Among restenotic lesions, 54.8% were occlusive, and shorter than baseline lesions. Angiographic distal embolization occurred in 37.8% and remained unresolved in 3.3%.

CONCLUSIONS: One-year primary patency was 85.5%. Exploratory analyses suggested an additive association between clinical and anatomical factors and loss of patency. These findings require confirmation given the single-arm design and limited number of patency-loss events.

Mean lesion length was 16.5 cm, 28.6% were chronic total occlusions, and 91.3% had Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System Grade 3/4 calcification.

title: Elastography and Vector Flow Imaging Detect Arteriovenous Fistula Stenosis Independent of Luminal Diameter.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic value of multimodal ultrasound (US)-including 2-dimensional (2D) US, sound touch elastography (STE), and vector flow imaging (VFI)-for the identification of functional and biomechanical abnormalities indicative of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis or occlusion in hemodialysis patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 37 hemodialysis patients with AVFs, divided into normal (n = 20) and dysfunction (n = 17) groups based on digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or clinical/US criteria. For the dysfunction group, AVF stenosis was defined as >50% luminal diameter reduction on DSA, and occlusion was defined as complete absence of flow. For the normal group, dysfunction was excluded by clinical examination (thrill/bruit) and normal duplex parameters. All patients underwent 2D US, STE, and VFI examinations. Key parameters measured included vessel diameter, elasticity (kPa), blood flow velocities, turbulence (Tur) index, and wall shear stress (WSS). Statistical comparisons were made between groups.

RESULTS: No significant differences were found in vessel diameter or intima status between groups. However, the stenosis/occlusion group exhibited significantly lower mean blood flow, peak systolic/end-diastolic velocities, and WSS, along with higher resistance index and vessel wall stiffness (STE mean, 30.35 kPa [SD ± 11.65] vs 20.7 kPa [SD ± 7.52]; P < .01). VFI revealed reduced blood flow velocity, Tur, and WSS in dysfunctional AVFs (all P < .01).

CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal US integrating 2D US, STE, and VFI provides a comprehensive assessment of AVF structure and function, detecting functional and biomechanical abnormalities associated with AVF stenosis or occlusion.

title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: A competing-risk analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation between 2017 and 2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P < .001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P < .001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P = .002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P = .030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss [subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR), 1.12; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.74-1.70], whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

title: Insulin dependence erodes the cardiac and survival advantage of asymptomatic status after carotid revascularization.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent DM (IDDM) and non-IDDM with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting, stratified by symptom status.

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed between January 2005 and January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. End points were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) non-IDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days, there were 1645 MIs, 2051 ipsilateral strokes, 1806 deaths, 3626 strokes or deaths, and 5029 MACE; at 1 year, 2378 MIs, 2924 ipsilateral strokes, 8269 deaths, 10,750 strokes or deaths, and 12,646 MACE, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR, 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR, 1.24), mortality (OR, 1.19), and MACE (OR, 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE: OR, 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P < .001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR, 1.54; P < .001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR, 1.05; P = .41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR, 1.19; P < .001). Relative to carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR, 2.10 and 1.93, respectively; P ≤ .01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every end point.

CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival end points, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable with symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent DM (IDDM) and non-IDDM with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting, stratified by symptom status.

title: Femoral artery access outcomes and technical considerations in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed-VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access. Data were obtained from the global genetically confirmed-VEDS Natural History Study and a retrospective single center cohort. Demographics, genotype, procedural indication, access and closure techniques, access-related complications, and outcomes were abstracted from clinical record. Major access-related complications were defined as femoral artery dissection, pseudoaneurysm, rupture, or closure device failure requiring open operative repair.

RESULTS: A total of 117 femoral artery access sites were used in 105 endovascular interventions among 60 patients between 1989 and 2025. Median age at intervention was 39 years, and 53.3% of patients were male. Among 99 procedures with known access modality, 84 were performed percutaneously and 15 involved planned open femoral exposure. Manual compression was used in 33 percutaneous access sites, with no major access-related complications. Percutaneous closure devices were used in 39 access sites; major complications occurred in five access sites across five procedures, all requiring unplanned surgical exposure and repair. One additional percutaneous access site required unplanned open repair for access-related arterial injury and external iliac artery dissection before any closure device was attempted. Of percutaneous closure device failures, Perclose ProGlide (Abbott Vascular, Inc.) and StarClose (Abbott Vascular, Inc.) had the highest rate of failure (18.8% and 33.3%, respectively). Three of four affected patients had large amino acid substitutions or exon skip mutations; the remaining patient had a small amino acid substitution but underwent 16F sheath placement. No access-related complications occurred after planned open exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: Femoral artery access in VEDS requires deliberate individualized planning. In this cohort, manual compression for smaller-caliber access (≤6F) was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas major complications occurred predominantly following attempted percutaneous closure. Planned open exposure, despite use in procedures involving larger sheath sizes, was not associated with access-related complications and may warrant consideration in selected circumstances, including procedures requiring larger sheath sizes, known previous closure-related arterial injury, and high-risk genotypes.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access.

title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly considering the conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding the optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized National Inpatient Sample (NIS) data coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize the contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI.

METHODS: We utilized NIS data (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. We evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and the rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. The Mann-Kendall test was used to determine the monotonic temporal trends.

RESULTS: The analysis included 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations (mean age, 69.7 years; 40.0% women; 69.5% White patients). The overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with a reversal and steady increase thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations involved revascularization (n = 14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n = 16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization procedures decreased (Ptrend = 0.016), whereas the proportion of endovascular procedures remained stable (Ptrend = 0.368), and the number of hospitalizations without revascularization increased (Ptrend = 0.016) over time. The rates of endovascular revascularization increased among women, nonfrail patients, and patients presenting with rest pain (all Ptrend > 0.05). Overall, the rates of in-hospital amputation (n = 6270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n = 1086 [2.3%]) remained stable (Ptrend > 0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased the most substantially among those with hospitalization without revascularization (Ptrend = 0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, the in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies, corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. The relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings indicate the need for further investigation into the optimal selection of patients with CLTI and the coordinated integration of nonoperative care, including medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment.

INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals.

RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.
englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.

OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.

INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).

RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.

title: [Overlooked thrombophilia in a younger woman with recurrent deep vein thrombosis].
abstract: Antithrombin is the most important endogenous anticoagulant, and hereditary antithrombin deficiency increases the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). In this case, we present a young woman with recurrent VTE and factor V Leiden heterozygosity but normal antithrombin activity. SERPINC1 sequencing revealed heterozygosity for SERPINC1:p.Val30Glu (AT Dublin), which is associated with transient antithrombin deficiency and mildly increased risk of VTE. Transient antithrombin deficiency can, in some cases, affect VTE management but may be missed unless SERPINC1 is sequenced.

title: Update of a living network meta-analysis comparing noncompounded 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (Varithena) ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation in chronic venous insufficiency.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (PEM) and endovenous thermal ablation (ETA) for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when PEM was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence.

METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life (QoL) or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference.

RESULTS: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). PEM was not statistically different from ETA for vein closure (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean, 28 months; range, 12-72 months) showed similar results (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.45-1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with PEM vs ETA (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.29-2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific QoL or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between PEM and ETA (Hedges' g standardized mean difference, 0.04; 95% CI, -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference.

CONCLUSIONS: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that 1% PEM is not statistically different from ETA for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between PEM ablation and ETA for a composite of disease-specific QoL and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.

This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026.
