title: Postpartum "Hypercoagulable Storm" With Extensive Iliocaval Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism in a Patient With Heterozygous Factor V Leiden.
abstract: A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department four weeks after a lower segment cesarean section with a four-day history of progressive dyspnea, bilateral lower limb swelling, and leg pain. At presentation to the emergency department, she was tachycardic (150 beats/min), hypotensive (88/60 mmHg), and tachypneic (38/min), with an oxygen saturation of 93% on room air. Venous Doppler ultrasonography demonstrated extensive bilateral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) involving the iliac veins, right external iliac vein, infrarenal inferior vena cava (IVC), and right popliteal vein, with left popliteal involvement. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography demonstrated acute pulmonary embolism (PE) involving the right pulmonary artery and multiple segmental branches, with right lower lobe pulmonary infarction. Thrombophilia evaluation identified heterozygous Factor V Leiden, with negative antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant and normal protein C, protein S, and antithrombin III levels. The initial presentation raised concern for high-risk acute pulmonary embolism physiology, with hypotension (88/60 mmHg), marked tachycardia, and respiratory compromise requiring high-flow oxygen. Category D1+R was considered provisionally; however, definitive classification was limited by the absence of documented hypotension duration and fluid responsiveness, lactate, echocardiographic right ventricular assessment, and computed tomography (CT) right ventricular (RV)/left ventricular (LV) ratio. A Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) was activated, and intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) was initiated. A retrievable suprarenal IVC filter was placed, followed by mechanical thrombectomy extending from the right popliteal vein to the IVC. At three months, the patient remained ambulatory without exertional dyspnea, and bilateral lower limb swelling had completely resolved. Repeat venous Doppler demonstrated recanalization of the previously thrombosed segments without significant residual occlusive thrombus. This case is presented because of the uncommon combination of extensive bilateral lower limb and iliocaval thrombosis with acute PE and pulmonary infarction in the early postpartum period in a patient with heterozygous Factor V Leiden. It highlights how postpartum hypercoagulability may interact with inherited thrombophilia to produce extensive multisite thrombosis and emphasizes the importance of early recognition, severity-based risk stratification, and coordinated multidisciplinary management.

Venous Doppler ultrasonography demonstrated extensive bilateral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) involving the iliac veins, right external iliac vein, infrarenal inferior vena cava (IVC), and right popliteal vein, with left popliteal involvement.

title: Preoperative Nutritional Testing Before Midfoot Fusion Is Infrequent, and With the Numbers Available, No Association Between Hypoalbuminemia and Postoperative Complications Could Be Detected: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adequate nutrition is essential for wound healing and postoperative recovery. Preoperative screening may identify high-risk patients and improve outcomes. This study aimed to determine whether abnormal preoperative nutritional laboratory values are associated with 90-day and 1-year complications including pseudarthrosis following midfoot fusion.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX research network of more than 147 million patients, evaluating patients undergoing midfoot fusion with available preoperative nutritional laboratory values. Rates of preoperative laboratory testing were assessed, followed by propensity score-matched analyses comparing patients with abnormal and normal values. Ninety-day and 1-year postoperative complications were evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 5667 patients underwent midfoot fusion. Preoperative nutritional laboratory markers were infrequently obtained (albumin 58.9%, leukocytes 36.0%, transferrin 3.2%, and prealbumin 1.9%) and often within normal limits (albumin 89.9%, leukocytes 99.5%, transferrin 79.7%, and prealbumin 91.0%). With the numbers available, no association could be detected between preoperative hypoalbuminemia and 90-day wound disruption (risk ratio [RR] 1.10, 95% CI 0.61-1.98), SSI (SSI; RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.54-1.68), hardware infection (RR 1.33, 95% CI 0.70-2.56), return to emergency department (ED; RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.70-1.59), or readmission (RR 1.13, 95% CI 0.88-1.45). With the numbers available, no association could be detected at 1 year postoperatively for pseudarthrosis (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.55-2.07), wound disruption (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.64-1.68), SSI (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.64-1.67), hardware infection (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.71-1.83), return to ED (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.83-1.39), readmission (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.95-1.46), hardware removal (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.66-1.71), pneumonia (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.36-1.71), and venous thromboembolism (RR 1.23, 95% CI 0.60-2.52).

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative nutritional laboratory markers are infrequently obtained and are rarely abnormal when measured. With the numbers available, no association could be detected between preoperative hypoalbuminemia and increased 90-day or 1-year complications including pseudarthrosis following midfoot fusion.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Adequate nutrition is essential for wound healing and postoperative recovery. Preoperative screening may identify high-risk patients and improve outcomes. This study aimed to determine whether abnormal preoperative nutritional laboratory values are associated with 90-day and 1-year complications including pseudarthrosis following midfoot fusion.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease and the heart: how trained immunity shapes cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing intestinal inflammatory disorder. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in patients with IBD, with elevated risks of myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, and venous thromboembolism that are independent of traditional risk factors. Disease activity and histological inflammation independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events, and Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis differ in cardiovascular risk profiles. This residual risk points to immune mechanisms that remain unclear. Trained immunity (TI), an innate immune memory induced by epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, may link chronic intestinal inflammation to cardiovascular injury. This review integrates epidemiological and mechanistic evidence, outlines cardiovascular risk features in IBD, examines the molecular basis of TI and its roles in atherosclerosis, myocardial injury, and heart failure, and evaluates candidate biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. We also discuss current limitations and challenges in clinical translation and propose future research directions, to inform mechanistic studies and clinical interventions for IBD-associated CVD.

Disease activity and histological inflammation independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events, and Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis differ in cardiovascular risk profiles.

title: Noninvasive hemodynamics of nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions are disturbed in patients with a history of deep vein thrombosis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVLs) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective case control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein (LCIV) stenoses greater than 20% were included and categorized by history of left lower-extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or previous venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, with statistical significance defined as P < .05.

RESULTS: Forty-five patients were included, comprising nine patients with previous DVT, and 36 without. Among all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed LCIV showed the strongest associations with a history of previous DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change [FC], -1.539; P = .007), peak velocity (log2FC, -0.999; P = .002), and mean velocity (log2FC, -0.989; P = .002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2FC, 0.363; P = .033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the LCIV at the compression point was the strongest predictor of previous DVT, whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging.

title: Admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio is associated with early major amputation after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited.

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810).

CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

title: Ultraselective N-Butyl Cyanoacrylate Embolization of an Arteriobiliary Fistula After Transjugular Liver Biopsy With Preservation of Parent Arterial Flow.
abstract: Hemobilia is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transjugular liver biopsy (TJLB). An arteriobiliary fistula associated with a hepatic arterial pseudoaneurysm may require prompt endovascular treatment. We report the case of a 17-year-old male who underwent TJLB to evaluate liver dysfunction in the presence of coagulopathy. Two days later, he developed abdominal pain and hyperbilirubinemia. Although his hemoglobin level was initially unchanged, progressive anemia subsequently developed despite blood transfusion. Computed tomography revealed a 3-mm pseudoaneurysm adjacent to the posterior sectoral branch of the right hepatic artery and findings suggestive of hemobilia. Five days after TJLB, ultraselective angiography confirmed communication between the pseudoaneurysm and the bile duct. Subsequent ultraselective embolization with a mixture of N-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) and Lipiodol achieved complete occlusion of the fistula while preserving posterior sectoral arterial flow. Minimal migration of the NBCA-Lipiodol cast into a peripheral bile duct occurred during embolization. Abdominal pain resolved, and bilirubin levels returned to baseline within five days. The radiopaque component of the migrated cast was no longer visible on follow-up CT, and subsequent magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography showed no intrabiliary filling defects. No clinically significant biliary complications were observed during 28 months of follow-up. This case illustrates the feasibility of ultraselective NBCA embolization when coil isolation is limited by vascular anatomy, while emphasizing the risk of intrabiliary migration and the need for follow-up.
englishSummary: Hemobilia is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transjugular liver biopsy (TJLB). An arteriobiliary fistula associated with a hepatic arterial pseudoaneurysm may require prompt endovascular treatment. We report the case of a 17-year-old male who underwent TJLB to evaluate liver dysfunction in the presence of coagulopathy.

title: The Safety and Efficacy of Intravascular Lithotripsy in Treating Calcified Peripheral Arterial Disease.
abstract: Calcified peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a common health condition associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Endovascular procedures have become more common in treating these lesions, and plain balloon angioplasty (PBA) is often used for vessels with mild-to-moderate calcification. However, decreased vascular compliance in heavily calcified vessels leads to poorer outcomes and higher complication risk. Intravascular shockwave lithotripsy is a more novel endovascular management option. It uses a specially designed balloon catheter to create shockwaves in an attempt to modify and increase compliance of the calcified plaque. This review aims to assess the safety profile and efficacy of intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). The currently available literature shows that use of IVL for calcified PAD has a good safety profile and low complication rate. Intravascular lithotripsy has also been shown to be more effective in treating patients with calcified PAD as compared to PBA alone. Whilst short-term and mid-term results are promising, there is a scarcity of published long-term data. Hence, further long-term data is required before a definitive conclusion can be drawn.

title: [Risk prediction of pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the risk factors for pneumonia after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) infection in maintenance hemodialysis patients from a single center in China, and to establish a multivariate model to predict the risk of pneumonia.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on maintenance hemodialysis patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen or nucleic acid tests treated at Peking University Third Hospital from December 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Demographic data, comorbidities, dialysis-related parameters, and laboratory test results were collected. Multivariate Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were adopted to explore risk factors of pneumonia, and a multivariate model was established to predict the risk of pneumonia occurrence.

RESULTS: A total of 209 hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection were enrolled, including 80 patients (38.3%) with pneumonia and 129 patients (61.7%) without pneumonia. Compared with the non-pneumonia group, the pneumonia group presented a significantly higher mean age [(65.8±13.7) years vs. (58.9±12.6) years, P < 0.001] and elevated C-reactive protein levels [4.58(1.62, 9.99) mg/L vs. 2.35(0.95, 6.50) mg/L, P=0.007]. In contrast, the pneumonia group had markedly lower hemoglobin [(109±15) g/L vs. (116±11) g/L, P=0.001], serum phosphorus [(1.60±0.52) mmol/L vs. (1.78±0.53) mmol/L, P=0.022], serum albumin [(35.9±4.1) g/L vs. (38.6±2.5) g/L, P < 0.001], arteriovenous fistula utilization rate (81.3% vs. 96.9%, P < 0.001), and single dialysis session duration [(232±14) min vs. (236±11) min, P=0.046]. Multivariate Logistic analysis revealed that advanced age (OR=1.030, 95%CI: 1.002-1.059, P=0.036), lower hemoglobin (OR=0.968, 95%CI: 0.942-0.995, P=0.019), lower albumin (OR=0.834, 95%CI: 0.738-0.943, P=0.004) were independent risk factors for pneumonia. Patients over 65 years old, with hemoglobin < 115 g/L or serum albumin < 36.8 g/L had elevated risk of pneumonia. A combined predictive factor Q composed of these three indicators was developed for risk prediction of pneumonia. We drew the ROC curve with the predictive factor Q [area under the curve (AUC) =0.756, 95%CI: 0.687-0.825, P < 0.001]. Taking the cut-off value of 0.575, the sensitivity and specificity of predictive factor Q for predicting pneumonia were 44.0% and 94.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, anemia and hypoalbuminemia are risk factors for pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients following SARS-CoV-2 infection. A predictive marker Q value less than 0.575 indicates low risk of pneumonia, which can be applied for rapid risk stratification among hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on maintenance hemodialysis patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen or nucleic acid tests treated at Peking University Third Hospital from December 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Demographic data, comorbidities, dialysis-related parameters, and laboratory test results were collected.

title: Incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections after PICC insertion: Impact of a newly established vascular access unit in a French university hospital.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are widely used, they remain associated with infectious risk. Even though the value of dedicated catheter teams is well-recognized, evidence regarding vascular access units is limited. This study compared catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) rates between a Vascular and Interventional Angiography Unit (VIAU) (insertion performed by physicians) and a newly established Vascular Access Unit (VAU) (insertion performed by nurse anesthetists under anesthesiologists' supervision).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted in a French university hospital, including patients having undergone PICC insertion from January 2017 to June 2020 (VIAU) and from January to June 2020 (VAU). CRBSI rates during catheter dwell time and within 8 days after PICC insertion were compared. Risk factors for CRBSI were assessed using logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: Among 3332 inserted PICCs, 266 (8.0%) CRBSIs occurred during catheter dwell time, with no significant difference between the VIAU (7.7%) and the VAU (9.3%). In multivariate analysis, the risk of CRBSI between the VIAU and the VAU did not significantly differ (adjusted OR = 0.978 [95%CI, 0.558-1.714]); non-metastatic cancer was associated with a higher risk of CRBSI, whereas older age appeared protective. The 8-day CRBSI rate (0.9%) was similar between the two departments (0.9% for the VIAU and 1.0% for the VAU). Slightly more than half of the CRBSIs were caused by Staphylococcus species, and one third by Gram-negative bacteria.

DISCUSSION - CONCLUSION: CRBSI rates between the established and the newly created units were similar. These results suggest that a dedicated vascular access unit staffed by trained professionals can achieve outcomes comparable to those obtained by an experienced unit.

Even though the value of dedicated catheter teams is well-recognized, evidence regarding vascular access units is limited. This study compared catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) rates between a Vascular and Interventional Angiography Unit (VIAU) (insertion performed by physicians) and a newly established Vascular Access Unit (VAU) (insertion performed by nurse anesthetists under anesthesiologists' supervision).

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation.

CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set.

title: Expressing Needs and Concerns During Nursing Care: An Ethnographic Study of Patients Undergoing Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: This focused ethnographic study aimed to explore how patients expressed their needs and concerns during nursing care while undergoing planned open repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Fieldwork was conducted in a vascular surgery ward at a Danish university hospital between December 2024 and August 2025. Ten patients admitted for planned open repair were followed during their inpatient stay through participant observation. The ethnographic record comprised 85 hours of observation and was analyzed using Spradley's Developmental Research Sequence within a hermeneutic interpretive orientation. The overall cultural theme identified was "Expressing vulnerability while trying not to be a burden." This theme captures how physical recovery needs were more readily expressed, whereas emotional and existential concerns were softened, held back, or communicated through silence, humor, or reliance on family members. The included cases illustrate three domains: unspoken suffering as a barrier to well-being, family members' work in making patients' needs visible, and becoming dependent on nursing care as a patient. The findings show that patients undergoing open repair struggle to voice vulnerability directly during hospitalization. The study highlights the importance of nursing care that attends not only to explicit requests for help, but also to subtle verbal, embodied, and relational expressions of vulnerability.

title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood.

METHODS: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis.

RESULTS: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI.

CONCLUSIONS: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

title: Differences in Clinical Presentation of Chronic Pelvic Pain Caused by Iliac Vein Obstruction Impacts Referral Pathway, Time to Diagnosis, and Post-stenting Pain Resolution.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but the pain is reproducible and easily identifiable; however, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data of women who were referred to a vascular surgeon with signs and symptoms of IVO, including CPP, and who underwent iliac venous stenting. Associations between clinical presentation (signs, symptoms, pain severity), medical and referral history, and stenting outcomes were compared between three patient groups based on the number of other specialist consultations before stenting (none, one, or at least two).

RESULTS: Data were for 113 women (46.5 ± 15.7 years) who had CPP for 6.3 ± 6.6 years with initial severity of 6.7 ± 2.3 (out of 10). CPP was reproducible for all women, with exercise, standing, and intercourse being the most common triggers. More than two thirds had lower limb pain, oedema, and varicose veins. At a median of 7 years post-stenting, the latest pain score was 0.8 ± 1.6, and approximately 80% had full pain resolution. Women who had seen at least two other specialists had the worst initial pelvic pain, the most prescription pain medication, back pain, other abdominopelvic signs and symptoms, and previous interventions, and the fewest varicose veins. These women endured 8.5 ± 7.9 years to diagnosis, but 99% still had significant improvement in, and 66% had full resolution of, their pelvic pain.

CONCLUSION: All patients had a reproducible pattern of venous origin pelvic pain, but those with worse CPP, more abdominopelvic symptoms, and less varicose veins had a more complex and delayed referral pathway and the lowest pain resolution.

Signs and symptoms vary, but the pain is reproducible and easily identifiable; however, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO.

title: ArtAssist sequential compression biomechanical device as a cost-dominant limb salvage strategy for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia: A decade and half, single-center cohort study with health economic and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive a median €88,820/patient; the long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device (SCBD) is lacking.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.

RESULTS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (hazard ratio: 1.70, 1.80, 1.71; all P ≤ .012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = .008). Ninety-day rental (€1373/patient) reduced total expenditure sixfold vs primary amputation (€5.3M vs €30.8M), saving €76,500/patient. Quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity yielded a gain of 3.37 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) per patient; incremental cost-effectiveness ratio €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.

CONCLUSIONS: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a sixfold reduction in costs vs primary amputation, +3.37 QALYs/patient, and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-center cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for nonreconstructible CLTI.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity.

title: Early venous filling is associated with unfavorable outcomes in acute basilar artery occlusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between early venous filling (EVF) on digital subtraction angiography and poor outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected. Candidate predictors were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Four variables (fasting blood glucose, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, EVF, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score) were included in Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression models for postprocedural malignant cerebellar edema (MCE) and poor prognosis (90-day modified Rankin Scale score > 2). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with internal validation by bootstrap optimism correction using 1,000 resamples.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 26 (25.7 %) had EVF, 29 (28.7 %) developed MCE, and 56 (55.4 %) had poor prognosis. With four predictors, the events-per-variable values were 7.25 for MCE and 11.25 for poor prognosis, using the smaller outcome category. EVF was associated with MCE (OR 34.650, 95 % CI 9.024-184.087; P < 0.001) and poor prognosis (OR 10.239, 95 % CI 2.889-54.718; P < 0.001) in the Firth models. For MCE, the apparent AUCs of the clinical model and the clinical model plus EVF were 0.804 and 0.944, respectively; the corresponding optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 and 0.926. For poor prognosis, the apparent AUCs were 0.762 and 0.836, and the optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.742 and 0.818. The optimism-corrected AUC increments with EVF were 0.138 for MCE and 0.076 for poor prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: EVF was independently associated with MCE and poor prognosis after MT in patients with ABAO.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected.

title: Construction and validation of a cross-sectional classification model for identifying adverse metabolic status in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome based on serum amino acids and lipid metabolic characteristics.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and externally validate a cross-sectional classification model for identifying adverse metabolic status at diagnosis in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) based on serum amino acid and lipid metabolic profiles.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 442 PCOS patients, comprising a training set (n=309; June 2022-December 2024) and an external validation set (n=133; January 2025-December 2025). Within each dataset, patients were classified into an adverse metabolic status group or a metabolically normal group according to the presence of at least one of the following conditions at baseline: metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance (IR), non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, impaired glucose tolerance, or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). At enrollment, serum concentrations of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), aromatic amino acids (AAAs), glucogenic amino acids, lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) species, and free fatty acids (FFAs) were measured using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Routine biochemical and hormonal parameters were also collected.

RESULTS: Multivariable logistic regression identified BMI ≥ 28.215 kg/m2 (OR=11.27), HOMA-IR ≥ 3.42 (OR=4.61), TyG index ≥ 4.84 (OR=5.44), valine ≥ 270.125 nmol/mL (OR=5.68), glutamate ≥ 63.185 nmol/mL (OR=8.87) and arachidonic acid ≥ 21.535 μmol/L (OR=10.85) as independent positive predictors of adverse metabolic status. In contrast, higher SHBG (OR=0.31), BCAA/AAA ratio ≥ 3.215 (OR=0.20), LPC(16:0) ≥ 142.06 μmol/L (OR=0.22), and LPC(18:1) ≥ 30.515 μmol/L (OR=0.28) were protective factors. The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.965 in the training set and 0.939 in the external validation set.

CONCLUSION: The nomogram integrating serum amino acids and lipid profiles with routine clinical measures may provide a reliable tool for classifying adverse metabolic status in PCOS patients at initial assessment.

Within each dataset, patients were classified into an adverse metabolic status group or a metabolically normal group according to the presence of at least one of the following conditions at baseline: metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance (IR), non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, impaired glucose tolerance, or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

title: End-stage renal disease and pulmonary hypertension: epidemiologic, pathophysiologic, and hemodynamic characteristics and related risk factors.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) in end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is classified as Group 5 PH, a category defined by unclear or multifactorial mechanisms. The condition affects a substantial proportion of ESRD patients and contributes significantly to cardiovascular mortality; moreover, PH may persist or even progress despite renal replacement therapy. Right heart catheterization (RHC) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) have characterized the hemodynamic profiles and cardiac structural changes in these patients, implicating anemia, volume overload, uremic toxins, hypoxia, left heart disease, and pulmonary vascular dysfunction as major drivers, with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) as a possible disease modifier in susceptible subpopulations. This review synthesizes findings from invasive hemodynamic studies to delineate the principal mechanisms underlying PH in ESRD. Particular emphasis is placed on the potential roles of AVF flow and dialysis-related factors - including membrane biocompatibility, microbubble embolization, and shear stress-induced microhemolysis - in driving disease progression, an area that remains inadequately understood.

title: Venous Hypertension Associated with an Abnormal Configuration of a Protruding Cephalic Arch Stent in Arteriovenous Haemodialysis Access: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cephalic arch stenosis is a common cause of access dysfunction in brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistulae, and recurrent lesions are often treated with stent placement. Although stent protrusion into the axillary vein is frequently tolerated, an abnormal stent-vein configuration combined with in stent re-stenosis may impair physiological venous drainage. This case report presents severe venous hypertension resulting from in stent re-stenosis within the protruding segment impairing physiological axillary venous outflow and an abnormal stent-vein configuration caused by stent tip contact with the opposite axillary vein wall, redistributing access flow.

REPORT: A 75 year old man receiving long term haemodialysis developed upper extremity oedema and prolonged post-dialysis bleeding from his brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula. Computed tomography showed a cephalic arch stent protruding across the cephalic axillary junction, its tip contacting the axillary vein wall opposite the junction. Access fistulography demonstrated severe in stent re-stenosis with neointimal hyperplasia reducing the available sidewall openings. Through the remaining patent openings, part of the access flow continued centrally and part was redirected into the axillary venous segment peripheral to the cephalic axillary junction, with retrograde opacification and subsequent collateral drainage. The protruding stent segment was excised, and the axillary vein reconstructed with a patch. After surgery, oedema improved, collateral venous flow decreased, and the access remained functional at one year despite residual re-stenosis.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that cephalic arch stent protrusion may become clinically significant when in stent re-stenosis within the protruding segment impairs axillary venous outflow and the stent-vein configuration causes access flow redistribution. In this patient, neointimal hyperplasia reduced the sidewall openings, impairing physiological axillary venous outflow, while residual openings allowed redistribution of access flow into the peripheral axillary venous segment. Recognition of this abnormal stent-vein configuration and flow pattern is important because open surgical reconstruction may be required to restore venous drainage while preserving haemodialysis access function.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to zone 0 or 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, and none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost to follow-up (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (such as aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, and survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (zone 1-3; complete 56% vs incomplete/LTF 27%; P < .001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs incomplete/LTF 18%; P < .001), in-hospital thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension (7% vs 2%; P = .028), and thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs incomplete/LTF 5%; P = .002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete 12% vs incomplete 5%; P = .007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs 15%; P = .002) within 1-year of acute dissection. The long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete 97% vs incomplete 97% vs LTF 91%), 3-years (complete 92% vs incomplete 95% vs LTF 81%; P = .021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (P = .13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (hazard ratio, 2.87; 95% confidence interval, 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (hazard ratio, 2.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.9).

CONCLUSIONS: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and midterm survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.

However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

title: Reintervention burden and patency of hemodialysis vascular access in a 15-year single-center cohort.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maintaining a hemodialysis access typically requires repeated intervention; yet, the cumulative reintervention burden-distinct from patency-is rarely quantified, and configuration-specific estimates from Asian centers are scarce. In this study, we evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous access cases over 15 years at a single center.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 871 consecutive cases of upper extremity arteriovenous access (648 fistulas; 223 grafts) created in 810 patients between 2009 and 2024. From operative records, every subsequent procedure was determined to be patency-maintaining or access-abandoning; operations unrelated to the access under study, including kidney transplantation, catheter procedures, and peripheral arterial interventions, were excluded. Patency was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method according to the accepted reporting standards and was compared across configurations-radiocephalic fistula, brachiocephalic fistula, basilic vein transposition, and graft. The reintervention burden is expressed as interventions per access-year. The predictors of the loss of primary patency were identified using multivariable Cox regression, and in a competing risk analysis, kidney transplantation was considered a competing event.

RESULTS: The median follow-up duration was 14.7 months. The overall primary, assisted primary, and secondary patency rates were 60.3%, 50.5%, and 44.6%; 87.1%, 81.5%, and 77.1%; and 96.8%, 95.7%, and 94.1% at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. The 1-year primary patency rates differed by the configuration: 70.1% for radiocephalic fistulas, 63.3% for brachiocephalic fistulas, 71.6% for basilic vein transpositions, and 36.2% for grafts (P < .001). Across 2211 access-years, 743 patency-maintaining interventions were performed (0.336 per access-year), and 37.2% of access cases required at least one reintervention. The intervention burden was concentrated in grafts: 1.09 intervention per access-year for grafts vs 0.25 intervention per access-year for autogenous fistulas, with a difference of approximately 4.4-fold. The graft configuration (hazard ratio, 2.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.86-3.06), female sex (1.37; 1.10-1.71), ischemic heart disease (1.42; 1.04-1.94), and diabetes (1.26; 1.00-1.57) independently predicted the loss of primary patency. These findings persisted after excluding maturation-assisting procedures and in the competing risk analysis (subdistribution hazard ratio for graft reintervention, 2.32).

CONCLUSIONS: High secondary patency was achieved at the cost of substantial reintervention concentrated in grafts, which required maintenance that was approximately 4.4 times that of autogenous fistulas. Reporting the explicit reintervention burden alongside patency supports autogenous-first, configuration-aware access planning and patient counseling.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Maintaining a hemodialysis access typically requires repeated intervention; yet, the cumulative reintervention burden-distinct from patency-is rarely quantified, and configuration-specific estimates from Asian centers are scarce. In this study, we evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous access cases over 15 years at a single center. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 871 consecutive cases of upper extremity arteriovenous access (648 fistulas; 223 grafts) created in 810 patients between 2009 and 2024.

title: A safe and efficient analgesic approach for percutaneous transluminal angioplasty: Fentanyl plus targeted local anesthesia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stenosis is a common complication of arteriovenous access (AV), for which percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) is a well-established intervention. Nevertheless, balloon dilation commonly induces pain. Common analgesic approaches during PTA encompass moderate intravenous sedation and analgesia, brachial plexus block, and local infiltrative anesthesia, each with its own limitations. A need currently exists for a safe, simple, and effective analgesic approach during PTA.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study was conducted between January 2020 and July 2022 at a single tertiary medical center. Patients with AV access dysfunction undergoing PTA were included. Patients were allocated into two groups based on the analgesia approach: one group received intraluminal fentanyl injection alone, and the other a combination of intraluminal fentanyl and local lidocaine infiltration at the stenotic site. Data regarding AV access type, lesion locations, 11-point Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) scores, and procedural complications were collected. Comparative analysis between groups was conducted using appropriate statistical methods, and significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 120 patients (mean age, 62.9 ± 11.8 years; 65% were male) were included in the study: 34 in the fentanyl-only group (group A) and 86 in the fentanyl combined with lidocaine group (group B). Group A had a higher proportion of male patients compared with group B (79.4% vs 59.3%, p = 0.037). No significant differences were found in balloon size, inflation pressure, fluoroscope time, or procedural complications between groups. The primary outcome, procedural pain, was significantly lower in group B as compared to group A (NRS score 2.3 ± 0.9 vs 5.1 ± 2.2, p < 0.001), and this analgesic advantage remained after adjusting for gender and age.

CONCLUSION: Our study findings suggest that administering a combination of intraluminal fentanyl and a direct lidocaine injection in patients undergoing percutaneous transluminal angioplasty is both an efficient and safe analgesic procedure for PTA.

title: Real-life venous thromboembolism risk scores in multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment with daratumumab and lenalidomide has improved survival in patients with multiple myeloma (MM), however the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) is high. Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort study.

METHODS: All consecutive MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and concomitant LMWH-ASA thromboprophylaxis between July, 2018 and September, 2023 were evaluated through chart review. Kaplan-Meier method and Concordance-Index (C-index) were used to estimate risk scores' prognostic accuracy.

RESULTS: 95 patients (median age 74 years) were included (n= 47 NTE-MM, and n= 48 RRMM). At 12 months from Dara-Rd initiation, 10 (10.4%) patients developed VTE; 4 (4.2%) had bleeding complications, and 2 (2.1%) patients died. Six VTE events (6.2%) occurred within first 6 months from Dara-Rd initiation while on LMWH prophylaxis, whereas 2 VTE (2%) developed in two patients receiving aspirin. The accuracy of IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM and EHR-CAT scores was generally poor, with C-Index values ranging from 0.43 (95% confidence intervals [95%CI] 0.30 to 0.56) to 0.53 (95%CI: 0.38 to 0.68). LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was completed by 89.5% of the cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-life cohort of MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and guideline-recommended antithrombotic prophylaxis, currently available VTE risk scores demonstrated moderate to poor prognostic accuracy. LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was feasible but associated with residual VTE risk.

title: The prediagnostic period of Behçet's disease: a nationwide population-based study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched case-control study using the electronic health records of Leumit Health Services. Patients with BD fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease or International Study Group classification criteria were identified by manual chart review and matched 1:5 with controls by sex, age, socioeconomic category and year of first observation. Clinical diagnoses, diagnostic investigations and laboratory measurements and medication dispensing recorded during the five years preceding diagnosis were compared between groups. Early and late laboratory measurements within the prediagnostic period were analyzed to assess temporal trends. Manifestations documented over the entire available record were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: The study included 218 patients who subsequently developed BD and 1,090 matched controls. During the five years preceding diagnosis, future patients with BD more frequently exhibited oral aphthosis (36.2% vs 3.0%; OR 18.2), panuveitis (4.6% vs 0.1%; OR 52.4), inflammatory polyarthritis (7.3% vs 0.6%; OR 14.3), and venous thromboembolism (4.6% vs 0.2%; OR 26.2) (all P<0.001). Over the entire available record, oral aphthosis was documented in 61.0% of patients with BD and 11.8% of controls. Autoimmune serology was frequently requested but remained largely negative. Laboratory analyses demonstrated a biphasic trajectory. Absolute monocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were lower than in controls at the early assessment (0.40 vs 0.44 ×109/L, P = 0.009, and 1.45 vs 1.49, P = 0.023) but significantly higher near diagnosis (0.64 vs 0.58 ×109/L, P = 0.025, and 2.44 vs 2.09, P = 0.003). This transition was accompanied by rising CRP, ESR, platelet count and globulin levels, persistently lower mean corpuscular volume and consistently higher IgA at both assessments (247 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.009, and 256 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.012), whereas IgG and IgM remained comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: BD seems to be preceded by a clinically and biologically active prediagnostic phase characterized by a distinct inflammatory multisystem footprint.

Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

title: Nongeneral Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals (PIs), and prespecified influence diagnostics.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with GA (risk ratio [RR] 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54-1.52; I2≈86%; wide PI). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I2≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in intensive care unit stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

CONCLUSION: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to GA. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus.

title: Outcomes of Open Versus Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting.

METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into 2 groups based on the intervention: EVAR versus OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed.

RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 0.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.18-0.34, P < 0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95% CI: 0.23-0.42, P < 0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95% CI: 0.19-0.31, P < 0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the 2 treatment modalities.

Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB).

title: Clinical outcomes of transperitoneal versus retroperitoneal approaches of open aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm with iliac bifurcation involvement (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared with OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study compared the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting.

METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as having AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes, such as overall 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, and stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses and a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression were performed.

RESULTS: Of all the reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA and 1791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with a higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (odds ratios [OR], 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.49; P = .011) and of MACE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44; P = .001) and a lower 1-year survival rate (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.09-1.39; P = .001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia (OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.91; P = .024), without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; P = .485), MACE (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.52-1.42; P = .563), and 1-year survival (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.59-1.47; P = .768).

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, iliac bifurcation involvement in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. In contrast, for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation.

title: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Stationarity in Predicting TEVAR Response.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for type B aortic dissections and rupture, with guidelines recommending systolic blood pressure (SBP) control below 130 mmHg to improve outcomes. While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) time-series metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes.

METHODS: Blood pressure (n = 560) and HR (n = 680) time-series data from 31 patients were analyzed alongside preoperative aortic geometry metrics. Exploratory data analysis identified correlations between BP variability and outcomes. Stationarity tests were performed on time-series data to assess statistical properties. Logistic regression models incorporating hemodynamic metrics, along with CT-derived features, were used to predict TEVAR outcomes.

RESULTS: Successful outcomes correlated with greater diastolic blood pressure variability and strictly stationary SBP. Logistic regression models combining these metrics along with heart rate standard deviation and preoperative aortic geometry achieved 96.67% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy in predicting outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Post-TEVAR behaviors of hemodynamic variables are critical predictors of TEVAR success, with higher DBP standard deviation and strict stationarity of SBP significantly associated with favorable outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of hemodynamic variability and stationarity in optimizing post-TEVAR patient care.

While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) time-series metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes.

title: Retrograde tibial sheath approach after early failure of crossover endovascular therapy for a heavily calcified persistent sciatic artery.
abstract: Persistent sciatic artery is rare, and revascularization for persistent sciatic artery-associated chronic limb-threatening ischemia remains uncertain. A 95-year-old woman presented with a nonhealing toe ulcer and a heavily calcified persistent sciatic artery with multilevel occlusive disease. Initial crossover endovascular therapy was limited to balloon-based treatment because of device-delivery difficulty; early recurrent narrowing likely resulted from calcification-related recoil. Seven days later, retrograde posterior tibial sheath access enabled persistent sciatic artery stenting. Anterior tibial access with anterior tibial artery-posterior tibial artery pull-through facilitated anterior tibial artery angioplasty through the posterior tibial sheath, restoring inline flow to the dorsalis pedis artery without complications.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

title: Characteristics of pediatric central venous catheter malfunction and subsequent catheter-related deep vein thrombosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central venous catheters (CVCs) are increasingly placed in children; however, malfunction and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are reasons for frequent removal.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to evaluate variables associated with CVC malfunction and, subsequently, the development of CVC-related DVT (CR-DVT).

METHODS: This subanalysis of the multicenter, prospective Clot Incidence Rates in Central Lines study enrolled children aged 6 months to <18 years with newly placed peripherally inserted central catheters or tunneled lines from 2013 to 2018. Time from CVC placement to first malfunction was analyzed in the full cohort using univariable and multivariable Weibull regression. Among CVCs that malfunctioned, time from first malfunction to CR-DVT was analyzed to assess tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) use and subsequent thrombosis.

RESULTS: Malfunction occurred in 380/1951 CVCs (19.5%). In multivariable analysis, prior CVC use (hazard ratio [HR], 1.51; 95% CI, 1.19-1.90; P = .001), multilumen catheters (HR, 2.89; 95% CI, 2.30-3.65; P < .001), and >2 insertion attempts (HR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.42-3.45; P < .001) were associated with a higher risk of malfunction, whereas catheter size >4 French and interventional radiology placement were associated with a lower risk. Among malfunctioning CVCs, 22/380 (5.8%) developed CR-DVT, with a median time to CR-DVT of 6 days after malfunction. Increasing t-PA use showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher subsequent CR-DVT.

CONCLUSION: CVC malfunction is common and associated with several modifiable catheter-related factors. Six percent of malfunctioning CVCs develop CR-DVT, and repeated t-PA use and persistent CVC dysfunction may warrant further evaluation for underlying thrombosis.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to evaluate variables associated with CVC malfunction and, subsequently, the development of CVC-related DVT (CR-DVT). METHODS: This subanalysis of the multicenter, prospective Clot Incidence Rates in Central Lines study enrolled children aged 6 months to <18 years with newly placed peripherally inserted central catheters or tunneled lines from 2013 to 2018.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX.

title: Beyond Patency: Patient-Centered Outcomes and the Proposed Accountability Gap in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries 1-year mortality of 20% to 25%, comparable with many solid-organ malignancies. Technically successful revascularization, defined by anatomical patency, does not reliably deliver pain relief, restored function, or sustained quality of life. This narrative review synthesizes landmark randomized trials (BEST-CLI, BASIL-1, BASIL-2) and current European and United States guidelines, grading every claim with a scheme in which population indirectness downgrades design strength. We examine 4 domains of morbidity persisting after anatomically successful revascularization: mechanistically heterogeneous pain; functional and quality-of-life decline; psychological burden; and sustained health care use, including chronic opioid use (approximately 35%), unhealed wounds at 1 year (10%-32%), and unplanned 30-day readmission (approximately 25%). No patient-reported outcome measure has been validated specifically for CLTI or used as a co-primary trial endpoint. We propose an accountability gap: the under-measured transfer of unresolved morbidity from vascular services to primary care. We state it as a falsifiable prediction about the discrimination of patency rather than prevalence, with a pre-specified effect size, explicit treatment of death as a competing risk, and a core outcome battery justified against COSMIN criteria. Patient co-production is the indispensable next step.

title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis.

METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status.

CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline.
