title: Endovascular stenting of extracranial cervical artery dissections: A two-center study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Extracranial arterial dissections (EAD) are uncommon in the general population but represent a relatively frequent cause of ischemic stroke in young adults. Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-four EAD patients who underwent stenting were included. A standardized follow-up protocol at 12 months consisting of a clinical neurological assessment accompanied by imaging studies, including either Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Digital Subtraction Angiography was adopted.

RESULTS: In our cohort, most dissections were spontaneous (81 %) and predominantly involved the internal carotid artery (85 %), with acute stroke being the most common indication for stenting. Technical success was achieved in 85.7 % and complications occurred in 10 %. Three patients with initial stent implantation failure underwent successful secondary attempt. No significant predictors of technical success were identified. At discharge, good functional outcome was observed in 83 % of patients and at 12 months most followed patients showed favorable radiological results with high stent patency (86 %) and excellent clinical outcomes (mRS 0-2 in 97 %).

CONCLUSION: The results of our study suggest that for selected patients with medical therapy failure or hemodynamic compromise, stenting is a reasonable alternative. Given the limited evidence on indications, safety and efficacy, further randomized studies comparing stenting with medical management are warranted.

Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature.

title: Perceptions of decompressive craniectomy following endovascular thrombectomy in the Middle East and North Africa: A multi-specialty cross-sectional survey of attitudes, reported practices, and barriers.
abstract: Decompressive craniectomy (DC) can be a life-saving rescue therapy for malignant cerebral edema after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), yet DC practices following EVT have not previously been examined across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). We conducted a web-based, bilingual (English/Arabic) cross-sectional survey of physicians involved in acute stroke care across 15 MENA countries (January-March 2025) using a 22-item instrument that underwent expert content-validity review (S-CVI/UA = 0.86) and cognitive-interview pilot testing, to describe self-reported attitudes, perceived practices, and barriers regarding DC after EVT, and to determine whether key findings remained consistent among clinicians with the most direct relevant experience. Of 440 physicians invited, 179 responded; five respondents from zero-EVT-volume institutions were excluded, yielding an analytic cohort of 174 (response rate 41%) from 13 countries, of whom 49% (n = 85) were neurosurgeons. Eighty-four percent of respondents endorsed DC over medical management in selected patients, but only 51% perceived DC was performed in a timely manner "always/often." The mean physician-estimated, recall-based consent rate was 52% (SD 19%), with a Gulf Cooperation Council versus North African difference (59% vs. 44%, p < 0.001) that persisted when restricted to clinicians with direct family-meeting or operative involvement. Leading perceived barriers were patient/family preferences (79%), surgical resource constraints (55%), and delayed detection (30%). These findings, which reflect physician perceptions rather than institutionally verified practice, support development of culturally adapted consent pathways, standardized DC candidacy algorithms, regionalized stroke networks, and a prospective MENA stroke registry to confirm whether these perception-based signals correspond to actual clinical practice and outcomes.

title: Adjuvant Systemic Hypothermia During Mechanical Thrombectomy (ReCCLAIM II): A Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypothermia reduces ischemic injury in preclinical stroke models, yet translation into the clinical setting remains challenging. We aimed to assess the feasibility of inducing adjuvant systemic hypothermia among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke during mechanical thrombectomy.

METHODS: This was a phase II randomized feasibility-controlled trial involving 10 sites in the United States, conducted between May 2019 and May 2024. All eligible patients had confirmed proximal middle cerebral artery or internal carotid artery occlusions, an Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score of 6 to 10, and symptom onset within 24 hours. Patients underwent mechanical thrombectomy and were randomly assigned to either treatment with adjuvant hypothermia using a novel intravascular cooling catheter or standard of care. The primary feasibility end points were the ability to achieve a target temperature of <34 °C within 1 hour of arterial puncture and overall door-to-reperfusion times. The primary safety end point was core-laboratory-adjudicated hemorrhagic conversion within 36 hours, and secondary end points included final infarct volume and serious adverse events.

RESULTS: A total of 95 patients were enrolled (29 in the roll-in phase and 66 randomized). The mean age of the randomized cohort was 65±12 years, with a median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 15. Among patients in the treatment arm, 30 of 33 (91%) achieved hypothermia within 1 hour of arterial puncture during thrombectomy, and 23 of 33 (70%) patients were at target temperature (<34 °C) before reperfusion. The median time to hypothermia was 10 minutes (interquartile range [IQR], 7-22) from arterial puncture. There were no significant differences in door-to-reperfusion times (hypothermia: 95 minutes [IQR, 54-116] versus control: 94 minutes [IQR, 77-121]; P=0.70). Final infarct volumes were numerically lower in the hypothermia treatment arm (hypothermia: 11 cm3 [IQR, 5-42] versus control: 30 cm3 [IQR, 6-80]; P=0.13), with no significant differences in the rates of hemorrhagic conversion or pneumonia. There was a higher number of serious adverse events in the hypothermia arm (45.5% versus 24.2%; P=0.12), although the trial was not powered for differences in serious adverse events or clinical efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first clinical trial to demonstrate the feasibility of early and rapid systemic hypothermia as an adjunct therapy during mechanical thrombectomy without delaying time to reperfusion. The potential impact on infarct volumes and serious adverse events, however, warrants further investigation.

englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Hypothermia reduces ischemic injury in preclinical stroke models, yet translation into the clinical setting remains challenging. We aimed to assess the feasibility of inducing adjuvant systemic hypothermia among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke during mechanical thrombectomy. METHODS: This was a phase II randomized feasibility-controlled trial involving 10 sites in the United States, conducted between May 2019 and May 2024.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Standalone Endovascular Embolization for Growing Meningiomas: A Multicenter Study Protocol.
abstract: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth. The primary end point is tumor growth control at 180 days after treatment, defined as a stable or reduced tumor volume based on quantitative volumetric assessment of the contrast-enhancing portion on magnetic resonance imaging. The secondary end points include the tumor volume change rate, embolized vessels, embolic materials, embolization results and characteristics, procedure-related complications, perioperative complications, functional outcomes (Karnofsky Performance Status and modified Rankin Scale), changes in clinical symptoms, and the need for additional treatment. Exploratory analyses will also assess the association between intratumoral penetration of embolic material and treatment outcomes. Patient recruitment is ongoing, and the results will be reported upon completion of the study. This study represents a prospective attempt to evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization for meningiomas. If safe tumor growth control can be achieved, this study may provide preliminary evidence supporting standalone embolization as a potential less-invasive treatment strategy.
englishSummary: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth.

title: Global Disparity Within the Management of Traumatic Abdominal Vascular Injuries: Analysis of a Global Dataset.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular injuries are common to trauma and carry a high risk to limb and life. Integrating specialist vascular care into existing trauma systems is essential; however, global data on this topic remains limited. This study describes global patterns of abdominal vascular trauma, through secondary analysis of the Global Outcomes After Laparotomy for Trauma (GOAL-Trauma) study dataset, examining system- and patient-level differences across resource settings.

METHODS: Patients of any age with blunt or penetrating trauma who underwent an abdominal vascular procedure during trauma laparotomy were included. Patient characteristics, injury patterns, peri-operative factors, and outcomes were recorded. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics and differences across Human Development Index (HDI) tertiles were analyzed with the Kruskal-Wallis or χ2 tests, where appropriate.

RESULTS: A total of 178 patients from 82 hospitals across 33 countries were included, representing one in 10 patients (178 of 1769) of the original dataset. A higher proportion of patients had vascular procedures in the upper HDI tertile (64 of 492, 13.0%), compared to middle (82 of 714, 11.5%) and lower (32 of 563, 5.7%) HDI tertiles. The median time from injury to operation was 5.0 hours (IQR 2.0-9.0). Among patients who were hypotensive on presentation, time from arrival to operation was significantly longer in the lower HDI tertile (p = 0.033). The most common regions of vascular injury were the inferior vena cava (37 patients, 20.8%) and iliac vein (30 patients, 16.9%). Thirty day post-operative mortality was 17.4% (31 of 178 patients), with only around half of the patients (94 of 178, 52.8%) discharged to their usual place of residence.

CONCLUSIONS: As trauma systems become integrated into national healthcare services, prioritizing vascular care is crucial. There remains considerable variation in the provision of vascular services in trauma globally, yet given the time-critical nature of vascular injuries, it is essential to ensure effective, integrated care pathways.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited.

METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12.

DISCUSSION: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.Clinical Trial Registration: http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population.

title: The Central Coupler of ClpXP Controls Intersubunit Communication and Couples Intrasubunit Chemical Energy with Force Generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Image-Guided Navigation in Complex Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex endovascular aortic repair exposes patients and operators to substantial radiation, contrast, and long procedures. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image-guided navigation, based on cloud-based 3-dimensional image fusion, has been proposed to improve intraoperative guidance, but its comparative benefit is uncertain.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (last search July 2025) for studies comparing AI-assisted image-guided navigation with conventional fluoroscopy and digital subtraction angiography during complex endovascular aortic repair. No navigation platform was prespecified. Random-effects meta-analyses yielded mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was quantified with I2. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Three retrospective cohorts (332 patients; 189 AI, 143 control), all evaluating one cloud-based platform (Cydar EV), were eligible. AI-assisted navigation was associated with a lower radiation dose (2 studies, 216 patients; MD -1,435.85 mGy, 95% CI -2,208.84 to -662.86; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were found in fluoroscopy time (MD -11.04 min, 95% CI -25.37 to 3.29; I2 = 65%), operative time (MD -16.39 min, 95% CI -37.21 to 4.42; I2 = 0%), or contrast volume (MD -30.59 mL, 95% CI -73.95 to 12.76; I2 = 94%). Mortality and major adverse events (single studies) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSION: Cydar EV-assisted navigation may reduce radiation dose during complex endovascular aortic repair, but evidence is limited to retrospective studies of a single platform and does not establish a class effect for other AI-assisted navigation systems. Prospective comparative studies across platforms are needed.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (last search July 2025) for studies comparing AI-assisted image-guided navigation with conventional fluoroscopy and digital subtraction angiography during complex endovascular aortic repair.

title: Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction Models for Peripheral Artery Disease: A Nationally Representative Analysis of NHANES 1999-2004.
abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated the association between small dense low-density lipoprotein (sdLDL) and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and developed prediction models using NHANES 1999-2004.MethodsThis weighted cross-sectional study included 3,415 participants (3,227 without PAD and 188 with PAD). PAD was defined by ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.90; participants with ABI ≥1.40 or missing ABI were excluded. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed the association between sdLDL and PAD. For machine learning, complete-case data (n=2,828) were split into training (70%) and test (30%) sets before feature selection and preprocessing. Correlation screening, LASSO, encoding, standardization, and SMOTE were restricted to the training set. Nine algorithms were evaluated using discrimination and calibration metrics.ResultssdLDL was not independently associated with PAD in the fully adjusted model (OR=1.01, 95% CI 0.94-1.10, P=0.69). LASSO retained eight predictor domains: age, body mass index, C-reactive protein, education, estimated glomerular filtration rate, hypertension, poverty-income ratio, and smoking. In the test set, gradient boosting machine achieved the highest AUC (0.833, 95% CI 0.777-0.889), followed by logistic regression (0.819) and XGBoost (0.811). SHAP analysis highlighted age, eGFR, and smoking-related variables as important contributors.Conclusions: sdLDL was not independently associated with PAD. Several models showed acceptable discrimination, with GBM performing numerically best and logistic regression remaining competitive. External validation in contemporary cohorts is required.

title: Management of intraprocedural complications from thoracic central venous recanalization: Hemothorax and pericardial tamponade.
abstract: Thoracic central venous recanalization is increasingly performed by vascular interventional radiologists to restore venous access and alleviate symptoms of central venous obstruction in patients with chronic, occlusive disease. While the procedure offers substantial clinical benefit, it carries risk of life-threatening intraprocedural complications including hemothorax and pericardial tamponade. These complications arise from the unique proximity of thoracic central veins to the potential spaces of the pleura and pericardium combined with the significant mechanical forces required to traverse and reopen fibrotic, chronically occluded venous segments. These complications may occur suddenly, requiring immediate recognition and decisive management to prevent rapid deterioration and death. This article reviews risk factors for iatrogenic hemothorax and pericardial tamponade, and provides a practical guide for managing these emergencies with discussion of clinical evaluation, procedural steps, and post-procedural management for emergent chest tube placement, pericardiocentesis, and stent graft placement.

title: Advanced extravascular bypass techniques for the end-stage thoracic central venous occlusion patient.
abstract: In cases where blunt recanalization of central venous occlusions fails, more advanced techniques such as sharp recanalization and radiofrequency guidewire recanalization may be needed to traverse the occlusion. However, when these fail or are infeasible, several additional techniques are available, which entail creating a path outside of the vein lumen. For patients who are dependent on central venous access, such as for hemodialysis, an inability to achieve access to the right atrium will result in inevitable mortality; thus a thorough understanding of all techniques is important. This article describes advanced extravascular techniques to achieve access to the right atrium.

title: A last resort that works: Distal deep vein arterialization in no-option diabetic critical limb-threatening ischemia: A prospective interventional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease characterized by ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcers, and gangrene. In patients with "no-option" CLTI, distal deep vein arterialization (DDVA) offers a potential limb salvage strategy. We prospectively studied the outcomes of open DDVA in patients with diabetes with CLTI.

METHODS: This prospective interventional case series included 10 patients with diabetes with CLTI (rest pain, ulcers, or gangrene) confirmed using duplex ultrasonography and CT angiography underwent open DDVA. Vascular anastomosis was performed between the posterior tibial artery (PTA, n = 9) or anterior tibial artery (ATA, n = 1) and one of its venae comitantes in the tarsal tunnel. Demographics, operative details, and postoperative outcomes were analyzed. The outcomes of interest included wound healing, pain relief, limb salvage and mortality.

RESULTS: The cohort included 8 men and 2 women, with a mean age 59.6 years. All patients underwent DDVA between the posterior/anterior tibial artery and corresponding vena comitans. By 1 month, 6 patients achieved complete wound healing, whereas 4 had small residual ulcers that fully healed by 2 months, and mean VAS pain scores improved from 7.7 to 1.8. at 2 months, CT angiography confirmed patent arterio-venous anastomoses in all patients. At an average follow-up of 12.5 ± 5.9 months, all patient achieved ambulatory, ulcer free, and major amputation-free survival.

CONCLUSION: Open DDVA is a feasible and effective revascularization option in no-option diabetic CLTI, which offers encouraging early results in limb salvage, wound healing, and pain relief. Larger studies with longer follow-up and objective perfusion assessment are warranted.

In patients with "no-option" CLTI, distal deep vein arterialization (DDVA) offers a potential limb salvage strategy. We prospectively studied the outcomes of open DDVA in patients with diabetes with CLTI.

title: Endovascular Management of Life-Threatening Hemoptysis in Rare Pulmonary Vascular Diseases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Massive hemoptysis in patients with complex pulmonary vascular disease is difficult to manage because surgery is frequently contraindicated, making endovascular therapy an important treatment option.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 3 patients with life-threatening hemoptysis caused by distinct rare etiologies: systemic-to-pulmonary collateral bleeding in Eisenmenger syndrome due to patent ductus arteriosus, complex collateral bleeding associated with left upper lobe aspergilloma, and post-tubercular collateral hemorrhage. Angiography-guided transcatheter embolization was individualized using particles, coils, and a vascular plug according to vascular anatomy. All patients achieved immediate hemostasis without major procedural complications, with sustained freedom from recurrent hemoptysis during 6-12 months of follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Successful bronchial artery embolization depends on meticulous angiographic evaluation and anatomy-driven device selection. This series demonstrates the versatility of endovascular techniques, including vascular plug implantation for high-flow bronchial collaterals in cases where conventional embolization is technically challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Individualized, anatomy-guided endovascular therapy provides a safe, effective, and organ-preserving treatment for life-threatening hemoptysis in complex pulmonary vascular disease. Careful procedural planning is essential for durable clinical success.

title: Risk-benefit profile of upper versus lower extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal insertion site for peripherally inserted central catheters in neonates remains uncertain. International guidelines differ in their recommendations regarding upper- versus lower-extremity placement, and existing systematic reviews are limited by small samples, narrow outcome coverage, or outdated evidence.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the potential risk-benefit profile of upper- versus lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 6, 2026, for studies comparing upper- versus lower-extremity placement in neonates. Primary outcomes were venous thromboembolism, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter tip malposition; secondary outcomes included phlebitis, catheter migration, catheter leakage, catheter occlusion, catheter breakage, total complications, dwell time, unplanned removal, pericardial or pleural effusion, sepsis, and all-cause mortality. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Crude estimates were pooled, sparse and heterogeneous adjusted estimates were summarised narratively, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.

RESULTS: Twenty-one observational studies from 10 countries, involving 15,289 catheters, were included. For primary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism (RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; P = 0.017; low certainty) but higher risks of central line-associated bloodstream infection (RR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.95; P = 0.018; very low certainty) and catheter tip malposition (RR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.61-4.30; P < 0.001; very low certainty). For secondary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with lower phlebitis risk (RR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.94; P = 0.022; low certainty) but higher risks of catheter migration (RR = 1.74, 95% CI 1.27-2.38; P < 0.001; low certainty), catheter leakage (RR = 2.24, 95% CI 1.35-3.73; P = 0.002; moderate certainty), and a marginally higher risk of unplanned removal (RR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.00-1.51; P = 0.048; very low certainty). A post hoc exploratory analysis suggested a possible higher risk of pericardial or pleural effusion (RR = 3.79, 95% CI 1.20-12.02; P = 0.024; very low certainty). No statistically significant between-site differences were observed for other secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Crude observational evidence suggested a potential bidirectional risk-benefit profile across catheter-related outcomes. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because non-randomised designs remain susceptible to residual confounding. The observed associations may inform risk-informed, individualised site selection but do not establish a universally preferred site. Prospective studies with standardised outcomes and adjusted analyses are needed.

title: Impact of portable point-of-care ultrasound on clinical decision-making and referrals in general practice: a cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in general practice, but evidence on its impact on clinical decision-making when performed with portable devices remains limited. Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

METHODS: Cross-sectional observational study conducted over 12 months in a primary care centre in Barcelona, Spain. Three general practitioners with accredited training performed POCUS examinations using portable devices in 108 patients. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥15 years requiring clinical ultrasound. Clinical management plans were documented before and after POCUS using same questionnaire. Changes in decision-making and referral patterns were analysed using McNemar's test. Reporting followed the STROBE statement for cross-sectional studies.

RESULTS: POCUS changed clinical decision-making in 66.7% of cases. Intended referrals to secondary care decreased from 44.4% to 25.0% (absolute risk reduction 19.4%, 95% CI 8.4-30.5%, relative risk reduction 44%). Musculoskeletal examinations represented 73.1% of cases, with management modified in 63.3%. All seven patients with suspected deep vein thrombosis were managed without hospital referral. Referrals for conventional radiology ultrasound decreased from 32.4% to 12.0%, while GP-performed invasive procedures (infiltrations) increased from 0.9% to 18.5%.

CONCLUSION: Portable POCUS substantially influences clinical decision-making and reduces secondary care referrals in general practice. Further research is needed, especially longitudinal studies, to evaluate whether these changes translate into improved health outcomes for patients.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

title: Design and baseline characteristics of the CagriSema cardiovascular outcomes trial (REDEFINE 3).
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) is a fixed-dose combination of the amylin receptor agonist cagrilintide and the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide administered subcutaneously once weekly. CagriSema has demonstrated significant weight reduction and improved glycemic control in participants with excess adiposity and type 2 diabetes (T2D).

METHODS: REDEFINE 3 is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving participants with established cardiovascular disease (CVD) and body mass index (BMI) ≥25.0 kg/m2 with/without T2D randomized to CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg or placebo, plus standard of care. The safety objective is to confirm noninferiority of CagriSema compared with placebo on cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (MACE-3). The efficacy objective is to confirm the superiority of CagriSema compared with placebo on cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or revascularization (MACE-4).

RESULTS: Between 1/2023 and 12/2024, 7,076 adults at 575 sites in 24 countries were randomized. Mean age at baseline was 66 years. BMI ≥30 kg/m2 was present in 76% of participants (n = 5,370). In participants with T2D (n = 4,348, 61%), the mean duration of T2D was 12 years and mean glycated hemoglobin was 7.7%. Most participants had a prior myocardial infarction (n = 4,369, 62%). Prior stroke (n = 1,311, 19%) and peripheral arterial disease (n = 769, 11%) were less common, and 617 participants (9%) had more than one qualifying CVD criteria.

CONCLUSION: The REDEFINE 3 trial will provide evidence regarding the cardiovascular safety and efficacy of CagriSema, a novel fixed-dose combination therapy that could improve cardiovascular outcomes in a broad population of people with established CVD and excess adiposity.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The REDEFINE 3 trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05669755).

title: Supraclavicular artery island flap for head and neck reconstruction: Our experience and exploratory analysis of risk factors.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The supraclavicular artery island flap (SCAIF) is being increasingly used for reconstruction of complex head and neck defects as an alternative to the traditional free flap or pedicled pectoralis flap. Here, we describe our experience with SCAIF for oncologic head and neck reconstruction and aim to identify patient factors associated with flap complications.

METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent SCAIF reconstruction at a tertiary academic center was conducted between 2015 and 2023 (n=23). Collected variables included patient characteristics, operative parameters, and postoperative outcomes.

RESULTS: The mean patient age was 70.2 years. Six patients had a history of prior radiation, and 6 underwent ipsilateral neck dissection. Twelve patients received adjuvant radiation following flap transfer. Minor flap-related complications included delayed wound healing (n = 3) and partial flap necrosis (n = 6). One patient experienced total flap necrosis. Systemic complications included myocardial infarction (n = 2), pulmonary embolism (n = 1), atrial fibrillation (n = 1), and deep vein thrombosis (n = 1). Advanced age was associated with recipient-site complications (p = 0.018). Elevated body mass index was associated with systemic complications, longer ICU stays, and increased total hospital length of stay (p=0.036, p = 0.008, and p = 0.001, respectively). History of vascular disease and diabetes mellitus were associated with flap necrosis and delayed wound healing, respectively (p=0.025 and p=0.004). Longer operative time was associated with flap dehiscence (p=0.002).

CONCLUSION: SCAIF is a reliable and versatile reconstructive option for oncologic head and neck defects, including in previously operated or irradiated necks. Caution is warranted particularly in patients with diabetes or vascular disease, as vascular comorbidities appear to be more clinically precise risk factors than chronological age alone. Elevated body mass index also warrants consideration.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: The supraclavicular artery island flap (SCAIF) is being increasingly used for reconstruction of complex head and neck defects as an alternative to the traditional free flap or pedicled pectoralis flap. Here, we describe our experience with SCAIF for oncologic head and neck reconstruction and aim to identify patient factors associated with flap complications. METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent SCAIF reconstruction at a tertiary academic center was conducted between 2015 and 2023 (n=23).

title: Clinical and economic impact of central venous catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infections in pediatric intensive care units: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Central venous catheter-associated and catheter-related bloodstream infections may increase mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs in critically ill children. This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible. The exposure will be catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infection, compared with patients from the same catheter-exposed source population who are infection-free at the relevant risk time. Mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs are co-primary outcomes. Multiple bibliographic databases, gray-literature sources, and study registries will be searched without date restrictions. Two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data, assess risk of bias, and evaluate certainty. Meta-analysis will be performed when studies are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis will be used.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The review is expected to clarify the magnitude and methodological robustness of the clinical and economic consequences of these infections and identify priorities for future pediatric intensive care research.

This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible.

title: Modified Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair for Aortic Coarctation with Segmental Post-stenotic Aneurysms.
abstract: Aortic coarctation can be complicated by descending thoracic aortic aneurysms in adults. A 31-year-old man presented with exertional chest pain radiating to the back. Preoperative evaluation showed a 27-mmHg arm-leg systolic pressure gradient, echocardiographic coarctation with a 10-mm narrowest diameter and 25-mmHg gradient, and computed tomography showing two segmental post-stenotic aneurysms, the largest measuring 62 mm. He underwent one-stage modified frozen elephant trunk repair using a Medtronic thoracic stent graft sutured to a surgical graft. The postoperative gradient decreased to 5 mmHg, with stable 9-month follow-up.

title: Inflammatory and Hemostatic Biomarker Response after Endovenous Laser Ablation versus High Ligation and Stripping: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate and compare perioperative inflammatory response, primary hemostasis, and coagulation cascade activation between endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) and high ligation and stripping (HLS) in patients with great saphenous vein (GSV) incompetence.

METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included 39 patients with unilateral GSV incompetence (Clinical Etiologic Anatomic Pathophysiologic C2-C6), randomized to EVLA using a 1,470 nm radial fiber (n = 21) or conventional HLS (n = 18). Blood samples were collected at baseline, 8 hrs, 7 days, and 30 days postoperatively to assess inflammatory cytokines, adhesion molecules, and acute-phase markers. The primary endpoint was differences in biomarker levels between techniques over time.

RESULTS: The EVLA group demonstrated significantly earlier return to daily activities compared to HLS (17 vs. 30 days, P < 0.0001). Distinct inflammatory patterns were observed: EVLA showed increased P-selectin at 1 week and elevated interleukin-1, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and interleukin-6 at 1 month, indicating a delayed inflammatory response. In contrast, HLS demonstrated higher von Willebrand factor levels at 1 week, suggesting earlier endothelial activation. No cases of deep vein thrombosis or endovenous heat-induced thrombosis were observed.

CONCLUSION: EVLA and HLS exhibit distinct temporal patterns of inflammatory and hemostatic activation. EVLA is associated with a delayed pro-inflammatory response, whereas HLS demonstrates earlier endothelial activation. Despite these differences, both techniques showed similar safety profiles. These findings may contribute to individualized thrombotic risk stratification and perioperative management strategies in venous surgery.

METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included 39 patients with unilateral GSV incompetence (Clinical Etiologic Anatomic Pathophysiologic C2-C6), randomized to EVLA using a 1,470 nm radial fiber (n = 21) or conventional HLS (n = 18). Blood samples were collected at baseline, 8 hrs, 7 days, and 30 days postoperatively to assess inflammatory cytokines, adhesion molecules, and acute-phase markers.

title: Outcomes of Open and Endovascular Interventions in Octogenarians with Infrainguinal Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite prior studies showing that lower extremity revascularization in the elderly population could be performed safely, there continues to be significant debate regarding the outcomes in octogenarians with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). The choice between bypass and endovascular therapy (ET) in this population is controversial. This study aimed to examine outcomes of the bypass and ET in octogenarians presenting with CLTI using the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database.

METHODS: The VQI database was queried for all patients with infrainguinal CLTI that received bypass or ET between 2016 and 2023. Two cohorts, octogenarians (80-89 years old) and nonoctogenarians (51-79 years old) were compared. Three types of revascularizations were compared within the age categories: bypass with a single-segment great saphenous vein (SSGSV), bypass with an alternative conduit (AC), and ET. Primary outcomes included postoperative myocardial infarction (MI) and 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included 1-year rates of death, major amputation and major amputation/death. Multivariate logistic regression model was used for MI and 30-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier survival and time-varying Cox regression analyses were used for 1-year outcomes.

RESULTS: Data from a total of 134,808 limbs and 91,938 patients were analyzed (octogenarian = 25,547, 18.9%). Octogenarians had approximately two-fold higher 30-day mortality across all revascularization strategies compared to nonoctogenarians. In octogenarians, the rates of SSGSV, AC, and ET were 6.3%, 7.4%, and 86.3%, respectively. After adjusting for potential confounders, ET was associated with lower odds of postoperative MI compared to SSGSV and AC bypasses, with no significant difference in 30-day mortality by revascularization type. At 1 year, AC bypass (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 1.30 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.20-1.41]; P < 0.001) and ET (aHR = 1.18 [95% CI: 1.10-1.28]; P < 0.001) were associated with higher hazards of major amputation/death compared to SSGSV bypass in octogenarians. ET had lower hazards of major amputation compared to SSGSV bypass (aHR = 0.78 [95% CI: 0.70-0.86]; P < 0.001) and AC bypass (aHR = 0.64 [95% CI: 0.57-0.70]; P < 0.001), as well as lower hazards of major amputation/death compared to AC bypass (aHR = 0.91 [95% CI: 0.85-0.97]; P = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Octogenarians experience substantially higher perioperative mortality across all revascularization strategies. In octogenarians with CLTI, ET was the predominant approach and was associated with lower postoperative MI risk compared to bypass independent of the conduit. ET had higher hazards of combined major amputation/death compared to SSGSV bypass, driven solely by higher mortality. The higher mortality in ET may reflect these patients' higher overall risk profile. Moreover, ET was associated with lower hazards of combined major amputation/death compared to AC bypass.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Despite prior studies showing that lower extremity revascularization in the elderly population could be performed safely, there continues to be significant debate regarding the outcomes in octogenarians with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). The choice between bypass and endovascular therapy (ET) in this population is controversial. This study aimed to examine outcomes of the bypass and ET in octogenarians presenting with CLTI using the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database.

title: Fragility analysis should complement statistical reporting in thrombosis trials: lessons from reduced-dose direct oral anticoagulants for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism.
abstract: Randomized trials and meta-analyses in thrombosis are traditionally interpreted using effect estimates, confidence intervals, and P values. While indispensable, these metrics often provide limited insight into the robustness of trials reporting statistically significant findings. Fragility analysis offers a complementary approach by quantifying the minimum number of event-status changes that would reverse statistical significance. Despite increasing adoption across oncology, ophthalmology, orthopedics, and cardiovascular medicine, fragility analysis remains underutilized in thrombosis studies. Using a recent meta-analysis comparing reduced- vs full-dose direct oral anticoagulants for extended treatment of cancer-associated venous thromboembolism as an illustrative example, we demonstrate how fragility analysis provides additional context regarding the stability of trial findings. More importantly, we argue that fragility analysis should become a routine adjunct to conventional statistical reporting in thrombosis trials and systematic reviews to facilitate interpretation of evidence, improve transparency, and enhance shared decision-making.

title: Thrombin generation in critically ill adults: a systematic review of venous thromboembolism and pharmacological thromboprophylaxis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains an important complication in critically ill adults despite standard pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis. Thrombin generation assays (TGAs) offer a global functional assessment of coagulation by capturing the kinetics and magnitude of thrombin formation and may complement conventional measures of coagulation such as anti-Xa activity.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of thrombin generation with VTE and its use as a pharmacodynamic measure of thromboprophylaxis in critically ill adults.

METHODS: The review was conducted according to JBI methodology and reported per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to December 18, 2025. We included studies of adults (≥18 years) managed in high-acuity or intensive care settings with TGA measurements reported in relation to VTE incidence or thromboprophylaxis effect.

RESULTS: We included 15 eligible prospective studies comprising 2250 patients (9 surgical trauma cohorts, 4 medical intensive care unit [ICU] cohorts, and 2 mixed ICU cohorts). Calibrated automated thrombography was the most used TGA platform (80.0%). Eleven studies (73.3%) evaluated associations between TGA and VTE incidence, with inconsistent findings. Some trauma cohorts identified shorter time-to-peak thrombin or lag time as predictors of VTE, while other studies found no significant associations. Of 8 studies (53.3%) assessing TGA pharmacodynamics, 7 measured anti-Xa activity, which correlated with lower endogenous thrombin potential and peak thrombin.

CONCLUSIONS: TGA most consistently served as a pharmacodynamic measure of low-molecular-weight heparin effect: anti-Xa activity correlated with suppressed endogenous thrombin potential and peak thrombin. TGA did not reliably predict VTE, though shorter time-to-peak and lag time preceded thrombosis in trauma cohorts. TGA should be advanced as a coagulation-phenotyping tool in prospective ICU studies with standardized assays, consistent sampling in relation to dose timing, and concurrent anti-Xa and thrombin generation measurement.

Thrombin generation assays (TGAs) offer a global functional assessment of coagulation by capturing the kinetics and magnitude of thrombin formation and may complement conventional measures of coagulation such as anti-Xa activity. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of thrombin generation with VTE and its use as a pharmacodynamic measure of thromboprophylaxis in critically ill adults.

title: [Complex femoral access in TAVI: From risk identification to alternative approaches].
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the reference treatment for severe aortic stenosis across all surgical risk categories. Transfemoral access remains the default approach, but vascular complications, especially in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), can limit its feasibility. This review follows a three-step structure. First, when to suspect complex femoral access? The concept of "hostile" access (small calibre, severe calcification, tortuosity) and the Hostile and Passage-Puncture scores allow this risk to be stratified from preoperative imaging. Second, how to manage a complex femoral access? Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) and orbital atherectomy expand eligibility for transfemoral access in severe calcified PAD, dedicated techniques (buddy wire, snare) address aortic and iliofemoral tortuosity, and careful puncture-site planning limits local complications. Third, when and which alternative access to consider when transfemoral access remains unfeasible? Transaxillary/subclavian, transcarotid, transcaval or, more rarely, transapical/transaortic, are associated with different risks and selection criteria. As TAVI expands to lower-risk populations, a structured vascular access strategy remains essential to procedural success and to decrease vascular complications.

Transfemoral access remains the default approach, but vascular complications, especially in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), can limit its feasibility. title: Surgery for Acute Type A Aortic Dissection on Preoperative Anticoagulants and Antiplatelet Agents.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients taking direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin, or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) who present with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) pose unique challenges. Our objective was to investigate the surgical outcomes of this patient population.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 20,530 patients who underwent first-time sternotomy repair of ATAAD was performed in The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database from 2017 to 2022. Propensity score matching was used to pair each patient on DOAC (n = 625), warfarin (n = 245), and DAPT (n = 525) with 2 controls. Outcomes included operative mortality and reoperation for bleeding.

RESULTS: Compared with the mortality in matched controls, mortality was higher in patients on DOACs (24.8% vs 17.9%; odds ratio [95% CI]: 1.5 [1.2, 2.0]; P < .001), warfarin (26.7% vs 19.2%; OR [95% CI]: 1.6 [1.1, 2.4]; P = .02), or DAPT (27.4% vs 20.1%; OR [95% CI]: 1.5 [1.2, 2.0]; P = .001). Reoperation for bleeding was higher for DOACs (12.0% vs 7.0%; OR [95% CI]: 1.8 [1.3, 2.5]; P = .001) and DAPT (15.2% vs 7.3%; OR [95% CI]: 2.2 [1.6, 3.2]; P < .001), and a similar trend was noted for warfarin (11.4% vs 7.8%; OR [95% CI]: 1.5 [0.9, 2.6]; P = .11). Most patients on a DOAC (76.5% [478 of 625]) or DAPT (71.2% [374 of 525]) underwent surgery on the day of admission. Although there was a nonsignificant difference toward lower mortality for patients on a DOAC who had surgery on day ≥1 (17.4% vs 25.0%; P = .08), there was no difference for those on DAPT.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing first-time surgery for ATAAD who were on DOACs, DAPT, or warfarin preoperatively had increased bleeding complications and mortality. For those on DOACs or DAPT, further study is required to investigate whether delaying surgery impacts outcomes.

Our objective was to investigate the surgical outcomes of this patient population. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 20,530 patients who underwent first-time sternotomy repair of ATAAD was performed in The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database from 2017 to 2022.

title: Impact of the infusion line on co-loading and highly diluted norepinephrine administration through a single peripheral venous catheter: An in vitro simulation of the infusion protocol used during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid crystalloid co-loading and prophylactic norepinephrine may share a peripheral intravenous catheter during cesarean delivery. We assessed whether infusion-system architecture alters fluid and drug delivery.

METHODS: Six infusion-system configurations were tested in vitro. Norepinephrine 8 μg/mL was infused at 30 mL/h (4 μg/min) while 1000 mL saline was delivered from a pressure bag initially inflated to 300 mmHg. Outcomes were crystalloid volume delivered during the first 10 min, time within the norepinephrine target range of 3.5-4.5 μg/min, and the proportion of measurements outside ±12.5% of the configuration-specific median.

RESULTS: Crystalloid volume at 10 min ranged from 596 ± 30 to 947 ± 30 mL between configurations (P < 0.001). Time within the norepinephrine target range ranged from 32.8 ± 6.1% to 71.4 ± 9.9% (P = 0.019), and instability ranged from 23.8 ± 6.2% to 54.6 ± 13.0% (P < 0.001). Among the configurations tested, those in which pressurized crystalloid entered downstream of the convergence of actively controlled drug infusions showed the most favorable balance between crystalloid delivery and norepinephrine stability.

DISCUSSION: Infusion-system architecture influenced both rapid crystalloid delivery and distal norepinephrine stability. When pressurized crystalloid and actively controlled drugs share a peripheral intravenous catheter, a distal crystalloid entry may represent a favorable system architecture. Clinical relevance requires further evaluation.

We assessed whether infusion-system architecture alters fluid and drug delivery. METHODS: Six infusion-system configurations were tested in vitro.

title: Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 Encephalitis With Gram-Negative Bacteremia in a Kidney Transplant Recipient With a Failing Allograft.
abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis is extremely rare after kidney transplantation. We report a 37-year-old man who had received a deceased donor kidney transplant 16 years previously and had chronic allograft dysfunction. Before his first infectious episode, return to dialysis was anticipated, and arteriovenous fistula formation had been planned. Baseline serum creatinine was 3.55 mg/dL, which corresponded to an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 22 mL/min/1.73 m2. The most recent outpatient assessment before infection showed a serum creatinine of 4.3 mg/dL, a spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 2.19 g/g, and a cyclosporine trough level of 58 ng/mL. In January 2026, the patient was hospitalized with a lower respiratory tract infection, cytopenias, bleeding manifestations, and worsening graft function that required transient hemodialysis. In April 2026, he was readmitted with fever and later developed a seizure. Cerebrospinal fluid showed pleocytosis, and herpes simplex virus type 1 DNA was detected by FilmArray. Blood cultures were positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae. The patient improved after renal-adjusted acyclovir and broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy. A few weeks later, he was readmitted with graft pyelonephritis and progressive graft failure that led to chronic hemodialysis and further reduction of immunosuppression. Although this work is based on a single observation, this case illustrated how immune dysfunction associated with advanced allograft failure may compound ongoing immunosuppression and emphasized that bacterial infection does not exclude concurrent herpes simplex virus encephalitis when neurological manifestations develop.

We report a 37-year-old man who had received a deceased donor kidney transplant 16 years previously and had chronic allograft dysfunction. Before his first infectious episode, return to dialysis was anticipated, and arteriovenous fistula formation had been planned.

title: Embolization of the Transhepatic or Trans-Splenic Route With a Gel Foam, N-Butyl Cyanoacrylate and Lipiodol Combination in Liver Transplant Patients After Percutaneous Portal Vein Treatment.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Portal vein stenosis or occlusion following liver transplant can greatly affect patient outcomes, potentially leading to graft loss. Percutaneous treatments, including balloon angioplasty and stenting, require a transhepatic or transsplenic route. This study investigated the efficacy of embolizing the parenchymal tract with a combination of gel foam and an N - butyl cyanoacrylate - lipiodol mixture in transplant recipients following portal vein interventions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our study followed 23 procedures performed on 16 liver transplant patients ( 7 pediatric, 9 adult ) seen between January 2020 and November 2024. Of these, 21 procedures involved the transhepatic route and 2 involved the transsplenic route. Patients were diagnosed with portal vein stenosis or occlusions through color Doppler ultrasonography or computed tomography scans and then underwent balloon angioplasty or stenting. Parenchymal tract embolization was performed with gel foam, followed by N - butyl cyanoacrylate and lipiodol.

RESULTS: All procedures were successful, with no bleeding complications. Follow - up imaging and laboratory tests revealed no significant adverse events or unintended embolization of portal vein branches. No major complications were observed, even in patients with preexisting ascites.

CONCLUSIONS: The combination of gel foam, N - butyl cyanoacrylate, and lipiodol for embolizing the parenchymal tract after portal vein interventions is a highly effective technique with a low risk of bleeding and minimal risk of complications, making it a valuable option for repeated portal vein treatment in liver transplant patients.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Portal vein stenosis or occlusion following liver transplant can greatly affect patient outcomes, potentially leading to graft loss. Percutaneous treatments, including balloon angioplasty and stenting, require a transhepatic or transsplenic route. This study investigated the efficacy of embolizing the parenchymal tract with a combination of gel foam and an N - butyl cyanoacrylate - lipiodol mixture in transplant recipients following portal vein interventions.

title: [Predictive value and threshold effect analysis of the novel systemic immune-inflammatory complex index for functional outcomes at 90 days after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between the baseline systemic immune-inflammatory complex index (SIICI) and the 90-day functional prognosis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing reperfusion therapy, as well as the threshold effect.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled. Patients were divided into good prognosis group [modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 0-2] and a poor prognosis group (mRS score was 3-6) according to the 90-day score after onset. The clinical data and blood routine indicators within 24 hours after onset were collected, and SIICI and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. Univariate Logistic regression analysis was performed to screen 90-day functional prognosis-related influencing factors in patients with AIS after reperfusion therapy. Multivariate Logistic regression with multi-gradient adjustment was used to determine whether SIICI was an independent risk factor for poor functional prognosis or not. The restricted cubic spline (RCS) model was applied to analyze the dose-response relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor functional prognosis, and piecewise linear regression model was used for threshold effect analysis. Subjects were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a ratio of 7 : 3 for constructing a prognostic prediction model based on SIICI and internal validation. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve and decision curve analysis (DCA) were plotted to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit of the model.

RESULTS: All 1 919 AIS patients were enrolled in the final analysis, including 1 176 cases (61.28%) in the good prognosis group and 743 cases (38.72%) in the poor prognosis group. Univariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age, history of atrial fibrillation, bridging therapy, endovascular thrombectomy, elevated baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, prolonged total length of hospital stay, increased white blood cell count, elevated neutrophil count, elevated monocyte count, increased SII and elevated SIICI were risk factors for poor 90-day functional prognosis of AIS patients, and the history of hyperlipidemia and elevated lymphocyte count were protective factors (all P<0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that after adjusting for gender, age, past medical history, Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification and baseline NIHSS score, SIICI remained an independent risk factor for poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients [odds ratio (OR)=1.008, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.001-1.014, P=0.022], whereas SII showed no statistical significance after adjustment (OR=1.010, 95%CI was 0.999-1.020, P=0.067), suggesting that SIICI possessed better stability of independent association than the traditional inflammatory index SII. The RCS model verified a significant non-linear relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients (P<0.001). The optimal inflection point value of SIICI determined by piecewise linear regression was 15.03. When SIICI<15.03, each one-unit increase in SIICI was associated with an 11% increased risk of poor functional prognosis (OR=1.112, 95%CI was 1.078-1.147, P<0.001). When SIICI≥15.03, no statistically significant correlation was observed between SIICI and poor functional prognosis (OR=1.005, 95%CI was 0.998-1.012, P=0.136). For the SIICI-based prognosis prediction model, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.656 (95%CI was 0.626-0.686) in the training set and 0.639 (95%CI was 0.593-0.686) in the validation set, indicating favorable prognostic discrimination ability. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test yielded P=0.064, suggesting good model calibration. DCA revealed that the model obtained significant clinical net benefit within the high-risk threshold range of 0-0.8.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SIICI is independently correlated with the 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients after reperfusion therapy and shows a significant threshold effect. It exhibits superior predictive performance compared with the traditional inflammatory index SII. The prognostic prediction model constructed based on SIICI can assist clinicians in stratifying the risk of early functional prognosis in patients with AIS undergoing reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled.

title: Longitudinal monitoring of adalimumab levels and anti-adalimumab antibodies in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the association between longitudinal adalimumab concentrations, anti-adalimumab antibodies (AAA) levels, and clinical response in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS).

METHODS: A prospective multi-center, observational cohort study of AS patients receiving adalimumab therapy was conducted. Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization. Adalimumab concentrations were measured using a validated sandwich immunoassay. Measurement of AAA levels was performed with a laboratory-developed immunoassay system integrating electrochemiluminescence technology with specific immunomagnetic separation, with result reported as signal-to-noise ratio (S/N).

RESULTS: A total of 140 patients receiving adalimumab monotherapy were included. The median follow-up period was 169 days, and 711 plasma samples were available for adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels measurements. Seven patients had pre-existing AAA, and 120 (90.2%) of the remaining 133 patients tested positive for AAA during follow-up. A total of 48 patients were excluded from the exposure-response relationship dataset owing to pre-existing AAA (n=7), lack of active disease (n=26), incomplete follow-up (n=8), and prolonged dosing intervals (n=7). Among the remaining 92 patients, a total of 58 (63%) achieved clinical response. Adalimumab concentrations were higher, and AAA levels were significantly lower, in responders compared with non-responders at multiple time points. Exposure-response relationship models also revealed a steady-state adalimumab concentration target of 5.1 μg/mL and a week-4 concentration target of 3.3 μg/mL, corresponding to an 80% probability of clinical response. Thirty-six of 92 patients (39.1%) exhibited AAA-S/N values exceeding the putative clinically meaningful threshold (AAA-S/N=10). Patients in the high-AAA group (AAA-S/N≥10) had lower drug levels (median: 1.5 μg/mL vs. 6.9 μg/mL, P<0.0001) and poorer response rates (38.8% vs. 78.6%, P = 0.0002), relative to those in the low-AAA group (AAA-S/N<10). Furthermore, patients who were week-4 AAA-positive exhibited a 1.8-fold increased risk of non-response (relative risk, 95% confidence interval, 1.1-2.8).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that longitudinal profiles of adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels show a strong association with clinical responses in this Chinese AS cohort, which may inform therapeutic drug monitoring-guided adalimumab treatment strategies that remain to be further validated.

Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization.

title: Temporal Net Water Uptake Evolution and Its Association with Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes. In this study, we aimed to determine how associations between NWU and functional outcome vary across imaging times up to 1 week after stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included patients from the Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial of Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Netherlands (MRCLEAN-NO IV) trial with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who were treated with endovascular treatment and had baseline, 24-hour, and 1-week follow-up noncontrast CT scans. Functional outcome at 90 days was evaluated using the mRS, analyzed both as functional independence (mRS 0-2) and across the full ordinal distribution (mRS 0-6). In the primary analysis, associations between NWU measured at different imaging time points and functional independence were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models. To evaluate temporal changes in NWU, ΔNWU was calculated at different time intervals (baseline to 24 hours, 24 hours to 1 week, and baseline to 1 week), and its association with outcomes was analyzed using analogous regression models.

RESULTS: Of 539 MRCLEAN-NO IV patients, 115 were included in this study. The median time from stroke onset to randomization was 92 (IQR, 70-140) minutes. The median NWU evolved from 4.3% (interquartile range [IQR], 2.1%-6.8%) at baseline to 9.0% (IQR, 3.0%-13%) at 24 hours and 15% (IQR, 11%-19%) at 1 week. The median patient-level change (ΔNWU) from baseline to 1 week was 10% (IQR, 5.3%-16%). NWU measured at 1 week, but not at baseline or 24 hours, was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an adjusted OR (aOR) of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.90) per 5-percentage-point increase in NWU. Furthermore, a higher increase in NWU from baseline to 1-week imaging was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an aOR of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.86) per 5-percentage-point increase in ΔNWU1wk-BL.

CONCLUSIONS: In our population, NWU measured at 1 week is associated with 90-day clinical outcomes, suggesting that lesion evolution continues in the first week after stroke onset and may therefore represent a target for secondary treatments to improve clinical outcomes.

The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) in Medicare Advantage and Medicare Fee-for-Service: Differences in Patient Characteristics, Utilization, and Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over half of Medicare beneficiaries are enrolled in privately administered Medicare Advantage (MA) plans, and aortic stenosis predominantly affects older patients. In this study, we evaluated whether differences in care delivery between MA and fee-for-service (FFS) Medicare contribute to cardiovascular outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).

METHODS: Medicare patients who underwent TAVR from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2022, were eligible for cohort inclusion. TAVR utilization rates in MA and FFS were calculated as the age- and sex-standardized number of procedures per 10 000 person-years. Patient characteristics were compared between MA and FFS using standardized mean differences (SMDs), with an SMD ≥10% considered meaningful. The association of MA versus FFS enrollment with 30-day and 1-year outcomes was assessed using logistic and Cox regression models, respectively.

RESULTS: Among the 317 630 patients (64.4% FFS, 35.6% MA) undergoing TAVR, the mean age was 80.6±7.0 years, and 55.1% were men. TAVR utilization rates were similar between MA and FFS, with 11.2 TAVRs/10 000 person-years in FFS compared with 11.7 TAVRs/10 000 person-years in MA by the end of the study. Compared with FFS patients, MA patients were more likely to be Black (5.4% versus 3.0%; SMD, -11.9) and dual-enrolled in Medicaid (13.7% versus 8.6%; SMD, -16.3). Comorbidity profiles were similar (SMD, <10%). In the comorbidity-adjusted model, MA patients had lower odds of 30-day death (adjusted odds ratio, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.86-0.95]). At 1 year, MA patients had a lower adjusted risk of death (hazard ratio, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.92-0.96]), all-cause readmission (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.85-0.88]), stroke (hazard ratio, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.87-0.94]), and aortic valve reintervention (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.76-0.96]).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite similar clinical profiles and TAVR utilization, MA patients appeared to experience better 30-day and 1-year outcomes than FFS patients. Differences in care delivery may contribute, but future studies are needed to understand differences in outcomes.

In this study, we evaluated whether differences in care delivery between MA and fee-for-service (FFS) Medicare contribute to cardiovascular outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). METHODS: Medicare patients who underwent TAVR from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2022, were eligible for cohort inclusion.

title: Changes in Stroke Care Regionalization in California Associated With Evolving Evidence of Benefit for Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Network Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2015 demonstration of the benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) led to increases in interhospital transfer of patients with large vessel occlusion stroke. We sought to characterize the associated evolution in stroke care regionalization.

METHODS: We used comprehensive California statewide all-payer administrative data from 2010 to 2021 to identify ischemic stroke encounters and transfers (using recorded disposition and adjacent claims). We applied network analysis methods to create the interhospital transfer network, examine access to EVT-capable hospitals (time-varying, based on performance of ≥2 EVT cases that year), and used block models to identify clusters of hospitals closely connected through transfer by year and pre- versus post-2015. We used regression modeling with a linear spline and knot at 2015 to examine changes in network characteristics over time.

RESULTS: We identified 19 244 transfers between 338 hospitals. Pre-2015, 7 of 11 clusters had ≥1 EVT-capable hospital. Post-2015, 24 of 26 clusters had ≥1 EVT-capable hospital. More hospitals had EVT capability over time (21.6% [70/324] to 33.7% [106/315]). EVT-capable hospitals consistently received more transferred patients relative to noncapable hospitals (mean number of received transfers/y pre-2015: 55.2 versus 15.6; post-2015: 97.3 versus 13.8). Initially, transfers for EVT increased from 10.7% of EVT cases having an interhospital transfer in 2010 to 36.0% by 2016. After 2016, the trend reversed, decreasing to 21.7% by 2021.

CONCLUSIONS: The California stroke system of care became less regionalized for EVT access from 2010 to 2021. Although we expected increased consolidation with fewer clusters centered around EVT-capable hospitals, we instead observed an increased number of EVT-capable hospitals with more clusters around them and less need for transfer to access EVT. More work is needed to examine the relative trade-offs of regionalization patterns in stroke systems of care, given recognized benefits of more regionalized care around higher-volume centers in other conditions.

We sought to characterize the associated evolution in stroke care regionalization. title: Ascites and Hyponatremia.
abstract: Ascites and hyponatremia in cirrhosis both arise from portal hypertension-induced splanchnic vasodilation, leading to reduced effective arterial blood volume and neurohormonal activation. Ascites represents the most common decompensating event in cirrhosis and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality, while hyponatremia independently predicts poor prognosis and transplant outcomes. This article outlines evidence-based diagnostic strategies and stepwise management, including dietary modification, diuretics, paracentesis, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt and transplant referral, as well as emerging therapies. These two conditions are interrelated, and multidisciplinary care is needed.

title: Active (Systolic) Reflux Demonstrated in a Below-Knee Isolated Incompetent Perforating Vein Associated With a Symptomatic Varicose Vein Using Infrared Thermography, Illustrated by a Case Report.
abstract: BackgroundThe role of incompetent perforating veins (IPVs) in varicose veins is controversial. There are different views on the mechanism of "incompetence" and, hence, the importance of IPVs. Those following CHIVA and "haemodynamic surgery" principles suggest higher velocities in the deep veins cause blood to flow inwards due to the Venturi effect. The senior author of this case has previously proposed that increased pressure by muscle activity forces blood out of any IPV, a phenomenon called "active" reflux. This case report appears to show active reflux in an isolated IPV using infrared thermography.MethodsA 34-year-old lady presented with a tender lower leg varicose vein due to an isolated IPV. She was placed supine and still for 10 minutes, then performed 10 plantar- and dorsi-flexions. Next, she stood up and stood still for 10 minutes. Her leg was monitored throughout using an infra-red camera (IFC).ResultsImmediately on lying, the IFC showed the vein, indicating blood flowing out of the IPV from the warm deep compartment into the colder superficial compartment (passive/diastolic or gravitational reflux). Over 10 minutes, the signal reduced significantly, suggesting no more blood was being pumped out through the IPV. During 10 plantar- and dorsi-flexions, the signal returned strongly, indicating blood being pumped out of the IPV once again. On standing, the signal was strong initially, but after 10 min of standing still, the signal had faded, indicating a lack of passive (gravitational) reflux in the IPV.ConclusionThis case suggests that reflux through this IPV is due to muscle activity and not by passive reflux due to gravity. This could explain why IPVs can cause fasciocutaneous damage and/or varicose veins in the lower limb. If correct, failure to identify and treat IPVs during varicose vein surgery would mean that the procedure would be inadequate.
